beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.anriss.text: For KU64, 2025 is a special year: the practice is celebrating its 20th anniversary – from a local neighbourhood practice to the largest single dental practice in Europe. We're taking a look back with patients, staff, partners and specialists

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.0.text.text: 2025 is a special year for KU64: the practice celebrates its 20th birthday – from a local neighbourhood practice to the largest single dental practice in Europe. We're taking patients, staff, partners, fellow professionals and friends on a journey through the practice's history and its milestones. Find out which course has been set for the coming years, why children cry when leaving KU64, and why our practice is also an art gallery.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.1.text.text: The key facts at a glance | Rethinking dentistry with KU64 | A building that brings a smile to your face | The practice of short distances | Pioneers from day one: quiet innovation, early impact | Twenty years of closeness: here, every person counts | The people behind KU64 | Art meets practice: an impact reaching far beyond Berlin | At KU64, thank you means: setting a course together | From anniversary to the future: progress with a plan

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.10.text.text: With this anniversary, KU64 celebrates a promise: "Twenty years ago, we set out to rethink dentistry: evidence-based, digital, and as patient-friendly as possible," recalls founder and owner Dr Stephan Ziegler. His vision at the time was to turn palpable fear into trust, seven days a week. Today – now across three locations – reception still says: "It doesn't smell like a dentist here, but like fireplace wood, lemon and mint tea, or freshly brewed coffee." And how do you celebrate 20 years without confetti in the waiting room? With a Mediterranean cruise for all staff.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.11.text.text: A building that brings a smile to your face

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.12.text.text: Since 9 July 2005, KU64 has given the listed ECO building – home to the former "Hollywood" cinema at Kurfürstendamm 64 – a completely new feel: a sunny, sandy dune landscape designed by the architectural trio GRAFT, deliberately created to look nothing like a dental practice. Everything invites a little moment of respite: warm light, soft lines, clear pathways. It's no wonder some guests smile and ask if they've stumbled into a spa. And since GRAFT also designed a house for Brad Pitt, the charming rumour persists that he visits himself. He doesn't, but other familiar faces do. On its 20th anniversary, this healing architecture still embodies exactly what it always set out to do: slow things down, offer calm, build trust – the foundation on which two decades of KU64 have grown.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.14.text.text: Yet this atmosphere would be nothing more than appearance without the medical substance behind it. No one wants to travel across the city clutching a referral for orthodontics. That's why KU64 brought all dental specialisms together under one roof early on, from orthodontics to its own surgical unit and dental laboratory.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.15.text.text: Even after expanding in 2005 from 250 to almost 2,000 square metres, one thing stayed the same: short distances, decisive diagnostics, digital processes. In 2013, KU64 expanded its practice further with its own surgical unit. This collaboration brings very concrete benefits to everyday care. High-quality full-mouth restorations become a team effort. Dentures can often be made on the very same day, while the patient enjoys a cappuccino in the waiting lounge or takes a stroll along the Ku'damm. And many decisions are made not within weeks, but on the same day. In 2019, KU64 continued this expansion by opening an additional practice in Potsdam. In 2023, the next expansion followed with the opening of the practice in Berlin-Mitte.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.16.text.text: Pioneers from day one: quiet innovation, early impact

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.17.text.text: At KU64, innovation takes hold early and visibly. "Excellence doesn't happen by chance," explains Dr Ziegler. "It's the result of adhering to guidelines, ongoing training, and a willingness to integrate technologies sensibly, early on." Twenty years ago, specially trained prophylaxis assistants at KU64 were already independently carrying out professional teeth cleaning, at a time when elsewhere this was still improvised "between two rooms". Guided Biofilm Therapy with AirFlow was introduced as one of the first in Germany. The rubber dam became standard when removing old fillings, and amalgam was consistently phased out. Digital impressions replaced impression material, making treatments more precise and comfortable. In 2014, KU64 became the first practice in Berlin to bring the Coachman concept of Digital Smile Design into everyday use – a digital method that shows the future smile realistically before treatment and allows for precise planning. Since then, KU64 has focused on smile makeovers: high-quality, interdisciplinary-planned, comprehensive aesthetic restorations.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.18.text.text: Twenty years of closeness: here, every person counts

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.19.text.text: Success stories have many chapters, and KU64's has more than 160,000. That's how many patients found help here over twenty years, 130,000 of them at Ku'damm alone. Over 70 per cent of them now recommend KU64 to others. Four out of five patients come from Berlin and Brandenburg, and yet the response reaches far beyond: people travel to KU64 for treatment from all over Europe, the Arab world and Russia.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.2.text.text: The key facts at a glance

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.20.text.text: The age range is wide too: from the first milk tooth to the age of 98. Just how much life history comes together in one practice is shown by a 50-year-old denture handed in at our Lost & Found office – living proof of just how long dental solutions can last.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.22.text.text: Innovation, trust and excellent patient care show themselves above all in the people who live them out every day. There's a point of contact for every concern. Over 20 years, the KU64 team at Ku'damm has grown to 200 colleagues, including 32 dentists. A further team of 25 supports KU64 in each of Berlin-Mitte and Potsdam. Together, the team speaks around 30 languages, from German to Mongolian.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.23.text.text: KU64 set a special milestone in 2010: with the opening of the children's department and orthodontics, care for young patients found a permanent, lovingly designed home. Nine paediatric dentists work here with great patience and their own approach to help anxious children feel safe. Since then, specialised treatment of chalky teeth (MIH) in children has also become a fixed part of the service. Alongside the fireplace lounge, another waiting area has since brought relaxation and joy: a genuine play paradise with an Xbox, children's cinema, PlayStation, formicarium, aquarium, and a life-size XXL dinosaur. Here, tears are shed less often in the treatment chair than when leaving the play area.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.24.text.text: Art meets practice: an impact reaching far beyond Berlin

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.25.text.text: Anyone waiting at KU64 is treated to culture. Three to four exhibitions a year, more than sixty over two decades, have turned the practice into a gallery. In the endodontics room hangs a three-by-three-metre work by Rayk Goetze. Teams from all over the world book guided tours, including from industries far removed from medicine.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.26.text.text: Responsibility is also part of the KU64 profile: for years, the practice has run its own charity projects, for example in South Africa, providing practical help where it's needed. By now, more than 2,000 media reports have carried this Berlin story far beyond the city: from CNN and CBS to The New Yorker, FAZ, ARD and ZDF.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.27.text.text: Art on the walls, precision in the hands, and in between, small everyday constants: since 2005, every goodie bag for our patients has included credit-card-sized dental floss – unassuming, practical, popular.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.28.text.text: At KU64, saying thank you means: setting a course together

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.29.text.text: For the anniversary, there was deliberately no party and no open day – instead, genuine appreciation: in June 2025, Dr. Ziegler invited the entire team on an exclusive Mediterranean cruise with workshops, keynotes, team-building and a joint outlook for the next 20 years. There was gratitude, celebration, laughter and shared discovery. His line of the evening still stands: „You are my greatest pride!“ – an emotional declaration of love to the KU64 crew. Without the best staff in the industry, KU64 would not be possible.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.3.text.text: Healing architecture as a guiding principle

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.30.text.text: From anniversary to the future: progress with a plan

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.31.text.text: For the 20th anniversary, the course remains clear: digitalisation, digitalisation, digitalisation. In 2016, the IT upgrade marked the first major digital leap. The next stage now builds on that. Over the coming five years, KU64 is focusing on minimally invasive procedures, AI-supported planning and services, and close research partnerships. Sustainability is to become measurable: low-paper workflows and digital, low-radiation X-ray processes will continue to be expanded. Training brings these advances into everyday practice: KU64 trains extensively and currently has the most dental trainees in Berlin and Brandenburg. Continuing education is equally important. The team keeps developing continuously, even beyond the annual requirements of the dental association. Or, as Dr. Ziegler puts it: „We train, we keep developing, and we stick together. That's the only way top-level medicine stays practical for everyday life.“

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.4.text.text: KU64 opened on 9 July 2005 at Ku'damm 64 – deliberately designed to feel free of fear, with the sunny, sandy dune architecture created by GRAFT. Clear pathways, warm light and calming materials create a sense of ease before treatment even begins.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.5.text.text: A strong community across three locations

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.6.text.text: Today, 200 staff members work at Ku'damm. A further 50 staff support KU64 at the Potsdam location (since 2019) and in Berlin-Mitte (since 2023). Altogether, more than 160,000 treatments have already been carried out.

beitrag.20-jahre-ku64.bloecke.8.text.text: KU64 marked its 20th anniversary with all staff on a Mediterranean cruise, featuring workshops on realignment: more digitalisation, AI-supported planning and services, minimally invasive procedures, and measurable sustainability.

beitrag.360zahn-aus-duesseldorf.bloecke..text: Regular, valuable dental insights between Düsseldorf and Berlin
MVZ for dentistry, paediatric dentistry and orthodontics

Anyone who thinks all dental practices are alike hasn't yet come across 360°zahn in Düsseldorf. Our most recent meeting as part of the CLUB OF EXCELLENCE showed us once again why this practice is so special.

Imagine walking into a practice where state-of-the-art technology meets genuine warmth. That's exactly what awaits you at 360°zahn. The four-person leadership team here has created something that goes far beyond the usual concept of a dental practice.

What impressed us most? The way 360°zahn is revolutionising patient education. Picture a virtual library brimming with knowledge: an extensive dental encyclopaedia, engaging blog posts and – brace yourselves – over 700 instructional videos! This isn't just information, it's pure empowerment for patients.

But it's not only the digital side that shines. The practice concept itself works like a finely tuned machine. From general dentistry and orthodontics to their own in-house lab – every part fits perfectly with the next. It's as if all the experts you could ever need had been gathered under one roof.

What connects us so strongly with the team at 360°zahn is a shared passion for innovative dentistry. Dr Ehsan Andabili, Efthimios Giannakoudis, Nektarios Papagrigoriou and Dr Elham Andabili-Barthel all share our vision of continuously advancing dental medicine. In our conversations, it becomes clear that we all strive to keep redefining the boundaries of what's possible in our field and to offer our patients the best possible care. This shared focus on progress and excellence in dentistry forms the basis of our valuable professional exchange and mutual inspiration.
360°zahn is more than a practice; it's a glimpse into the future of dentistry. If you're looking for excellent dental care in Düsseldorf, we can only say: you know where to go!
Dear colleagues on the Rhine, keep up the great work. You inspire not only your patients but also us fellow professionals in the field. We're already looking forward to our next exchange!

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.10.te.text: KU64 and GRAFT – the new world of beauty

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.102.t.text: Yesterday, a huge area for paediatric dentistry called KU64-Youngstars opened at KU64. A large crowd of children stormed the unique world of experience.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.103.t.text: Some of the highlights – such as the climbing wall, the slide and the ball pit, a first for a children’s dental practice in Berlin – were immediately taken over.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.104.t.text: A practice safari led children and parents through the new treatment rooms and the cosy play corners.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.105.t.text: The newly created cavity cave caused great amazement, and while the television magician Ully Loup revealed all kinds of magic tricks, a mascot in the shape of an oversized tooth pirate wandered through the rooms, offering to pose for photos with visitors.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.12.te.text: Our lounge is causing a stir

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.14.te.text: The waiting lounge at KU64 gained great fame in September!

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.15.te.text: Pictures of the practice featured on both the official magazine of the largest textile trade fair in Frankfurt, “Textil Fashion Spezial”, and on the cover of the property supplement of the Berliner Zeitung.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.18.te.text: “Office fashion can be this trendy. This season, classic suits, clean cuts and elegant ensembles are mixed with extravagant blouses, refined accessories and bold colours. The perfect blend of wearable and modern.”

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.19.te.text: Photographer Jochen Arndt shows autumnal business fashion for today's modern woman. The fashion shoot was carried out entirely on the premises of the KU64 dental practice on Kurfürstendamm in Berlin.

With a helping hand from Hollywood, the founding trio has also made a name for itself in Germany – breaking with a fair few conventions and clichés along the way.”

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.28.te.text: “The lads have long been in the spotlight, even without Brad Pitt. Their signature style is flowing spaces with soft curves and gentle, sweeping lines. Interiors that feel like dream scenarios – as seen at the KU 64 dental practice and the Hotel Q in Berlin, both of which reflect a spatial concept that breaks with common conventions.”

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.55.te.text: (…) The KU64 dental clinic in Berlin, 2005, is located on the boulevard, and it employs a similar strategy, allaying the anxieties of patients and evoking the sand dunes of a summer resort.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.59.te.text: The KU64 dental practice in Berlin is the first dental spa in Germany. Its founder is Dr Stephan Ziegler, who, in his practice (around 1,000 square metres) designed by the renowned architectural firm GRAFT, houses a dental wellness centre of the highest calibre, where the motto “Nothing hurts here!” applies.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.6.tex.text: BREAKING NEWS – KU64 architects GRAFT win the European Prize for Architecture for 2011 – the design and realisation of the “extraordinary dental practice on the Kudamm” receives special mention:

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.60.te.text:
To help patients relax and take their mind off things before a dental examination, Dr Ziegler's team also offers, among other things, to play the patient's preferred music (via mp3) from the available programmes or brought from home.
The music can be listened to both during the waiting time and during the dental treatment itself. As an alternative to music, patients can also watch a DVD using special glasses.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.62.te.text: KU64 dental practice in Berlin is the first Dental Spa in Germany. Its founder is Dr Stephan Ziegler, whose practice (of around 1000 sqm), designed by the renowned architects GRAFT, houses a first-class dental wellness centre, where the motto is “Here, nothing hurts!”.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.63.te.text: To distract and relax the patient before the dental examination, Dr Ziegler's team offers, among other services, the option of listening to music chosen by the patient (via mp3), selected from the available programmes or brought from home.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.64.te.text: The music can be listened to both during the waiting time and during the dental treatment. As an alternative to music, there is also the option of watching a DVD with special glasses.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.68.te.text: The Bund Deutscher Architekten has chosen “KU64 – Die Zahnspezialisten” as a positive example of a successful combination of architecture and health for their annual brochure!

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.70.te.text: A regular visit to the dentist doesn't have to start in a grey waiting room. At this practice (KU64), doctor and architect have shown how things can be done differently.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.71.te.text: Simply entering the spacious practice, which was designed entirely by an architectural firm, gives patients a greater sense of trust than other visits to the doctor.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.72.te.text: Reception is already the first step into this other world: here, the patient is welcomed as a guest. The unusual yet comfortable furnishings make the waiting room feel like a place of rest, whose atmosphere takes away much of the unease of a dental treatment.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.73.te.text: Despite the necessary high-tech equipment, these rooms still leave space for conversation between doctor and patient. (…) With so much dedication to the patient, one can be confident of first-class treatment here.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.74.te.text:
Source: “Spaces for Life”,
               brochure of the BDA (Bund Deutscher Architekten)
As at: 30.06.2008

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.77.te.text: “They are the architects of great relaxation. They build holidays, the loveliest dune houses in the Caribbean, undulating hotels on America's coastlines. And now they want to bring their massage-soft forms to bear on the centre of Germany, long tense with ideology, to help it achieve a looseness never known before. Of all places, it is to be Berliner Schlossplatz, a site of bitter debate over reconstructed baroque façades, absurd palace demolitions, and the republic's overall approach to the politics of history. What does the architecture group called Graft make of this historical weight? They let it float. (…)

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.78.te.text: They love connecting, bonding, blending — even a dental practice in Berlin they turn into a place of pure harmony. Nothing feels clinical, nothing smells of the dentist. Sun-yellow walls curve like dunes, and the waiting room becomes a cosy nook with wine-red loungers and a fireplace. Architecture as pain therapy: fear is meant to turn into relaxation. (…)”

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.79.te.text: Read the full article online here

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.81.te.text: KU64 - The coolest dental clinic in the world

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.83.te.text: Who would have thought a dental clinic could be this cool? The 10,180-square-metre clinic (named KU64 after its address on Kurfürstendamm) is located in Berlin and was designed by the acclaimed firm GRAFT, which is also behind Berlin's new super-lifestyle hotel Q.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.84.te.text: The incredible design makes you feel as if you're in a first-class Hollywood bar — certainly not the usual atmosphere one associates with utilitarian spaces like this, which houses eight dentists. The arch-like rooms are flooded with light and convey an elegant sense of movement and space. Here, even a root canal treatment feels inviting.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.86.te.text: Who would have thought a dental clinic could be this cool? The 10,180-square-foot clinic (called KU64 after its Kurfürstendamm address) is located in Berlin and was designed by the hot firm, GRAFT, the same people that were behind Berlin’s new super lifestyle Hotel Q.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.87.te.text: The incredible design makes you feel like you’re in an A-list Hollywood members bar – certainly not the usual ambiance associated with utilitarian spaces like this one which houses eight dentists. The cocoon like spaces are filled with light, creating an elegant sense of flow and space. It makes even a session of root canal seem inviting.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.9.tex.text: “For the Dental Clinic KU64 (2009) in Berlin, GRAFT forwards a radical new understanding of hospitals in general and specifically dental clinics – away from negative prejudices of hygienic, sterile, and all white toward a new design atmosphere of art, well-being and relaxation.”

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.91.te.text: Architects in the capital are inventive and keen to experiment.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.92.te.text:

The architects at Graft take a less classically refined approach – two years ago, their flowing spatial structures for “Hotel Q” on Knesebeckstraße already caused a sensation. Last year, Graft, who gained some fame as the architects behind Brad Pitt’s studio house, reinvented the concept of the dental practice.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.93.te.text:
On Kurfürstendamm, they designed a cheerful yellow spatial landscape intended to “lead away” “from the feeling of physical and mental exception”. The loungers in the waiting room and the doors of the treatment rooms are cut out of a flowing continuum of floor, wall and ceiling.
(…)

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.97.te.text: Dr Stephan Ziegler works among yellow dunes

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.98.te.text: BERLIN – After more than 10 years of successful practice, the team around Berlin colleague Dr Stephan Ziegler embarked on a project that reinvented the dental practice once again. The old practice in Berlin-Wilmersdorf was closed, the team moved to Kurfürstendamm, and the “other practice” became the “practice of dental specialists” – KU64. Within the profession, this practice was also a step into new architectural dimensions: the architectural firm GRAFT, which had already worked for Hollywood stars such as Brad Pitt and created Berlin’s extraordinary Q! Hotel, designed the interior. The one requirement from the enterprising colleague: nothing should be reminiscent of a dental practice.

beitrag.architektur-design.bloecke.99.te.text: Source: Dental Tribune, German Edition, No. 4/2006 February

The KU64 team
KU64 training with social competence and responsibility

As a dental practice with social competence and responsibility, we naturally train our own new talent, above all dental nurses (ZFA, m/f/d). Our years of training experience and expertise benefit new talent in particular. So far, ALL ZFA trainees at KU64 have been successfully taken on permanently – a truly outstanding success rate!
We're also happy to further train dental nurses (m/f/d) to become dental administrative assistants or prophylaxis assistants.

We do a lot to make sure everyone at KU64 feels comfortable, especially our trainees, who are just starting out on their career path. Alongside first-class training, they work through every department of a highly modern dental practice before deciding on a particular area (general dentistry, oral surgery, orthodontics, and so on). In addition to the treating dentist, each trainee is also supported by an experienced, long-serving dental nurse who mentors them throughout their entire training. This way, you benefit from their know-how.

Male trainees in dentistry and their career prospects

We are especially proud to have trained and employed male trainees as dental assistants too – still a rarity today. With Jens Schönfeld, KU64 has made history. He was one of the first male dental assistants in the country to complete his training, going on to complete further training as a dental hygienist assistant. beitrag.flowable-injection-technique.blo.text: Small gaps between teeth, uneven front teeth or awkward tooth shapes are not a medical problem, but they can make your smile look less attractive. With the Flowable Injection Technique, we offer a minimally invasive treatment at our dental practice – often without any grinding of the teeth. We reshape the teeth aesthetically using flowable composite, giving your smile a fresh new look. In this article, you'll find out who the method is suitable for, how it works, and when ceramic veneers may be the better choice.
In brief

Small gaps between teeth can strongly shape a smile – especially when they are in the visible front tooth area. With the Flowable Injection Technique, such gaps can often be visually harmonised by widening the neighbouring teeth or adjusting their shape using tooth-coloured composite. This can be of interest, for example, with fine gaps between the incisors or small dark spots between a tooth and the gum. It is important that the position of the teeth, their size and the appearance of the gums all match.
If you would like a more harmonious tooth shape

Sometimes, when you smile, a tooth looks a little too short, an edge appears irregular, or the front teeth look uneven overall. Small chips, worn biting edges or asymmetrical tooth shapes can also make a smile look less even. The Flowable Injection Technique can specifically balance out such details. With its help, a deliberately designed tooth shape is created that suits your face, lip line and natural tooth colour.
If you are looking for a tissue-sparing alternative to veneers

Classic ceramic veneers are a high-quality solution for aesthetic changes, but depending on the starting situation, they often require the tooth surface to be prepared by grinding. The Flowable Injection Technique can be a tissue-sparing alternative for smaller corrections, provided the teeth are basically healthy and stable.
If you would like to try out the look of ceramic veneers

The Flowable Injection Technique is especially helpful if you're still unsure which shape, length or width of veneers would suit you. Together with your dentist, you can discuss whether the planned result looks natural and fits your face. In some cases, the Flowable Injection Technique can be the right solution on its own. In other cases, it serves as a way to get a sense of the result before a longer-term option such as ceramic veneers is planned.
How long do composite veneers last?

Composite is a tooth-coloured material that can be shaped and repaired easily. Compared with ceramic, however, the material is softer and more prone to staining or wear. Coffee, tea, red wine, nicotine or strongly pigmented foods can change the surface over time. Grinding or heavy clenching can also shorten its lifespan.

With good care, composite veneers can last several years. To keep them looking their best for as long as possible, we recommend regular professional teeth cleaning, good daily oral hygiene and routine check-ups with your dentist. Small rough patches, discolouration or edges can often be polished or touched up. This is an advantage over some other cosmetic treatments: composite can often be repaired directly, without having to replace the whole restoration.

The Flowable Injection Technique is a gentle and efficient treatment option in modern dentistry if you would like small aesthetic corrections to your smile. However, the method does not automatically replace ceramic veneers, orthodontic or restorative treatments. Our specialists in dental aesthetics will be happy to advise you.
When is Flowable Injection not recommended?

The Flowable Injection Technique can make small cosmetic corrections very gently. However, it isn't the best choice for every starting situation. What matters is whether your teeth, gums, bite and cosmetic goal all fit together. Sometimes it makes more sense to first stabilise the dental foundation or to choose a different treatment, for example ceramic veneers, orthodontic correction, whitening or a restorative solution with dentures.
In cases of major misalignment

If your teeth are noticeably rotated, tilted or shifted, composite won't correct the underlying cause. The Flowable Injection Technique can balance out the appearance, but it can't replace actual tooth movement. In such cases, orthodontic treatment is often the right approach.
In cases of severe grinding or clenching

Sometimes, when you smile, a tooth looks slightly too short, an edge looks uneven, or the front teeth appear irregular overall. Small chips, worn edges or asymmetrical tooth shapes can also make your smile look less even. The Flowable Injection Technique can correct these details in a targeted way. It creates a deliberately shaped tooth form that suits your face, lip line and natural tooth colour.
In cases of decay, old leaking fillings or unstable tooth structure

Flowable Injection is a cosmetic method. It doesn't replace necessary dental treatment. If decay, leaking fillings, cracks or heavily damaged tooth structure are present, these issues must be treated first. Only on a healthy, stable foundation can your veneers hold up reliably.
In cases of gum inflammation or periodontitis

Healthy gums are essential for a beautiful, lasting result. Inflammation, bleeding gums, gum recession or untreated periodontitis can affect both the appearance and the long-term stability of your veneers. In this case, the priority is first to treat your gums with the help of our KU64 periodontology specialists.
Your beautiful new smile with the Flowable Injection Technique
In cases of very dark discolouration

The Flowable Injection Technique mainly changes the shape and covers small defects in your teeth. Strong internal discolouration, very dark tooth shades or blotchy patterns can't always be reliably concealed with it. Depending on the goal, whitening beforehand may be needed, or a ceramic solution should be chosen instead.
In cases of unrealistic expectations

The Flowable Injection Technique can visibly improve small details, but it can't completely transform every smile. As a quick, cost-effective solution, it has its limits. That's why we give you honest advice: you should know in advance what result is realistic, how long it's likely to last, and what care will be needed afterwards.
How treatment with the Flowable Injection Technique works at KU64

We create your new veneers using the Flowable Injection Technique following a clear process. The goal is a harmonious smile that suits your natural tooth shape, tooth colour, lip line and face. Alongside aesthetics, we also pay attention to function, bite and easy oral hygiene.
1. Consultation and cosmetic analysis

It all starts with a personal consultation. We discuss what bothers you about your smile and what result you're hoping for. We then examine your teeth, gums and bite. Small gaps, uneven edges or asymmetrical tooth shapes in the front teeth can only be corrected beautifully in the long run if the dental foundation is stable. At this stage, we also clarify whether the Flowable Injection Technique is the right choice for your situation.
2. Planning

If the method is suitable for you, we plan the desired tooth shape. Depending on your situation, we use either a digital scan with a digital preview or a classic impression for a wax-up: a planned preview of your new tooth shape made from wax.

A small detail can sometimes change the whole impression: a fine gap between the front teeth, an uneven tooth edge, a tooth that looks slightly too short, or old small fillings that catch the eye when you smile. You might notice this especially in photos, on video calls or in the mirror in the morning. Medically, nothing dramatic has usually happened, but your smile simply doesn't look as harmonious as you would like, and you don't want to accept that.

A mock-up makes the possible result even more tangible. Our clinicians make the planned shape visible with a physical model directly in your mouth, so you can better judge how your smile might look afterwards. This step is especially important to make sure the length, width, symmetry and overall impression suit you and don't look artificial.
3. Preparation

Before the actual treatment, your tooth surfaces should be clean and well prepared. Plaque, discolouration and soft deposits can affect adhesion and the aesthetic result. For this reason, a professional teeth cleaning is usually required beforehand.

We then prepare your teeth for the composite by gently polishing and cleaning them. Depending on the initial situation, this is done in a very substance-sparing way. In many cases, no conventional grinding of healthy tooth structure is needed.
4. Injecting the flowable composite

To create the veneers, we fit you with a transparent template made based on the detailed planning and data. It determines the final tooth shape. Through small openings, we use a device similar to a syringe to inject flowable, tooth-coloured composite into the template. The material is distributed precisely at the intended points and settles onto the tooth surface.

We then cure the composite with light. This is how the planned shape emerges step by step. Throughout, we ensure a precise template, a controlled amount of material and careful workmanship, so that the result looks natural.
5. Finishing and high-gloss polishing

Once the composite has cured, we remove the template. We then check the shape, transitions, bite contacts and aesthetics. Any small excess is carefully removed with a file, after which we smooth the edges and polish the surface. High-gloss polishing is more than just a cosmetic step: a smooth surface feels more pleasant, is easier to clean and is less prone to discolouration.
Finally, we discuss with you how to care for your composite veneers and which check-up or hygiene appointments make sense. This helps your new smile stay beautiful and stable for as long as possible.

The Flowable Injection Technique is a modern variant of veneers in aesthetic dentistry, allowing smaller shape corrections to visible teeth to be carried out in a particularly tissue-sparing way. To do this, the dentist makes a transparent template that can transfer your desired tooth shape precisely onto your teeth.
Flowable injection or ceramic veneers – which suits you better?

Whether flowable injection veneers or ceramic veneers suit you better depends on your aesthetic goal, your tooth structure, your bite, and your expectations regarding durability and colour stability. Both methods can make your smile look more harmonious, but they differ considerably in terms of material, effort, cost and long-term effect. The table below gives you some initial guidance.
Table: Composite veneers and ceramic veneers compared
What to keep in mind after treatment

After treatment with the flowable injection technique, you can usually get back to your daily routine quickly. However, keeping your composite veneers looking good, smooth and stable for as long as possible depends on proper care and regular check-ups. At KU64, we discuss with you in detail after treatment which care routine suits your teeth and when check-up or hygiene appointments make sense. This way, your new smile stays not only beautiful but also healthy. Any minor discolouration, rough spots or fine edges can be re-polished or corrected directly during check-up appointments.
Pay attention to thorough dental hygiene

Pay particular attention to thorough daily dental care with a toothbrush, dental floss or interdental brushes. Plaque should be removed as thoroughly as possible, especially at the transitions between the tooth and the composite. Regular professional teeth cleaning also helps keep the surfaces clean and well maintained.
Avoid strongly staining and hard foods

In the first few days after treatment, you should keep consumption of strongly staining foods and drinks to a minimum, for example coffee, tea, red wine, curry or dark berries. Smoking can also encourage discolouration. In addition, avoid biting into hard objects with your front teeth, such as nuts, hard bread crusts, ice cubes or packaging.
Wear a night guard

“With the Flowable Injection Technique, flowable composite – a tooth-coloured resin – is applied directly to the tooth surface through small openings in a template. This allows small gaps between teeth, uneven tooth shapes, worn edges or fine defects to be harmonised – quickly, cost-effectively and in many cases without the classic grinding down of healthy tooth structure.”
If you grind or clench your teeth, you should wear a protective splint at night. This relieves the composite build-ups and reduces the risk of chipping or wear.
Flowable injection at KU64 Berlin: aesthetics begins with good advice

Do you need further information, or do you have questions about the content of this blog article or about the service surrounding the new flowable injection technique? Simply get in touch with us or book an appointment directly.

beitrag.interview-dentosophie-clara-cons.text: Allow us to introduce: Clara-Constanze Meinberg, expert in holistic dentistry and Dentosophy at KU64 in Berlin-Charlottenburg. With her unique qualification as a dentist, alternative practitioner and hypnosis

Allow us to introduce: Clara-Constanze Meinberg, expert in holistic dentistry and Dentosophy at KU64 in Berlin-Charlottenburg. With her unique qualification as a dentist, alternative practitioner and hypnotherapist, she significantly broadens the perspective on health and treatment in her practice.
Breathing, tongue and bite in balance

We often see non-specific complaints such as chronic tension in the jaw, neck and shoulder area, recurring headaches, difficulty concentrating or exhaustion, which are rarely linked to the oral cavity. In the clinical examination, we also often find dry mucous membranes, increased tooth decay and gum recession caused by periodontitis, as well as disrupted swallowing and tongue resting position.
Children are often affected too. Are there typical signs that should make parents take notice early on and consider Dentosophie treatment?

Typical early signs in children include a permanently open mouth – especially during sleep –, snoring or restless sleep, as well as teeth grinding. Even small signs such as very tousled hair at the back of the head in the morning can indicate that the body moves a lot at night to compensate for breathing imbalances. This is often accompanied by increased susceptibility to infections and difficulty concentrating. From a professional point of view, it is crucial that these functional disorders are recognised early, as they have a strong effect on growth, muscle control and the long-term stability of the teeth and jaw.
What exactly is the Balancer, and what does it change in the mouth and jaw area?

The Balancer is a flexible training appliance developed for use as part of Dentosophie. The patient wears it between the upper and lower jaw and can use it to train muscles and nerves in the mouth and facial area in a targeted way. Through repeated impulses with corresponding exercises, daily wear and later nightly wear, the body learns to naturally control central functions such as breathing and bite again. This specifically improves the resting position of the tongue, the swallowing pattern and the coordination of the jaw muscles. As a result, harmful habits such as grinding or clenching gradually recede. At the same time, this has a positive effect on the natural movement and tension patterns throughout the body's overall regulation.
How does Dentosophie treatment typically proceed with you?

First, I carry out comprehensive initial diagnostics, during which I discuss not only functional findings but also the patient's individual goals and wishes, and we select the appropriate Balancer. At the start of treatment, patients should train with the Balancer for about five minutes a day, supplemented by a further relaxed wearing time of around one hour per day without active exercises. I guide them through this during our sessions, and we check the progress of the treatment together. Once everything has settled in well, the therapy is gradually extended to include wearing the Balancer at night. Alongside this, I meet with patients at intervals of six to eight weeks to monitor the course of treatment. Depending on need and circumstances, I also use additional targeted manual therapy and osteopathic treatments.
How long does the treatment take?
For adults, treatment is generally designed to last around six months; for children and young people, a longer course of treatment may be appropriate depending on the situation.
When do patients first notice that something is really changing?

The gentle, cause-oriented approach of Dentosophie brings breathing, tongue position and bite back into balance. This improves the functional causes of complex conditions such as teeth grinding, jaw tension, certain chronic pain conditions or snoring. Through targeted exercises and the Balancer training device, the system is rebalanced to reprogramme basic functions and enable the body to find better balance overall. Find out in our interview with Dentosophie therapist Clara-Constanze Meinberg how this holistic approach can be a real turning point for many patients and how it helps with numerous complaints such as malocclusions and muscle function disorders.

The first changes usually appear very early after the start of treatment, initially in the chewing system, but beyond that also in a stabilisation of overall posture and regulation. Patients often report that complaints such as pain and restricted movement resolve – complaints they had not previously connected with the mouth and jaw system at all.
Last updated on 01.04.2026
Further information and appointment booking

We currently offer Dentosophie at KU64 at our Charlottenburg and Potsdam locations. Anyone interested or affected can find all the information about Dentosophie, along with the option to book an appointment, on our services page.

PRESS/ COMMUNICATIONS/ MARKETING
Profile of Petros Prontis
Ms Meinberg, what does holistic dentistry mean to you in everyday practice?

Dental treatments often don't give enough consideration to the general influences on the body, while on the other hand general medicine frequently neglects the oral cavity – even though many imbalances show up early in the mouth and can be recognised there. I look at patients in terms of their entire physical and functional interconnection. This creates a differentiated overall picture, so that we don't just treat symptoms but work specifically on the underlying functional causes.
Before studying dentistry, you trained as a naturopath and hypnotherapist. How does this combination shape your view of health and treatment?

Both have significantly broadened my perspective on health. I no longer see just the patient with toothache, but the entire 'package' they bring with them. My screening deliberately goes beyond the obvious complaints and often asks questions that initially surprise patients but reveal key connections.
Most people probably think of teeth first when it comes to dentistry. Why do breathing, tongue position, swallowing and chewing play such a big role?

The tongue is the 'queen of posture' – its resting position and function have a major influence on the balance and stability of the muscles and jaw, and thus on regulation throughout the entire body system. If this finely tuned interplay of breathing, swallowing and chewing falls out of balance – for example through mouth breathing – this often shows up not only as tooth decay and gum disease, but also as unconscious compensatory habits such as teeth grinding or clenching, which point to disturbed function.
What signs do you see particularly often in your practice when mouth closure, mouth breathing or tongue position are out of balance?

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.13.text.text: How the “ray of happiness” improves eyes, ears and skin

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.14.text.text: Dear laser… you are the concentrated light that makes these five readers beam. You've taken away their pain, helped them hear again and see better. For 50 years, you've been making the world brighter. A BamS report on the laser, the ray of happiness

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.15.text.text: Where do dentists use the laser?

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.16.text.text: Dr Stephan Ziegler of the KU64 dental practice, Berlin: “Mainly in the treatment of periodontitis, an inflammation of the gums and the structures supporting the teeth. The laser makes it easier than hand instruments to reach deep gum pockets, which can then be cleared of bacteria. It also works without contact, germ-free and sterile, so the gums can heal more quickly afterwards.”

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.17.text.text: Do patients with statutory health insurance have to pay extra for the laser?

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.18.text.text: Dr Ziegler: “Private health insurers cover the cost. Those with statutory health insurance pay around 20 to 30 Euro extra per tooth.”

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.2.text.text: Here follows an interview with Dominik Demski, trainee dental nurse and, from now on, assistant to dentist and KU64 owner Dr Stephan Ziegler:

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.20.text.text: Dr Ziegler: “No. The light beams feel like small stings. Anyone who is sensitive needs a local anaesthetic, just as with treatment using the conventional drill.”

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.21.text.text: Source: By Anna Meissner, Volker Weinl and Kerstin Quassowsky for Bild am Sonntag, 24.05.2010

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.22.text.text: No red wine, no coffee – Dr Ziegler in Maxim – interview about beautiful white teeth

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.23.text.text: Dr Ziegler, what should be kept in mind when whitening teeth at home?

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.24.text.text: While wearing the tray, you must not eat or drink anything. Foods that stain, such as red wine, red sauces, beetroot, berry juice and so on, must also be avoided during the whitening days. Before and after wearing the tray, the teeth must be thoroughly brushed and cleaned. It's also worth noting that no intensive fluoride treatment should be carried out in the four weeks before whitening.”

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.26.text.text: In the first phase after whitening, staining foods (see above) as well as drinks such as red wine, coffee and black tea should be avoided completely – and even after that, only consumed in moderation.

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.27.text.text: Is there a risk with home whitening?

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.28.text.text: The only risk factor lies in how it's used: incorrect application can cause chemical burns to the gums.

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.29.text.text: Tell us the truth about men as patients!

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.3.text.text: When did you first hear about training as a dental nurse, and which aspects of this profession sparked your interest?

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.30.text.text: Men know more precisely what they want, and once they've made up their mind, they're happy to spend a lot of money on it. Men are definitely more sensitive to pain than women. They often say at first that they don't want any injection, but end up needing one anyway.

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.4.text.text: I've always had a strong interest in this field. Even at school, I was interested in anatomy and in medical caring professions.

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.5.text.text: Have you ever faced discrimination because of your choice?

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.6.text.text: No, never! I feel very comfortable and confident in what I do. There have never been any negative comments – if anything, positive ones, sometimes full of surprise!

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.7.text.text: How was your decision to enter a profession traditionally dominated by women received in your personal circle?

beitrag.interviews.bloecke.8.text.text: Everyone was genuinely happy for me. What matters is choosing a profession you're truly interested in. I think men can also have real sensitivity towards patients and their needs – something usually only credited to women.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.55.text.text: KU64 – YoungStars is KU64's new world of holistic dental care for children and teenagers. A huge, colourful play area with a ball pit, climbing wall, "tooth decay cave", PlayStation and lots of great books gives kids plenty of room for play, fun and a relaxed visit to the dentist.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.56.text.text: Special features of the KU64 children's dental team include child hypnosis, little magic tricks, and treatment with laughing gas – so that both children and grown-ups simply love going to the dentist! It's no secret that the KU64 team of specialists has twenty years of dental experience in preventive care and orthodontics. With cool braces and brackets, our children's dentists give kids a cheeky, gorgeous smile. Young children are gently introduced to dental treatment through play at the KU64 Doctor School. At the end, they receive fun stamps on a "certificate". The ambitious goal of the KU64 team:

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.57.text.text: "The little ones should leave our practice with a smile and come back with a smile," says Dr Stephan Ziegler, dentist and owner of KU64.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.58.text.text: A genuine innovation at KU64 is preventive dental care for children with a success guarantee – no tooth decay up to the age of 18. The KU64 programme is so well designed that, following a tooth decay risk test, the following guarantee can be given: children will remain free of tooth decay if they attend preventive check-ups at individually set intervals. Participation in the programme is covered by a flat monthly fee of between 10 and 20 Euro (NOTE: THIS OFFER NO LONGER EXISTS), depending on the risk level determined. If the success rate is not 100%, all dental treatments and measures for the young patients are free of charge!

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.61.text.text: Then KU64 is the right place for you! 30 dentists covering all specialisms take care of beautiful new teeth. We specialise in complete aesthetic restorations – a process many know as a "makeover"! Find out what options we offer in this article!

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.65.text.text: In January, the Berlin dental practice KU64 opened KU64-Youngstars for children's dentistry. A large crowd of children stormed the adventure world. The climbing wall, the slide and the ball pit were claimed straight away. A practice safari led children and parents through new treatment rooms, play corners and the newly created "tooth decay cave".

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.66.text.text: At KU64, children aren't greeted by a magician as they were at the opening, but by a member of staff who can do magic too. Here, there are play areas instead of waiting areas. Young children from around two or three years old who need treatment and time to get used to things first go to the Doctor School. Through play, they become familiar with the treatment situation and receive a certificate confirming that they're ready for the dentist.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.67.text.text: Unlike the children's dental practice motto "open wide or general anaesthetic", the KU64 children's dentist takes time to ease any fear. Through magic tricks, child hypnosis, music, stories and many other little helpers, general anaesthetic can be avoided in 98 percent of cases.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.68.text.text: New is preventive dental care for children with a success guarantee. Following a tooth decay risk test, the practice guarantees: children will remain free of tooth decay up to the age of 18 if they attend preventive check-ups at individually set intervals. Participation is covered by a flat monthly fee of between ten and twenty Euro, depending on the risk level determined. If the success rate is not 100 percent, all dental treatments and measures are free of charge.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.70.text.text: KU64 reinvents the children's dental practice: with a success guarantee against tooth decay in children!

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.72.text.text: On 24 January, a huge area for paediatric dentistry called KU64-Youngstars opened at the KU64 dental practice at Kurfürstendamm 64. A great crowd of children stormed this unique world of experience.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.73.text.text: Some of the highlights, such as the climbing wall, the slide and the ball pit – the first of their kind in a children's dental practice in Berlin – were immediately claimed. A practice safari led children and parents through the new treatment rooms and cosy play corners. The newly created tooth decay cave caused great amazement, and while the magician Ully Loup, known from television, revealed all kinds of magic tricks, a mascot in the shape of an oversized tooth pirate wandered through the rooms and was the most popular photo subject.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.74.text.text: At KU64, children are not greeted by this magician, but by a member of staff who can also do magic. Here, there are no waiting areas for children, only play areas. Very young children (from age 2-3) who need treatment – but also need to get used to the situation first – start out in the "doctor school". Here, they get to know the treatment situation through play, and at the end, just like at school, they receive a certificate confirming that they are now ready for dental treatment.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.75.text.text: Unlike the classic children's dental practice, run on the motto "open wide or general anaesthetic", our paediatric dentist takes the time to help children overcome their fear. Through magic for children, hypnosis for children, music, stories, pleasant-tasting numbing gels and many other little aids, general anaesthetic can be avoided in 98% of cases.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.76.text.text: A genuine innovation at KU64 is preventive care for children with a success guarantee – free of tooth decay up to the age of 18. The programme is so well thought out that, after a tooth decay risk test, we are confident enough to give this guarantee. What we promise: children stay free of tooth decay if they attend preventive check-ups at individually set intervals. Taking part in the programme costs a flat monthly rate of between 10 and 20 Euro (NOTE: THIS OFFER NO LONGER EXISTS), depending on the risk determined. Should the outcome not be 100% successful, all dental treatments and measures are free of charge! Through this programme, the interests of child, parents and dentist at KU64 are all aligned! Here, the dentists are pleased (including financially) when teeth stay free of decay.

Yevgeni Viktorov MSc (Master of Science Periodontology) is this year's winner of the "YOUNG ESTHETICS" promotional prize awarded by the German Society for Aesthetic Dentistry (DGÄZ). beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.82.text.text: Dr Yevgeni Viktorov presented a fully documented, interdisciplinary case on improving red and white aesthetics, complete with digital images and full situation and working models. beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.95.text.text: The mere smell at the dentist's is enough to make anxious characters break out in a sweat – not to mention the whirring sound of the drill and the sight of the bulky treatment chair. So the KU64 dentists have set themselves an ambitious goal: “The little ones should leave our practice with a smile and come back with a smile,” says Nadia Mokbel, paediatric dentist at KU64 Zahnspezialisten and a mother herself. The atmosphere can play a big part in whether children tremble when another dental visit is due.

beitrag.kinder-betreuung.bloecke.96.text.text: The Graft architects – known to the wider public as the “Brad Pitt architects” – have already designed the other rooms at the KU64 practice. Now the sixth floor is being converted into the KU64 Kids Club, so that even particularly anxious children and teenagers won't shy away from their six-monthly check-up. Light-flooded rooms and bright colours help them feel at ease. Sometimes that uneasy feeling simply disappears while romping around, for instance in the futuristic area with its colourful ball pit and slide. For teenagers, there's internet access and a Playstation. At the brushing fountain, they learn proper oral hygiene. (kni.)

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.anriss.text: As one of the largest and most modern dental practices in Europe, we have for years focused on innovation and high-tech, while also prioritising digitalisation, resource conservation, energy efficiency, recycling and environmental awareness

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.bloecke.0.text: As one of the largest and most modern dental practices in Europe, we have for years focused on innovation and high-tech, while also prioritising digitalisation, resource conservation, energy efficiency, recycling and environmental awareness! Here’s an overview of what we practise every day!

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.bloecke.1.text:
Public transport pass instead of company car
Our staff can choose to receive a public transport pass. There is also a rather restrained company car policy – but only for electric vehicles.

Water for staff
We treat our own drinking water on site – this means avoiding the purchase of over 2,000 plastic water bottles (for our 200 staff) every month!

Social commitment
Through the registered association BIG SMILE E.V., we help disadvantaged children in Berlin, Brandenburg and South Africa.

Saving the rainforest
As a practice, we've purchased 'rainforest shares', making our contribution against rainforest deforestation.

Recruitment and staff administration
All processes are fully digitalised – from the online application right through to payroll!

Home office & video conferences
Thanks to these two options, we save time, fuel costs and on-site resources.

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.bloecke.2.text:
Digital is green
The further we digitalise the practice, the more paper, packaging, energy and resources we save! One example: the medical history form that patients used to fill in ran to 3 pages – now it's all done digitally on a tablet. For years now, we've had no paper patient records or conventional X-rays. We handle recall reminders entirely digitally too – no post, no paper!

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.bloecke.3.text: Here are more processes that run entirely digitally at KU64:

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.bloecke.4.text:
Less waste – more environment
We rely on centralised procurement management. We bundle orders and consistently separate packaging so it can be reused as recyclable material. We take care to produce as little waste as possible, ideally none at all. We use only reusable cups in the treatment rooms. One member of staff is responsible for sterilising instruments. She collects and sterilises the instruments centrally – rather than each dental nurse doing this individually for her own room. We naturally use refillable materials and deliberately avoid single-use items where we can. Our waste separation follows the medical requirements for a dental practice. Amalgam removed by drilling is collected and sent for metal recovery.

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.bloecke.5.text:
Prevention instead of repair
Prevention costs less in the end and is also more sustainable for the environment. For example, we use biocompatible materials for dental restorations and were one of the first practices in Berlin to stop using amalgam completely.
Durability means more savings
But when repairs are needed: our fillings and dental restorations last a very long time. This durability saves you time and money, and saves the environment packaging as well as production and transport chains. Our very long guarantee periods – far longer than legally required – are clear proof of this.

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.bloecke.6.text:
Our own laboratory – short distances
Our dental restorations are produced entirely in-house, either in our own laboratory or even in the treatment room thanks to CEREC technology, which we were among the first in Berlin to offer. No transport costs!

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.bloecke.7.text:
Living vertical gardens
In no fewer than 3 places, living vertical gardens do more than look good on the walls – they also create a pleasant atmosphere, provide plenty of oxygen and reduce dental practice smells! Our green 'lungs'!

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.bloecke.8.text:
Bamboo instead of plastic
Our new multi-use toothbrush made from renewable materials such as bamboo now replaces the disposable plastic toothbrush in the oral hygiene room! We encourage our patients to bring their own toothbrush if they'd like to freshen up before treatment. If they forget or haven't had the chance, we now help out – but in an environmentally conscious way, because caring for the environment starts with brushing your teeth.

beitrag.ku64-die-gruene-praxis.bloecke.9.text:
Energy efficiency
Our windows and outer doors are foil-coated so that heat doesn't escape in winter and the sun's warmth doesn't get in during summer. Timer switches on numerous devices, as well as motion-sensor lighting, help save electricity.

beitrag.ku64-in-den-medien.bloecke.185.t.text: One in ten doctors' practices is now also open on Saturdays or Sundays

beitrag.ku64-in-den-medien.bloecke.186.t.text: Anyone who fell ill at the weekend used to be doubly unlucky: alongside having to endure their symptoms, those affected mostly found medical help only at a hospital's emergency department – and often only after hours of waiting. After all, doctors' practices were closed on Saturdays and Sundays. „But pain doesn't take days off,“ says Petros Prontis, manager of the dental practice KU64 on Kudamm.

beitrag.ku64-in-den-medien.bloecke.187.t.text: The practice is open every day: on weekdays until 8pm, and at weekends until 7pm. „For many working patients, this means they can visit the dentist without stress,“ says Prontis. But the dentists benefit too. The generous opening hours have brought the practice additional patients.

beitrag.ku64-in-den-medien.bloecke.193.t.text: Feel-good drilling - the first dental practices discover the wellness idea

beitrag.ku64-in-den-medien.bloecke.195.t.text: More and more practices are following suit. When the drill whirrs and the smell of dental chemicals fills the air, many people start to panic. That's why some clever US dentists have given their practices a makeover and a new label. In the dental spa, there are no shrill noises and no unpleasant chemical smell, but calming colours, soft music and friendly staff who give patients a neck massage in between.

beitrag.ku64-in-den-medien.bloecke.196.t.text: In Berlin too, dentists are now trying their hand at feel-good drilling. The dentists at the KU64 joint practice in Charlottenburg were the pioneers. They had their practice premises designed by the renowned architecture firm Graft. Meanwhile, more and more practices in Berlin are following this concept. Patients respond well to the new wellness practices, though the relaxing effect is probably limited - after all, a dentist's chair is never quite that comfortable.

beitrag.ku64-in-den-medien.bloecke.201.t.text: „The resolution to “quit smoking” is often made but rarely kept. The dentists at KU64 have led by example since the practice was founded. Neither staff nor patients are allowed to light up a cigarette on the premises. (…)

beitrag.ku64-in-den-medien.bloecke.202.t.text: The risk factors of smoking go far beyond respiratory illnesses. The toxic effect of tobacco smoke weakens the immune defences, which can lead to gum inflammation and periodontitis. Smoking also disrupts wound healing, for example after an implant has been placed, resulting in infections and even implant loss. Another unpleasant side effect of tobacco use is bad breath: studies have found a higher concentration of tooth-decay-causing bacteria in the saliva of smokers. (…)

beitrag.ku64-in-den-medien.bloecke.203.t.text: By the way, most statutory health insurers cover the cost of a stop-smoking course. The KU64 team is happy to advise anyone interested.“

GRAFT – always staying relaxed
February 2007

“They are the architects of great relaxation. They build holidays, the most beautiful dune houses in the Caribbean, undulating hotels along America’s coasts. And even Germany’s capital, long tense with ideology, they want to help find a relaxation it has never known, using their massage-soft forms. Of all places, it is to be Berlin’s Schlossplatz, a site of bitter debate over reconstructed Baroque façades, absurd palace demolitions and the republic’s proper politics of history altogether. What does the architecture group called Graft make of this historical weight? They make it float. (…)

They love connecting, bonding, merging – even a dental practice in Berlin they turn into a place of pure calm. Nothing feels clinical, nothing smells like a dentist’s. Sun-yellow walls curve like dunes, the waiting room becomes a cosy space with wine-red loungers and a fireplace. Architecture as pain therapy: fear is meant to turn into relaxation. (…)”

The noise level drops, people and cars are no longer part of an unceasing stream but become singular occurrences. The pulse of big cities is now only perceived by those who don't seek sleep but prefer artificial light sources to daylight. In his photo series "Fast City", begun in 2009, Rolf Zscharnack works with a combination of panning shots and long exposure.

The lights of the city, the neon signs and illuminated house fronts become abstract streaks of light. People fade into shadowy apparitions. The concrete place becomes a backdrop – the backdrop for a drama that, as it appears in "Fast City", never actually took place. The photograph becomes a visualised vision of light. "In the Fast City series, I expose the objects and buildings, not the people. They disappear into blur, as if erased, because they have no light of their own. Due to the speed of the camera's movement, it is often no longer possible to tell where the photo was taken."

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.1.te.text: Which home remedies really help with oral thrush, what should you avoid, and when is medication the right choice? Find out what can ease symptoms and discomfort – and why home remedies alone rarely solve oral thrush.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.10.t.text: What home remedies usually can't do

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.100..text: Mild home remedies can help to soothe the mucosa and ease symptoms somewhat. They can help bridge the time until a medical assessment and treatment, but they don't replace it.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.102..text: If the white patches increase, eating and swallowing become painful, or there's no clear improvement after a few days, you shouldn't put up with oral thrush any longer. It then makes sense to contact your dentist. This allows a quick check on whether it really is oral thrush and which treatment will help you.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.103..text: 5. Treat oral thrush specifically once diagnosed

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.104..text: Effective treatment usually involves antifungal medication, which works against the candida infection. For mild to moderate cases, locally acting remedies are often used. More severe or widespread infections may require systemic medication.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.105..text: How quickly home remedies and medication can work for oral thrush

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.106..text: Home remedies can often ease symptoms in the short term. Here you can find out when initial relief is possible and from what point medication or a medical assessment becomes important.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.107..text:
Straight away: home remedies can briefly ease the burning
Water, lukewarm tea or probiotic yoghurt can often soothe sensitive areas in the mouth for a short while.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.108..text: After 1 day: the fungus remains despite home remedies

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.109..text: If your mouth feels a bit better for a while, this doesn't mean the fungus is retreating. Lasting recovery without medication is rare.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.11.p.text: Replace a dental or medical check-up

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.110..text:
After 3 to 4 days: time to see a dentist and take medication
By this point, self-help usually isn't enough if symptoms such as white patches, bad breath, burning or pain persist. Home remedies can be used alongside treatment if agreed with your dentist.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.111..text:
After a few days on medication: the first effects are often noticeable
The burning usually eases and the mucosa can settle down. The fungus in the mouth is now being specifically treated.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.112..text:
After 7 to 14 days: the fungal infection subsides
Complete healing usually takes one to two weeks. What matters is that you use or take the medication regularly.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.113..text:
After 1 to 2 weeks without clear improvement: have the symptoms checked again
If oral thrush persists or comes back despite treatment, the cause and therapy should be reviewed once more. After that, the right care and mindful eating habits can help prevent it from recurring.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.114..text: Which medications can help with oral thrush

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.115..text: The fungal infection itself is usually treated with antifungal medications, which act against fungi such as Candida albicans and the infection they cause, also known as oral candidiasis.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.116..text: “An over-the-counter remedy for oral thrush can be helpful in some cases. What matters is that the treatment matches the cause. Especially if the symptoms are new, getting worse or keep coming back, a check-up with a dentist or doctor is often the best way to recover quickly.”

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.117..text: Over-the-counter medications for fungal infections in the mouth: no substitute for a dental visit

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.118..text: It's often tempting to quickly pick up a remedy from the pharmacy when dealing with oral thrush. Even so, not every product works equally well, and what helps one person doesn't automatically suit another. Especially with babies, children, more severe symptoms, a first occurrence, or if you're unsure whether it's really oral thrush, you shouldn't rely solely on your own diagnosis. In these cases, it's better to have the symptoms checked by a doctor or dentist. The following active ingredients can be used to treat oral thrush specifically:

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.119..text: Nystatin is a well-established active ingredient against fungal infections and is often used locally for oral thrush, for example as an oral gel or solution for the mouth. Its advantage is that it works directly in the mouth. For mild cases, nystatin is often a good first treatment option. In Germany, nystatin oral gels are available over the counter at pharmacies.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.12.t.text: How oral thrush is treated specifically

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.120..text: Miconazole is also one of the well-established active ingredients for oral thrush. It, too, is applied locally, usually as an oral gel. Studies describe nystatin and miconazole as well-researched treatments with similar effectiveness against oral thrush. In Germany, miconazole preparations are available to patients from pharmacies.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.121..text: Prescription-only: when medically prescribed medication is needed

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.122..text: Sometimes it turns out that a pharmacy remedy isn't enough for your situation. This is the case, for example, if the oral thrush is more severe, keeps coming back, causes pain when swallowing, if the immune system is already weakened, or if there's a suspicion that not just the mouth but also the throat or oesophagus is affected. In these cases, you need a medication that is prescribed by a doctor.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.123..text: Fluconazole is a systemically acting antifungal medication. Rather than being applied locally in the mouth, it works against the fungal infection throughout the whole body. Fluconazole is prescription-only in Germany. You receive it after an examination from your doctor or your dentist.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.124..text: Intravenous treatment for oral thrush: rarely needed

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.125..text: Treatment with medication given through a vein is not the standard approach for ordinary oral candidiasis. It's more likely to be considered in exceptional cases, for example when the fungal infection has spread widely, is particularly severe, or oral medication cannot be taken or tolerated.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.126..text: In many cases, however, an ointment or tablet is enough to relieve the symptoms.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.127..text: Home remedies for oral thrush in babies: what parents should know now

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.128..text: “You should take white patches in your baby's mouth seriously. Don't experiment with home remedies – have it checked early by a paediatrician or dentist, so your baby gets the right help quickly.”

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.129..text: Which home remedies and medications make sense for oral thrush in babies

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.13.p.text: With antifungal medication applied directly in the mouth, for example as a gel or solution
In more severe cases, if needed, also with medication that works throughout the whole body

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.130..text: Babies and children should only use home remedies for oral thrush with great caution. It's best to avoid anything that could irritate the sensitive oral mucosa. What adults sometimes find soothing isn't automatically suitable for babies and children. Medications made for adults are also not a good idea for your child.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.131..text: Babies and small children with suspected oral thrush in particular should have their symptoms checked early. This helps prevent the infection from spreading further or making feeding more difficult. Your paediatrician will decide which treatment makes sense and whether medication is needed.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.132..text: Homeopathy and globules for oral thrush: no substitute for medication

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.133..text: There is no scientific evidence that homeopathy and globules specifically treat oral thrush or effectively reduce the fungus in the mouth. However, patients can use them alongside antifungal medication.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.134..text: Checklist: when home remedies for oral thrush are no longer enough

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.135..text: Sometimes it's hard to judge symptoms correctly yourself. The checklist below helps you spot warning signs early. If you answer “yes” to several points, you should have oral thrush checked by a dentist or doctor.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.136..text: Self-check: should I see a doctor?

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.137..text:
☐ The symptoms are new and I'm not sure whether it's really oral thrush.
White patches, a sore tongue and bad breath should be checked by a dentist or doctor. This helps rule out other causes.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.138..text:
☐ So far I have only tried home remedies and have not had the oral thrush treated specifically.
Home remedies and good oral hygiene are generally not enough on their own. They can help bridge the time until a proper assessment, but they do not replace treatment.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.139..text:
☐ Alongside the coating on my tongue, I also have pain when swallowing or eating.
This can be a sign that the infection is more pronounced or is spreading further.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.14.t.text: These home remedies can provide useful support for oral thrush

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.140..text:
☐ The white coating is increasing or keeps coming back quickly.
Recurring or worsening symptoms can point to a persistent case of candidiasis. You should have the causes checked by a doctor or dentist rather than trying to treat them yourself.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.141..text:
☐ I am generally weakened or have pre-existing conditions.
For people with a weakened immune system, after taking antibiotics, with diabetes or other risk factors, a proper medical or dental assessment is especially important.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.142..text:
☐ My baby is feeding less well or seems unsettled while sucking.
Babies and young children with oral thrush should see a paediatrician as early as possible, especially if feeding is becoming more difficult.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.143..text:
☐ I am breastfeeding and have symptoms on my breast or nipples myself.
Oral thrush can be passed between babies, young children and breastfeeding mothers. In that case, both should be treated.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.144..text: Not sure whether your symptoms are really oral thrush?

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.145..text: Have your symptoms and any changes in your mouth checked now by our specialists at KU64, and get an individual recommendation on which treatment makes sense in your case.
