Managing Founding Partner
Profile of Dr Stephan Ziegler

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.15.t.text: Not everything recommended for oral thrush is actually helpful for your mouth's lining. Some home remedies can soothe and make everyday life a little easier. Others irritate the mouth further or achieve very little. With oral thrush, keep the following points in mind:

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.16.t.text: Brush your teeth extra gently for now

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.17.t.text: Gentle oral hygiene is especially important with oral thrush, because the lining of the mouth is irritated and sensitive. Brush your teeth carefully, ideally with a soft toothbrush.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.18.t.text: Replace your toothbrush after the infection has cleared. This stops you reinfecting your healthy mouth with any remaining fungal traces.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.20.t.text: The white fungal coating often sits particularly stubbornly on the back of the tongue. You can clean it carefully, using as little pressure as possible, with a soft tongue cleaner or your toothbrush.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.21.t.text: It's important not to scrub. This irritates the lining further and can cause small injuries.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.22.t.text: Rinse your mouth with water regularly

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.23.t.text: Fungi feed on food residue and spread more quickly in a dry environment. Rinse your mouth after eating and in between meals.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.24.t.text: Important: water doesn't fight the fungus causing the infection. But it can help keep your mouth fresh and the lining moist.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.25.t.text: Clean dentures and splints especially thoroughly

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.26.t.text: Removable dentures, prosthetics or splints offer the fungus a perfect place to hide. Clean these thoroughly every day.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.27.t.text: This helps prevent your mouth from being irritated or affected again and again.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.29.t.text: Sage has a mild disinfecting effect and can gently soothe irritated mucous membranes. Rinse your mouth with sage tea for one to two minutes, several times a day.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.3.te.text: Home remedies can ease the discomfort of oral thrush, such as burning, dryness or a furry feeling in the mouth. Still water, lukewarm sage tea, probiotic natural yoghurt and gentle brushing with a soft toothbrush can all help. Dentures or splints should also be cleaned especially thoroughly during this time. However, home remedies usually don't clear the fungal infection itself. For that, you generally need targeted treatment with an antifungal medication. So have oral thrush checked by a dentist or doctor early on, particularly if you have severe symptoms, pain when swallowing, if a baby is affected, or if there's no improvement after a few days.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.30.t.text: Let the tea cool to room temperature first, so it doesn't irritate your mouth further.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.31.t.text: Soothe your mouth with probiotic natural yoghurt

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.32.t.text: Unsweetened probiotic natural yoghurt can support recovery from oral thrush and have a soothing effect, as it cools the mucous membranes pleasantly and improves the overall feel of the mouth.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.33.t.text: Only use yoghurt without sugar. Sweetened products aren't a good idea with oral thrush, since sugar is the fungus's main food source and makes symptoms worse.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.34.t.text: Use garlic as a natural anti-fungal remedy

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.35.t.text: Garlic is often mentioned as a home remedy against fungal infections. You can use it to support treatment, for example in small amounts in food.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.36.t.text: However, garlic can also sting on irritated mucous membranes. If it feels unpleasant, it's best to leave it out.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.37.t.text: Home remedies don't work the same way for everyone

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.38.t.text: What works well for other people does not automatically mean it will help you too. How well a home remedy works for you depends a great deal on your personal immune system, the specific severity of the fungal infection and your oral flora.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.39.t.text: So listen to your body. Anything that stings, feels tight or uncomfortable is best left out. And usually, one or two gentle measures make more sense than several home remedies at once.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.4.te.text: What home remedies can do for oral thrush – and what only medication can achieve

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.40.t.text: These home remedies should only be used with caution for oral thrush

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.41.t.text: The following home remedies are often recommended for oral thrush. However, they usually only make sense as a supplement, and some are not well tolerated by irritated mucous membranes. So always pay attention to how your mouth reacts.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.43.t.text: Many people find a mild, alcohol-free mouth rinse pleasant, as it gently cleanses the mouth and improves the overall feel. It can also help to gently rinse away loose deposits.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.44.t.text: It's important that the rinse really is mild. Many products contain essential oils or other substances that can sting in an irritated mouth. If the rinse feels unpleasant, rinse with water afterwards and it's best to leave the product out altogether.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.45.t.text: Myrrh tinctures as an anti-inflammatory remedy

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.46.t.text: Myrrh is often recommended for irritated oral mucous membranes. For oral thrush, though, it's only of limited use.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.47.t.text: The reason: many myrrh tinctures contain alcohol. This can cause a noticeable stinging sensation on inflamed mucous membranes and irritate the mouth further. If you use such products at all, do so only very sparingly.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.48.t.text: Oil pulling with coconut oil or sesame oil

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.49.t.text: If you gently swish a teaspoon of sesame or coconut oil between your teeth for a few minutes each morning, it can leave a pleasant feeling in the mouth and help care for the oral cavity.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.5.te.text: A white coating on the tongue, a burning sensation or a furry feeling in the mouth: you might hope that mouth rinses, tea or a bit of extra oral care will sort things out on their own. With a fungal infection like oral thrush, though, this usually isn't enough.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.50.t.text: The benefit for oral thrush isn't well established. So oil pulling can at most be a supplement, but it doesn't replace treatment. It's also important to spit the oil out completely afterwards – not down the drain – and not to swallow it.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.51.t.text: Highly diluted bicarbonate of soda rinse

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.52.t.text: Half a teaspoon of bicarbonate of soda, fully dissolved in a large glass of lukewarm water, is considered a well-established home remedy for regulating your oral flora.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.53.t.text: The right dosage matters: too much bicarbonate of soda, or a paste applied directly to the mucous membrane, can irritate the mouth. If you use bicarbonate of soda, only as a heavily diluted rinse and never directly on sore areas.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.54.t.text: "With oral thrush, more isn't better. Stick to one or two tried-and-tested home remedies that work well for you. Use fewer, but more consistently."

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.55.t.text: Home remedies you're better off avoiding

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.56.t.text: Countless self-treatment tips circulate online that, on closer inspection, do more harm than good.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.57.t.text: Undiluted essential oils such as tea tree oil

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.58.t.text: Essential oils such as tea tree oil are often recommended as a natural remedy against germs or fungi. That may sound plausible, but they're not a good idea for self-treating oral thrush.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.59.t.text: That's because pure essential oils are too harsh for the already inflamed mucous membranes in oral thrush and can make the symptoms worse.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.6.te.text: Home remedies can soothe irritated mucous membranes and make everyday life a little more comfortable. They can, for example, ease burning, keep the mouth moist and support treatment. They usually don't eliminate the fungus itself (typically Candida albicans). For that, you generally need a suitable antifungal medication.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.61.t.text: Strong mouth rinses often give the impression of cleaning particularly thoroughly. That's exactly the problem with oral thrush.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.62.t.text: Alcohol-based or very intense rinses irritate the already compromised mucous membrane and cause a stinging sensation. At the same time, alcohol tends to dry out the mouth. And a dry, irritated mouth is exactly what you don't need with oral thrush. The mucous membrane then often recovers less well, and eating, drinking or speaking become even more uncomfortable.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.63.t.text: Irritating home remedies such as apple cider vinegar or lemon

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.64.t.text: Apple cider vinegar or lemon juice are often recommended online as home remedies because they're seen as natural and “cleansing”. For an inflamed mouth, though, they're usually too harsh.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.65.t.text: With oral thrush, acid can sting badly and irritate sore areas even more. On top of that, rinsing frequently with acidic solutions can also put a strain on your teeth. It's best to avoid these kinds of experiments in your mouth.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.67.t.text: Honey is considered a tried-and-tested home remedy for inflammation or a sore throat. Yeast products, too, are sometimes recommended for a healthy “flora” in the body. With oral thrush, this isn't advisable.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.68.t.text: Since Candida albicans is itself a yeast fungus that feeds almost exclusively on carbohydrates and sugar, you could actually fuel the infection this way. Instead, try to cut heavily sugary foods, honey and yeast preparations from your diet as far as possible, to deprive the fungus of its main food source.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.69.t.text: Good to know: your oral flora is easily thrown off balance

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.7.te.text: Important: anything that stings or further irritates your mucous membrane can make symptoms worse. It's best to have oral thrush checked by a dentist early on.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.70.t.text: Many microorganisms live naturally side by side in your mouth. As long as this balance stays stable, the oral mucosa usually remains healthy. If it's thrown off balance, a yeast fungus like Candida can spread more easily.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.71.t.text: This can happen, for example, after taking antibiotics, with a dry mouth, from a diet too high in sugar, or in people with a weakened immune system. Home remedies can then help support recovery, for instance by soothing the mucosa and being gentle on the mouth. However, they usually don't get rid of the fungus itself. That's why targeted treatment with medication often makes sense for oral thrush.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.72.t.text: At a glance: commonly recommended home remedies and tips against oral thrush

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.76.t.text: Gentle oral care with a soft toothbrush and normal pressure

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.77.t.text: Mild rinses, as long as they feel pleasant and don't sting

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.78.t.text: Essential oils or tea tree oil in the mouth, as they often irritate the mucosa

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.79.t.text: Gently clean the tongue too, but only if it doesn't hurt

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.8.te.text: What home remedies can achieve with oral thrush

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.80.t.text: Use myrrh tincture only very sparingly, as many products contain alcohol and can sting

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.81.t.text: Alcohol-based or very strong rinses, as they can dry out and further irritate the mouth

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.82.t.text: Rinsing with water, if this makes your mouth feel more comfortable

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.83.t.text: Coconut oil or oil pulling at most as a supportive measure, as it's too mild and superficial

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.84.t.text: Irritating home remedy experiments that sting noticeably or feel unpleasant in the mouth (e.g. apple cider vinegar)

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.85.t.text: Clean dentures or splints thoroughly and relieve the mucosa as much as possible

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.86.t.text: Baking soda rinse (diluted), for a more alkaline environment. However, not too highly concentrated.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.87.t.text: Sugar and yeast, as they act as “food” for the fungus and weaken the oral flora.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.88.t.text: Use lukewarm sage tea as a mouth rinse if it feels soothing

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.89.t.text: Probiotic yoghurt to help improve the balance of bacteria in the mouth

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.9.pu.text: Make eating and drinking more comfortable
Strengthen the immune system and help prevent a repeat infection

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.90.t.text: Garlic, due to its mild antifungal properties

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.91.t.text: Even though home remedies can certainly help, don't lose sight of what matters: home remedies are a way of bridging the gap until you see your dentist. They are not a lasting solution for oral thrush.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.92.t.text: A dental assessment brings clarity and often saves you unnecessary trial and error with home remedies. Once you have a diagnosis, start straight away with the prescribed medication instead.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.93.t.text: Immediate help for oral thrush: what you can do now

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.94.t.text: With oral thrush, it's important to act with care: protect the oral mucosa, gently ease the symptoms, and seek medical help in good time.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.95.t.text: 1. Watch out for typical complaints and symptoms

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.96.t.text: White patches, a burning feeling on the tongue and palate, a furry sensation in the mouth, or pain when eating and drinking are typical signs of oral thrush. If you notice such changes, it's worth paying close attention rather than simply ignoring the symptoms.

beitrag.mundpilz-hausmittel.bloecke.98.t.text: Don't try to scrub off the white patches, and don't repeatedly try new remedies. This puts extra strain on your mucosa. Eat and drink mild foods where possible, avoid anything very hot, spicy or acidic, and keep brushing your teeth and cleaning your mouth as usual, but consciously gently.

Thanks to high hygiene standards:
all dental treatments are possible
German Dental Association and Association of Medical Professions thank practice teams

Berlin, 14 May 2020 – The German Dental Association (BZÄK) and the Association of Medical Professions (Verband medizinischer Fachberufe e.V.) are informing patients that dental practices are once again offering preventive care and dental treatments in full. The high hygiene and infection control standards already in place before the Covid pandemic have been further strengthened, ensuring safety and effective protection for patients and staff alike. Current findings show that, worldwide, dental treatments have not led to increased Covid-19 infections among either dental teams or patients.
Henner Bunke, D.M.D./Univ. of Florida, BZÄK board representative for Dental

KU64, the renowned dental practice on Kurfürstendamm in Berlin, is now listed on Versicherungen-online.de. The partnership with Versicherungen-online.de, a portal for private health insurance (PKV), underlines KU64's commitment to service and patient comfort. Patients can leave reviews, strengthening the relationship between the practice and its patients. The listing makes it easier to access high-quality dental care and information about private health insurance.

Assistants (ZFA) and President of the Dental Association of Lower Saxony: "Visiting the dentist is safe for patients. That's why I recommend not postponing treatments, and especially not the important preventive check-ups. Good oral health requires regular monitoring and examination at the practice. Thanks to the well-established teamwork between dentists and dental staff, Germany's high hygiene standards are ensured. The daily commitment, strong sense of responsibility and loyalty shown by dental assistants, even during the Covid period, cannot be praised highly enough. They play a vital part in the excellent work carried out in dental practices."

"The situation regarding protective equipment has improved significantly," confirms Sylvia Gabel, Head of the ZFA Department at the Association of Medical Professions (Verband medizinischer Fachberufe e.V.).

"In addition, practice teams have reviewed and expanded their hygiene management, so that both patients and dental assistants can feel safe while the necessary occupational health and safety measures are observed." The BZÄK and the Association of Medical Professions e.V. thank the practice teams for their outstanding work during this time of crisis. Both partners are committed to health protection and teamwork. Even outside the pandemic, they are always there for their patients with dedication and empathy, setting aside their own concerns to ensure smooth operations in dental practices across Germany.

Unfortunately, poor teeth carry the stigma that one must be at fault and simply should have brushed better. In many cases, this is simply not true. That's why I find it brave and meaningful that Aline is sharing her story publicly, easing the psychological pressure on other patients in a similar situation. Aline has displaced canine teeth, meaning that in her case the canines lie deep within the jawbone but never erupted. About one in a hundred people has such a displacement, but the extent seen in Aline's case occurs in only about one in a thousand. March 2017
Coach Dipl. Ing. Alberto Ojeda prepares our reception team for the service offensive!
Perception and communication are sharpened.

The coaching enables staff members to recognise, both verbally and non-verbally, exactly what a patient's concern is, and to respond accordingly. A key part of this is truly listening and anticipating the patient's needs. In other words, they take care of the matter in a way that creates an element of surprise. If a problem arises, staff think one step ahead and act accordingly.
Knowledge is good; seeing yourself reflected teaches you something; repetition makes it stick.

Another extremely important part of the coaching is video feedback. Thanks to the motivating team spirit that has been built, staff members are open to 'looking at themselves critically'. These recordings are reviewed during coaching sessions. The results are remarkable. Staff members welcome open, systematically moderated feedback. They feel supported by the team, correct one another, and keep improving. 'You can only learn body language and new behaviour by experiencing it yourself,' the mime artist and communication expert Samy Molcho once said. In prepared role-play exercises, weaknesses become visible. Here too, staff receive suggestions for improvement, and their individual presence is refined through repetition.

The various facets of the coaching, combined with the team spirit that has been built, demonstrably create a lasting effect and an improvement in service at reception. This benefits not only the existing team, but also helps new staff members integrate well into the KU64 team.
This process is still ongoing, but the results are already visible. We would like to thank our patients in advance for their open and constructive feedback during this phase.
We would also like to thank our coach, Dipl. Ing. Alberto Ojeda, in advance for the coaching and his valuable support!

Yours,
Dr Stephan Ziegler
Dentist & KU64 owner

This has always been our motto, but in this year of practice expansion (the new rooms are expected to open in autumn), we want to raise patient wellbeing even further with a service offensive! A carefully considered coaching programme is preparing our reception team for a new patient experience at KU64.

The coaching focuses on service quality and preparing the reception team for KU64's new challenge: alongside the expansion, the reception areas for children and adults will be separated after the renovation of the 6th and 4th floors. This challenge requires strong team spirit and a genuine commitment to a philosophy of high-level service. To this end, Dipl. Ing. Alberto Ojeda has been coaching our eight-strong reception team since late 2016.

The reception offensive aims to ensure that the team works well together on a personal level, complements each other professionally, and offers exceptional service. This allows KU64's reception to create a sense of wellbeing from the moment a patient arrives. Something like: the patient arrives and is welcomed like a king or emperor! The goal is to bring genuine, professional care for patients to life. This attitude is repeatedly reviewed and reinforced during coaching.
What does the coaching involve?
A motivating team spirit is built and reinforced.

This resolves any internal tensions. As a result, the team pulls together and brings more presence and empathy to every patient situation. The warm atmosphere at reception and in the waiting area is meant to underline the feeling of 'coming home'.
Focus on quality assurance.

beitrag.referral-growth-culture-award-20.text: We are thrilled: KU64 has been honoured with the Referral & Growth Culture Award 2026 from Sprad. For us, this is more than just an award. It highlights the employer culture we have been living successfully for around

We are thrilled: KU64 has been honoured with the Referral & Growth Culture Award 2026 from Sprad. For us, this is more than just an award. It highlights the employer culture we have been living successfully for around 20 years now. It's a good opportunity to introduce KU64 as an employer in a bit more detail. In this blog post, you can read what team spirit, development and employee referrals have to do with the leaf-cutter ant colony in KU64's paediatric dentistry department, and why this image fits our everyday working life so well.
Where design, enjoyment and everyday team life come together

“This award is more than a trophy. It's proof that trust isn't a one-way street. Anyone who proudly recommends their employer to friends and family does so voluntarily, and hardly anything is more credible than that.”

Our strong performance in these areas is also reflected in our figures: 55 new hires in 2025, almost 40 percent of them through internal referrals. For us, recommendations are a strategy we actually live by. They lead to lower recruiting costs for agencies and job adverts, faster hiring, and teams that fit well together, both personally and professionally.
How referrals turn into new colleagues

At KU64, we deliberately make it simple to recommend someone. We regularly share open positions with our team through our newsletter. If someone recommends a suitable person and they join us, we record this in our software. After six months, the system automatically reminds us whether the probationary period was completed successfully. If it was, the person who made the referral receives a bonus of 500 euros. One example from our team shows just how well this works: a colleague has brought in more than five new employees for KU64 this way.
Working hand in hand every day

To understand why colleagues recommend KU64 so readily, it helps to look at our everyday work. Many things interlock here much like in a leafcutter ant colony – and we actually have one, in the Formicarium in the children's area of our practice.

The patient is always the connecting link. Depending on what they need, between ten and twelve people at KU64 are involved in their care: from the first phone call with our telephone team, through reception, treatment by the dentist and their assistant, right through to our dental administrative staff, oral surgery or preventive care. On top of this, our team speaks more than 30 languages, which allows us to support many patients in an even more personal and understandable way.

For all of this to run smoothly, we coordinate closely across several floors – digitally via Microsoft Teams, but just as much in person, in the corridor, in the kitchen or directly in the treatment room. It is precisely this close, reliable way of working together that makes KU64 a place where many of us enjoy working and want to stay for the long term.
Training that creates long-term prospects

Training is an important part of KU64's future. We currently train 22 apprentices as dental assistants (ZFA), deliberately investing in the specialists of tomorrow. This makes KU64 the practice with the most dental apprentices in Berlin and Brandenburg at present. Dental assistants are in particularly high demand today and hard to find on the job market. This makes it all the more important to us to inspire young people for this profession early on. Social media helps us here too, as many of our apprentices find their way to us through this channel.

An interior design reminiscent of a desert landscape, the smell of coffee, lounge music and a fireplace: there are few workplaces that radiate as much atmosphere the moment you walk in as KU64. Lunch together in our cosy staff restaurant, prepared by top chefs, along with barbecue evenings, trips and unforgettable celebrations, make KU64 a special place beyond the treatment rooms too, for our now 250 employees.
“Anyone who is curious, wants to grow and approaches new tasks with commitment is exactly right for KU64.”

What we would like potential applicants to know: don't change jobs just for a slightly higher salary. Far more important is an environment that brings joy to your work, allows you to develop and opens up long-term prospects. At KU64, this also includes continuous further training: every member of our team completes at least two training courses or external further education programmes per year.
Celebrating loyalty and belonging to the team

Loyalty and long-standing ties are not overlooked at KU64 – they are deliberately valued. For our 20th anniversary, our boss invited the entire team on a several-day cruise in the Mediterranean. Many still remember this experience fondly today. We also show that loyalty matters to us when it comes to work anniversaries: anyone who has been part of KU64 for five years can go out for a meal worth 250 euros with four favourite colleagues. After ten years with the team, a cruise or another five-day trip awaits.
Recognised across many areas

The Referral & Growth Culture Award 2026 is further proof for us of the high standard KU64 pursues in every area – from dentistry to service and architecture, right through to team culture. Our more than 70 awards over 20 years show that KU64's high standards are also regularly recognised from the outside.

A shared passion for the work

Whether dentist, orthodontist or dental hygienist: for many of us, KU64 is more than just a workplace. It is a place where people come together who are passionate about truly good, holistic dentistry. What makes KU64 special as an employer is exactly this sense of togetherness: genuine team spirit across four locations, high standards, opportunities for professional and personal development, flexible working models and modern digital structures.
“As Europe's largest single dental practice, we are big enough to offer real career paths and specialisations, yet we are still not an anonymous employer. That combination is rare.”

We are a strong, well-regarded team that sticks together and learns from one another. That's why many colleagues not only stay with us for a long time, but also recommend KU64 to friends and family. We are delighted that this has now been recognised with the Referral & Growth Culture Award 2026.
What lies behind our award

For us, this is the first time we have taken part in such a large international competition on referral and growth culture, organised by Sprad. Well-known employers such as Decathlon, Schindler and ING were also honoured there. The judging looked at how effectively we use our staff networks to attract talent, and how firmly employee development and internal career opportunities are actually embedded in our company culture. KU64 was recognised twice, in the categories “Outstanding Referral Culture” and “Outstanding Growth Culture”.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.17.tex.text: Would you like to see what our oral hygiene room for patients looks like, so you can freshen up before your check-up? Or our waiting room roof terrace? beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.18.tex.text: Here's what happened on our social media channels in July

All the latest news about our social commitment, our events, and of course our team members always appears fresh in your timeline on our channels. We also share exclusive updates there about all offers and discount promotions for patients. So go and follow us on Facebook, Twitter, Instagram and TikTok.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.2.text.text: On 14 September, we took part in the 2023 company hiking day. beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.20.tex.text: Here's what happened on our social media in July:

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.21.tex.text: As part of our "YPP After Work Event" series, we invited fellow dentists to our practice on 3 July. Our implantologists Dr. Jan Wagner and Dr. Surian Herrmann presented the entire workflow – from planning guided surgery with coDiagnostiX®, through the surgical procedure in a live operation, to coordinating between surgery, prosthetics and dental technology for the perfect immediate temporary restoration. Exchanging ideas with colleagues is invaluable, and you as a patient benefit most from it! We documented the event extensively on social media.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.22.tex.text: On 6 July, our summer exhibition opening took place, to which we invited you via social media. This year we're exhibiting illustrations, drawings and comics by the artist Sascha Vievers. It's our first exhibition opening aimed also at kids and families – the little ones will be thrilled to see Spiderman as art, and might even want to buy it! You can get a first impression in our video on Instagram. Missed the opening? No problem. We're showing the pictures until the end of September. So just drop by.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.23.tex.text: We've already had a bit of a celebration on social media: KU64 has now been around for 18 years! In July 2005, we opened KU64 at Kurfürstendamm 64. Our boss and KU64 owner Dr. Stephan Ziegler had already run a dental practice in Wilmersdorf for 14 years. He then decided to design a completely new kind of practice: EXTRAORDINARY, UNUSUAL, QUIRKY, DIFFERENT, MODERN, INNOVATIVE, HIGH QUALITY AND AS YELLOW AS THE SUN! And now we're celebrating KU64's 18th anniversary at the Kudamm location.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.24.tex.text: On 7 July, our big summer party took place, where the whole team of the practice raised a glass, not least to our anniversary. With great weather, there were some lovely photos, all of which you can find on social media.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.25.tex.text: But it's not just about celebrating to keep us such a great team – further training is important too! That's why, for example, we held a caries screening test workshop with speaker Dr. Lutz Laurisch. You can find the pictures on social media.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.26.tex.text: Speaking of the team: our prevention and cosmetics store now has a new head, Ricco. He's already introduced a few of his favourite products on social media.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.27.tex.text: We're proving that operating theatres can indeed create a sense of wellbeing too, with our new surgical treatment room. Take a look at the video on our channels.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.28.tex.text: Of course, we also use our channels for political topics. Under the hashtag #Zähnezeigen, we're joining the campaign by the National Association of Statutory Health Insurance Dentists against the cuts to funding for dental services under German statutory health insurance. That's saving money at the cost of your health. All the information here.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.29.tex.text: Long overdue is also the amalgam ban, which the EU Commission is finally addressing. For the sake of our patients, we've been avoiding this health-risky filling for 20 years already. If you still have such a filling, you can also have it removed by us.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.3.text.text: On 20 September, we held our Botox Day. We invited you via our social media channels to have a Botox treatment carried out that day with an exclusive discount of 75 euros. Other booked beauty treatments received a 25% discount.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.30.tex.text: More, more, more! As every month, you'll also find on our channels portraits of some of our many wonderful and motivated team members, along with all the anniversaries being celebrated, the graduation of our newly qualified trainees, introductions of new colleagues, and current job vacancies. And especially for the kids, plenty more fun and educational clips have been added on TikTok.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.31.tex.text: Here's what happened on our social media channels in June

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.32.tex.text: Do you already follow KU64 – the dental specialists in Berlin and Potsdam on social media? It's the only place where you'll always find all the latest news about our social commitment and our events, as well as, of course, our team members. But most importantly: that's where you'll also be informed about all offers and discount promotions for our patients! So it's best to follow us right away on Facebook, Twitter, Instagram and TikTok.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.33.tex.text: And here's what happened on social media in June: 1 June is World Children's Day! We place great importance on a child-friendly atmosphere at our practice. So on that day, we once again presented our facilities for our young patients in detail, from the dinosaur chair and the caries cave to the aquarium and the XL children's cinema. Take a look at our children's department on YouTube.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.34.tex.text: At the moment we have many positions to fill, as KU64 is growing and wants to succeed together with its team members. That's why we posted many job adverts on social media in June. We particularly need support in the office and are looking for dental administrative assistants (ZMV). Looking for a job? Take a look.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.35.tex.text: Here's what happened on our social media channels in May

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.36.tex.text: You can also find KU64 – the dental specialists in Berlin and Potsdam on social media! There you'll learn all the latest news about our team members, our social commitment and our events. Because KU64 is more than just a practice. We want you to feel comfortable with us and in our care.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.37.tex.text: We always keep you up to date on Facebook, X and Instagram. Especially for our youngest patients, we also have a TikTok channel. Alongside news about our practice, we'll also draw your attention there to all discount promotions and offers!

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.38.tex.text: And here's what happened on social media in May: It started with our charity project in South Africa. KU64, together with another practice, was awarded a prize for prevention! Our paediatric dentist Dr. Alexandra Wolf presented our aid project in South Africa in a talk at the congress of the German Society for Preventive Medicine (DGPZM), as part of the VOCO Practitioner Award. This award focuses on preventive #dentistry that is initiated and carried out solely by the practice and provides sustainable prevention. The talk was very well received by the audience, and there were many interesting questions about our project.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.39.tex.text: For our popular “Bleaching Days”, we once again had a few appointments available in May. On these days, you can restore your teeth’s natural colour at special rates. The dates are only announced via social media. All information about bleaching can be found here.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.4.text.text: There was also an award last month: our prevention manager Peggy Bofinger-Hoffmann was named Dental Hygienist of the Year. She received the award at the 8th International Congress on Prevention-Oriented Medicine, Dentistry and Dental Hygiene, presented by the Deutsche Mundgesundheitsstiftung (DMS) at Schloss Bensberg. We of course reported on the award ceremony on social media.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.40.tex.text: We reported a great deal on our social media channels about our participation in the family festival Hier & Jetzt. We were on site at the event location Alte Münze with our XXL mascot Kroko. Our paediatric dentist Jameela Haq and dental assistant Sarah Henkel provided excitement, games and fun, and gave the kids lovely gifts.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.41.tex.text: Another event we took part in was the Muddy Angels Run. With lots of videos and pictures on Instagram, we accompanied our team of 20 members at the women’s run. It involves mud and obstacles, with shared fun being the main focus.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.42.tex.text: In May, we also made the first announcements on social media about our new DSD Lounge. With the Digital Smile Design method, we can digitally visualise more extensive dental restorations in advance. This allows you to make the best decision, together with our experts, on how to optimally treat dental damage.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.43.tex.text: By the way, we don’t just take care of the beauty of your teeth – we also offer Botox treatments! There’s a discount exclusively for new customers. Our experts answered questions at the Botox Day on 30 May. You wouldn’t have missed it, thanks to the announcement on social media.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.44.tex.text: Last but not least, we also always post our current job vacancies on social media. If you’re a dental assistant looking for a new professional challenge at Germany’s largest dental practice, take a look.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.45.tex.text: Follow us today to stay informed about all our future promotions and events! You’ll find all our social media links under Press Info.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.5.text.text: There was even more to celebrate on 20 September. That's World Children's Day. Every child deserves a bright, worry-free smile and a trip to the dentist that's more fun than a birthday party! That's why we prepared take-home balloons and lots of goodies for our little champions, and invited everyone via our social media channels. But at our practice, every day is Children's Day! Our youngest patients can enjoy an XL crocodile with real teeth, an ant colony and aquarium, an XL children's cinema, a selfie box, X-Box and PlayStation consoles, touchscreen games, and an XXL waiting lounge with plenty of room for endless fun! Curious? Call us on 030-8647320 or book an appointment online for your child.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.6.text.text: But that's not all! Right after came Dental Health Day on 25 September. Of course, we shared the best tips for dental care with you on social media, from proper brushing to a healthy diet. Missed it all? No problem, we're happy to advise you in person at your next check-up. After all, the most important thing for healthy teeth is regular visits to the dentist.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.7.text.text: What happened on our social media channels in August

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.8.text.text: You should definitely follow KU64 – your dental specialists in Berlin and Potsdam – on social media! That's where we give you exclusive information about all our offers and discount promotions for patients. All the latest news about our social commitment, our events, and of course our staff, appears in your timeline as soon as it happens. So head over to Facebook, Twitter, Instagram and TikTok now.

beitrag.social-media-2023.bloecke.9.text.text: Here's what happened on our social media in August:

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.1.text.text: A wonderful and successful year has come to an end for KU64! We would like to thank all our patients most sincerely. Special thanks go to our fantastic team. Here is a look back at the December highlights on our social media channels.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.11.tex.text: Speaking of Christmas: if you don't just love decorating your home for the festive season but are also as keen on tooth jewellery as we are, we now have something special for you. From now on, KU64 offers sparkling highlights for your smile – professional, individual and stylish! Our special tooth jewellery days are the new trend, much like our popular Bleaching Days and Beauty Days.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.12.tex.text: Our glitter queen, orthodontic dental assistant Evgenia, is a true expert in this field. She and her team offer excellent advice and take the time to understand your wishes! This naturally includes professional application: tooth jewellery by an expert – safe and gentle! Our tip: a professional dental cleaning before the application makes both your teeth and the jewellery shine even more.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.13.tex.text: Of course, we shared plenty of information about our tooth jewellery days on our social media channels. If you really did miss it, take a look at the demo video on TikTok. And it's a great idea to keep in mind for next Christmas as a gift for your loved ones!

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.15.tex.text: It would certainly have been worth staying up to date in December too. Alongside the highlights, there was, as always, much more to discover – from anniversaries and new team members to our popular Beauty Days and our new image video. If you don't want to miss anything from now on, follow KU64 – your dental specialists in Berlin and Potsdam – on social media today. As a subscriber, you'll regularly receive exclusive information about our current offers, discount campaigns and events. beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.16.tex.text: What happened on our social media channels in November

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.17.tex.text: Probably the darkest month of the year already brought us plenty of bright moments, before the city lit up with festive lights and the days finally began to grow longer again. If you already followed us on social media, you'd have known all about it. Here are the highlights of our social media activity from November.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.18.tex.text: A charity project with a stopover in India

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.19.tex.text: We start with a heart-warming story: always on the move and high above the clouds as a flight attendant for Lufthansa, our paediatric dentist Dr Alexandra Wolf doesn't just lead an exciting double life with two remarkable professions. She also gets involved with great commitment in our charity work. Once a year, she flies to South Africa with a 10-strong KU64 team to provide dental care to an entire primary school.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.20.tex.text: Alexandra also gets involved in social projects whenever she can, beyond this annual trip. This was the case during a longer stopover recently in India, where she enthusiastically visited children's facilities. There, she raised awareness, gave tooth-brushing lessons and handed out toothbrushes, toothpaste and cups. She was supported in this by BIG SMILE e.V. and our loyal partners, this time in particular by toothpaste manufacturer Elmex! Thank you so much, dear Alexandra, for your tireless commitment.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.21.tex.text: You missed all the wonderful photos and videos from the campaign on social media. You can read all about our charity project here.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.22.tex.text: Gentle dental cleaning with Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT)

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.23.tex.text: One of our secrets to success is the continuous training of our staff. In our own beautiful training rooms, our teams regularly meet leading experts in dentistry. The goal: to stay up to date at all times, so we can offer you the best, most innovative and most effective care. This was also the case at the end of November: our prophylaxis and dental hygiene staff took part in in-depth training on the latest findings in periodontal research. You can see this for yourself, quite literally, on social media.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.24.tex.text: Of course, you can also read all the latest scientific findings yourself. Find out why our Guided Biofilm Therapy prophylaxis (GBT) is better than conventional dental cleaning, and it's a good idea to book a check-up appointment straight away.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.25.tex.text: Dentures without impressions or waiting time

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.3.text.text: December started with good news for dental health. We informed you in detail that, from 1 January 2025, the use of amalgam for dental fillings will be banned across the EU. We have known for a long time that amalgam is harmful, and we stopped using it in our practice almost 20 years ago! What was once criticised is now being celebrated as the right decision.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.4.text.text: If you still have amalgam fillings, we can remove them safely using our special triple protection method, freeing you from harmful mercury. Throughout the treatment, we protect you from the dangerous vapours and particles that can be released during removal. Your new filling is made from high-quality composite resin, which matches your natural tooth colour for a bright smile and is completely safe for your health. It's a good idea to book an appointment soon.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.5.text.text: A dentist between the treatment chair and the aircraft

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.51.tex.text: As you can see, it was an eventful autumn and you missed quite a bit. If you want to stay up to date from now on, simply follow KU64 – your dental specialists in Berlin and Potsdam – on social media. There, our subscribers regularly receive exclusive information about our current offers, discount campaigns and events. You can find us on Facebook, X, Instagram, Youtube, TikTok and Spotify.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.52.tex.text: What happened on our social media channels in August

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.53.tex.text: A summer lull? Certainly not at KU64 – your dental specialists in Berlin and Potsdam. In fact, we started the month of August by warmly welcoming our new trainees. Our trainee coordinators Dominik Demski, Dino Wendt and Anja Baranowsky, together with KU64 head Dr Stephan Ziegler, made sure our six newcomers had a really enjoyable start. After an exciting tour through our unusual, 3-storey practice in Berlin, things got going straight away: a warm welcome from the boss himself, and off into the adventure! After that, the new trainees dived into an action-packed crash course taking them on a playful journey through the world of dental assisting. Don't worry, it's guaranteed not to be boring here – learning with a fun factor is our motto. No wonder that almost all trained dental assistants stay with us afterwards. Just take a look at the beaming faces on social media. Feeling inspired too? Then click here for our training campaign 'We train'!

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.54.tex.text: Behind the scenes, we were busy too: our latest Youtube video about the charity project in South Africa is finally finished. As all our subscribers know, we have been travelling to South Africa together with the non-profit organisation BIG SMILE E.V. every year since 2009 to provide dental care for around 200 children there. In 2024, we were on site again, removing tooth decay, providing prevention and education, and giving the children a beaming smile. Former professional boxer and Big Smile e.V. ambassador Axel Schulz joined us this year. He supported us in the media and, together with the kids, initiated sports training sessions to boost their confidence. Here are some impressions of what it was like on site, in the video.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.55.tex.text: If you already followed us on social media, you would know that we regularly provide important, up-to-date information on health topics too. In August, our new information page on chalky teeth was completed. This enamel defect, with demineralised patches, affects many children and requires particular attention and treatment. Our caring paediatric dentists in Berlin-Charlottenburg know this subject inside out and are happy to advise you and your children. Since you missed the post about it as a non-subscriber, here's the direct link with all the information on the causes and treatment options for chalky teeth.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.56.tex.text: Without a social media subscription, you also missed Tooth Fairy Day. That's a shame, isn't it? On 22 August, the magical ritual is celebrated that has made small (and not-so-small) hearts skip a beat since it was invented in the 1980s: when a milk tooth falls out, it goes under the pillow or into a glass by the bed. During the night, the tooth fairy sneaks into the room and swaps the tooth for a little surprise! Anyone who happens to lose a tooth on Tooth Fairy Day can be especially pleased – perhaps the tooth fairy brings an extra-large surprise that day?

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.57.tex.text: As a follower, you would also already know how sought-after our experts are in the media. This month, for example, our dentist Samaneh Salehipour was a guest on RTL Punkt 12. The internet is full of beauty gadgets promising us dazzling white, tartar-free teeth. But do they really deliver? In the programme, Samaneh tested several of these 'miracle products'. Spoiler: one of them was immediately dismissed by our expert – a dangerous tartar remover. 'You need three years of training to use a device like that,' Samaneh points out on RTL. So, don't trust every hype! Since you missed this important information on social media, here's the link to the TV segment.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.58.tex.text: There was also coverage of our wonderful paediatric and adolescent dentist and Lufthansa flight attendant Dr Alexandra Wolf. She is deeply committed to our beloved project in South Africa. An interview with her was published in the renowned 'PJ – Prophylaxe Journal – Parodontologie und präventive Zahnheilkunde', which you can read as an e-paper.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.59.tex.text: Besides that, you missed further important health information, everything about pain-free preventive care, our summer opening hours on the usual seven days a week, our back-to-school campaign, and quite a few other things on our channels. So, as always, an important reminder to close: if you want to stay up to date at all times, follow KU64 – your dental specialists in Berlin and Potsdam – on social media right away. There, our subscribers regularly receive exclusive information about our current offers, discount campaigns and events for KU64 patients. So subscribe to us now! You can find us on Facebook, X, Instagram, Youtube, TikTok and Spotify.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.6.text.text: Our flying paediatric dentist Dr Alexandra Wolf regularly appears in the media. In December, she was a guest on the @Mund.auf.Podcast. There, she spoke about how she structures her everyday life between the treatment chair and the aircraft, why she chose this unique way of life, and what she brings from the aircraft cabin into the practice. Let yourself be inspired by Alexandra's remarkable path! For anyone who missed the podcast on our social media channels, here is the link again.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.60.tex.text: What happened on our social media channels in July

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.61.tex.text: Midsummer in Germany, isn't it lovely! And of course July was also the perfect month for our Summer Party 2024. On 12 July, we celebrated at our practice on Ku'damm with 200 staff members from three locations. The highlight of the evening was the exciting news about our next practice trip. Because to mark our 20th anniversary next year, our entire team will be going on a Mediterranean cruise. For the best staff in the world, we spare no expense. The mood at the summer party was correspondingly cheerful, as documented with plenty of photos and videos on our social media channels. Would you like to become part of this fantastic team too, as a trainee or a qualified professional? Then apply in under 60 seconds, and if all goes well, you might even join us on the cruise!

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.62.tex.text: That we do a great deal for our staff, and especially for our young talent, is shown not only by the many young people we successfully launch into working life. Most trainees are happy to stay with us afterwards, which makes us very proud. Just recently, five of them passed their exams as dental assistants and are now part of the team. You'll find their beaming faces and impressions from the spontaneous meal we invited them to on our social media channels, of course.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.63.tex.text: We're currently featured on this very topic in the IHK magazine 'Position'. Our wonderful trainee coordinator Lulu Bürger gave a great interview about our exciting training programme, explaining what role smartphone use plays in our training. Our charming dental assistants Sarah and Anja were photographed exclusively for us and shine not only on the cover, but across several pages of the magazine. You could have already read about this on social media too, but you can also click straight through to the magazine.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.64.tex.text: In fact, we're well represented in magazines this month: our all-rounder Dominik, who worked his way up from trainee to chief assistant, practice manager and training director, chats in an interview with BLU Magazine about the exciting training on offer at our modern KU64 dental practices – with locations on Ku'damm, Hausvogteiplatz and in Potsdam. And none other than our head, Dr Stephan Ziegler, gave an interview to CGM Magazine, including a photoshoot at our practice! More information on our social media channels.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.65.tex.text: Otherwise, quite a lot happened that you missed on social media. Beyond our summer party, we also got fully into the summer spirit. With the help of delicious premium ice cream from the Vanille & Marille manufactory, our reception manager Tanya turned our practice into a gelateria – to the great delight of our patients and staff alike. Feel free to drop by and enjoy a refreshing treat in the summer heat – because August is going to be even hotter! In case you're reading this too late: quickly subscribe to our social media channels, so you'll know straight away next time we run such a great promotion.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.66.tex.text: By the way: have you heard of Digital Smile Design yet? As a follower of our social media channels, you would certainly already know about it thanks to our information and videos on the subject. A beautiful smile isn't a dream – we create them at KU64 every day. Thanks to our sophisticated concept with over 30 dental specialists under one roof, we can achieve wonderful, very natural new smiles that are individual and unique. With the innovative Digital Smile Design (DSD) method, teeth are individually developed and simulated on the computer, then produced in our state-of-the-art dental laboratory. Excellent aesthetic results guaranteed! Using our functional analysis, we check, for example, how the jaw is positioned, how the jaw joints move and how the teeth relate to one another. We can then recommend measures and treatments for the best possible outcome. After all, patients shouldn't just have beautifully radiant teeth – they should also be able to chew well with them! All information and appointment booking.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.67.tex.text: And finally, as always, an important reminder: if you want to stay up to date at all times, follow KU64 – your dental specialists in Berlin and Potsdam – on social media right away. There, you'll regularly receive exclusive information about current offers, discount campaigns and events for our patients. So subscribe to us now! You can currently find us on Facebook, X, Instagram, Youtube, TikTok and Spotify.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.68.tex.text: What happened on our social media channels in June

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.69.tex.text: The Olympiastadion once again became the ultimate football temple of Europe in June and July! Six Euro matches took place here, including the round of 16, the quarter-final, and finally the final itself on 14 July. As a social media follower, you would already have known: we were chosen to provide dental care for the players in Berlin – an incredibly great honour for our team. We live team sport at the highest level and are proud to bring this experience into our work. Our dentists officially supported the players of the Berlin matches, ready to help whenever toothache or dental accidents occurred – around the clock, 7 days a week! Fortunately, nothing too serious happened. And by the way, you wouldn't have had to miss a match for a dental appointment either: we broadcast all the Euro matches live in our waiting lounge.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.70.tex.text: Such a shame! What you missed, though, was our Bleaching Day on 29.6. As a social media follower, you would have found out in time and could have got the complete package for 340 instead of 600 Euro. As always, we keep you up to date there on our promotions and special offers. So hit that subscribe button right away, so you can join in next time.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.71.tex.text: Of course, we don't just look after football stars – we also care for our smallest superstars with the greatest dedication: we're proud to introduce our brand-new certificate of bravery for our courageous young patients! From now on, all our youngest heroes will receive a certificate as a reward for their courage and bravery during their dental visit. You could have learnt about this on our social media channels. But of course, you can also find it on our children's dentistry page. And while you're there, why not book an appointment for your child straight away.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.72.tex.text: We'd be nothing without our team, and as regular readers know, we put a lot of effort into this. We're delighted to now officially work with role models as part of our staff development. Our practice manager Petros Prontis gave an interview to the Zahnärztliche Mitteilungen about how we specifically reach male applicants for dental nurse training – a profession typically chosen by women. We can now proudly present our male trainees as role models. How did this come about? What do we do as an employer to support it? And why do we especially want more men in the new training year starting in August? You can read all about it in the interview – and you'd have already seen it in your timeline if you were following us.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.73.tex.text: On social media, we regularly introduce some of our wonderful team members. Take Kim, for example, who started with us as a dental nurse and, through great dedication, continued her training. She's now close to qualifying as a dental hygiene assistant and is available for hygiene appointments from now on. So best book quickly. Are you aiming higher and want to become a hygiene assistant yourself? Then we'd love to meet you. Send us your CV at bewerbung@ku64.de.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.74.tex.text: Have you seen our YouTube Shorts yet? There you'll find plenty of portraits of our team members, such as Dr Alexandra Wolff, who leads a fascinating double life as a children's dentist and flight attendant. As a follower, you'd already know this, of course, since we've mentioned it several times on social media.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.75.tex.text: Finally, an important reminder as always: if you want to stay up to date, follow KU64 – your dental specialists in Berlin and Potsdam – on social media right away. There, you'll regularly get exclusive information about current offers, discount campaigns and events for our patients. So subscribe to us now! You can currently find us on Facebook, X, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and Spotify.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.76.tex.text: What happened on our social media channels in May

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.77.tex.text: A real highlight in May was the spectacular opening of Jazz Mang's exhibition – a huge success with over 300 guests! Born in South Korea, the painter has lived in Berlin since childhood. She has found her personal artistic expression in a vivid and striking visual language that creates expressive works between abstraction and figurative painting, combining contrasts, patterns and floral elements. A true feast for the eyes. The private view was made even more special by traditional Korean drummers and culinary highlights! The exhibition can be visited daily at our building on Ku'damm 64 until the end of August! You'll find photos and videos from the opening on our social media channels, of course.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.78.tex.text: Unfortunately, you've missed another round of our Botox Day if you still haven't followed us on social media: on 28 May, our hugely successful beauty event took place again, and as a follower you would have been informed straight away. But we're not that unkind, so here's a hint: the next date is already set. On 26 June, there'll be another round with a generous discount of €70 on Botox treatment and 20% off all other first-time treatments. All the details and appointments can also be found at KU64 Beauty.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.79.tex.text: As you know, we always keep you up to date on important topics around dental health and aesthetics via social media. For World Tea Day on 22 May, we discussed the causes of tooth discolouration, starting with substances like tea, red wine and tobacco. But did you know that fluoride, so important for dental health, can also cause discolouration? Of course, we won't leave you alone with this topic either. Regular professional teeth cleaning, dental check-ups and the occasional professional whitening treatment help keep your smile bright, despite tea drinking or other causes of discolouration.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.8.text.text: At the end of the month came the most wonderful time of the year – a time for reflection, joy and special moments with loved ones. At KU64, Christmas isn't just a celebration – it's an experience! With great heart and creativity, our team transformed the practice on Ku'damm into a true winter wonderland. The scent of fir and cinnamon filled the air, fairy lights created warmth, and our decorated Christmas tree left every visitor amazed. As a follower, you wouldn't have missed our lovely Christmas video with a tour through the practice. Naturally, there was also a huge KU64 Christmas party. Curious now? Simply scroll through our many posts with photos and videos on social media from the comfort of your sofa and see for yourself.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.80.tex.text: Of course, our dental practices are primarily about the medical care of our patients. However, it's also hugely important that everything runs smoothly when it comes to administration and billing for our services. That's why, at the spring workshop for the administrative assistants from all 3 KU64 branches, we explored general billing together, and in particular the guidelines for periodontitis treatment and billing, with great support from our speaker Christian López Quintero from the VABODENT Academy. As always, you'll find photos from the event on social media.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.81.tex.text: Speaking of team members: we're keen to support the next generation, and three of our male trainees were featured as role models in the Zahnärztliche Mitteilungen. We're constantly training new talent in a range of professions, so do take a look at our jobs page. Of course, you would have learnt all this on social media too, along with plenty of other information about our brilliant team, including portraits of both new and long-standing colleagues.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.82.tex.text: And finally, the important reminder once again: if you want to stay up to date from now on, follow KU64 – your dental specialists in Berlin and Potsdam – on social media right away. As you know, we regularly and exclusively inform you there about current offers, discount campaigns and events for patients. So subscribe to us on Facebook, X, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and Spotify.

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.83.tex.text: What happened on our social media channels in April

beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.84.tex.text: April once again showed why it really pays to follow our social media channels. You would have been among the first to hear about our fantastic campaign at “Potsdam tanzt in den Mai”. beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.86.tex.text: We also keep you up to date on professional topics via social media. Many trends aren't necessarily good for your dental health. beitrag.social-media-2024.bloecke.87.tex.text: In April, we also covered the most common dental disease, tooth decay, on our social media channels with information and images. In the second phase, plaque forms with yellow spots. Here, too, you can still do a lot before the tooth is irreparably damaged. Our children's dentist Dr Bahaa Youssef recommends using fluoride toothpaste, limiting sugar intake, attending regular check-ups, and not forgetting professional teeth cleaning. Best to book a consultation appointment straight away.

And of course, KU64 was right at the front again this year at the world’s largest dental trade fair in Cologne. beitrag.social-media-mai-2025.bloecke.10.text: What makes us so successful, and what our trainees can learn intensively with us: that our dental practice lives and shapes modern dentistry, day after day. These are our nine standards:

beitrag.social-media-mai-2025.bloecke.11.text: Digital power: high-tech instead of handiwork. With 3D scans, digital X-rays and CAD/CAM technology, we offer precise, fast and comfortable treatments.
People at the centre: it's not just about teeth here – it's about you. With a welcoming atmosphere, a friendly reception, hardly any waiting times and, yes: seriously good coffee.
Always up to date: our team trains regularly and brings the latest treatment methods straight to the treatment chair.
Cleanliness at clinic level: hygiene standards are our top priority. For your safety – day in, day out.
Stylish atmosphere instead of sterile coldness: who says dental practices have to be cool and clinical? Our rooms are designed so that you almost forget where you are.
Consciously sustainable: we pay attention to environmental impact – from choosing materials to our daily practice routine. Because the future matters.
Prevention rather than aftercare: for us, modern preventive care means gentle, effective and tailored to you. We do everything we can to stop problems before they start.
Safe amalgam removal: to remove old fillings, we work with a rubber dam and triple protection – for maximum safety with minimal risk. Because your health comes first.
Flexibility for your life: whether you're an early riser or a weekend visitor, we're here for you 7 days a week – no emergency dental service stress required. Find all the details on Instagram.

beitrag.west-coast-kids-2026-hilfsprojek.text: From 7 to 14 February 2026, we once again travelled to South Africa as part of our West Coast Kids aid project, this time with a ten-person team, about 150 kilometres north of Cape Town. In the remote community of Paternoster on

From 7 to 14 February 2026, we were once again in South Africa with a ten-person team as part of our West Coast Kids charity project, around 150 kilometres north of Cape Town. In the remote community of Paternoster on the West Coast, we provided voluntary dental treatment to 127 primary school children aged five to twelve – for the 14th time already.

Drawing on our experience from previous years, the journey began with a familiar sense of tension: what would await us this year? Would we again be caught out by a power cut? Did all the children have written permission from their parents for treatment? These questions accompanied our team – Dr Stephan Ziegler, dentist Juliane Kottenhagen, the two paediatric dentists Inke Supantia and Dr Erny Grundmann, dental hygienist Michaela Kunkel, preventive care assistant Nicole Dickhoff-Kranz, assistant and receptionist Sarah Henkel, and the three dental nurses Lysann Kosiol, Huyen Nguyen-Dieu and Nico Schillings – all the way until arrival.

We paid particular attention to visible damage in the front teeth, such as chipped incisors after falls, dark areas of decay, or clearly worn tooth edges that are immediately noticeable when a child smiles. We know how quickly children can be teased or excluded because of this. Between treatments, there was always time for playing, talking and distraction. At the end, every child was sent off with a group hug. One especially memorable moment was our visit to the neighbouring kindergarten: due to legal requirements, we were not yet able to treat the youngest children, but they listened attentively, tried out toothbrushes, and proudly took their toothbrushing sets home.
An emotional rollercoaster

Many other moments will probably only reveal their full significance in hindsight, since there was hardly any time to pause on site. Even though we were overwhelmed by emotions every day, we had to keep working with focus, so that none of the precious minutes were lost.

What touched us again and again was the great appreciation shown to us: the children thanked us with small handmade gifts, parents with home-baked treats, and on the street we were often greeted with great warmth.

After school, the team was also invited into the homes of some of the children and their families. An important gathering point in the community is "Tanni Anni", which provides around 100 children with a warm meal every day after school. With our support, we were able to help ensure that this work can continue.
A message that reaches beyond Paternoster

At the farewell, all the pupils and teachers gathered in the schoolyard, sang and danced for the team, and presented a card signed by everyone. This shared farewell showed that our work here truly makes a difference – in people's hearts, too. Time and again, we notice that this project is about far more than just healthy teeth. Over the years, we have become familiar faces. Even though we are only here for one week a year, we accompany many of the children along part of their journey as listeners, friends and a source of comfort. In moments like these, the meaning of our commitment becomes especially clear to us, and it's this experience we would also like to share with people back in Germany:
"Helping people to help themselves is often a small gesture that costs almost nothing, but achieves a great deal when you stay committed to it over time."

For KU64, this social commitment is a way of showing gratitude and taking responsibility. 18 years ago, a patient asked the practice whether it would like to help, and took the first step. Since then, the West Coast Kids project has stood for consistent action, teamwork and solidarity. No one is paid; everything is done on a voluntary basis. The team members contribute their expertise and their time.

This mission is also made possible thanks to the support of partners and sponsors, including Simone Jacke, who came up with the idea and leads the charity organisation of accommodation for West Coast Kids, dental hygienist Karen Paulse, who has supported the project on the ground since day one, Sven Riegel from Druck & Stick Berlin for the team shirts, Henry Schein Dental for 200 toothbrushes and toothpastes, Condor for their extra service, and our factoring partner BFS Health Finance GmbH.

But even before we had unloaded the first box, the nervousness gave way to a familiar feeling. The loud, joyful welcome from the children, along with the teachers and volunteers we've come to know as friends, quickly pushed our initial worries into the background. It was also very moving to see many of the children again whom we have supported for years.

The fact that other doctors, dentists and private individuals are now also getting involved in further charity projects in Paternoster confirms that this is the right path. And, quite by the way, this year showed that not every worry comes true – the power, thankfully, stayed on throughout.
Last updated on 17.02.2026

Dentist and co-founder of the project
Profile of Juliane Kottenhagen
"Some of our former patients now attend secondary schools in other towns. Others are studying in Cape Town and made a special trip to come and greet the team."
A dental practice in the community hall

After our arrival in Paternoster, there was little time to settle in, in the usual sense. Within a few hours, the church community hall next to the primary school was transformed into a makeshift but well-functioning dental practice. As in previous years, we borrowed the treatment chairs from a disused practice in a nearby town. Instruments, filling materials, suture material and even two suitcase-sized portable suction units were brought over from Germany. Thanks to the detailed checklists from previous missions, every step ran smoothly. The routines were well rehearsed, so within five treatment days we were able to see all 127 children from the primary school.
Light-bulb moments: how brushing teeth builds confidence

"This year, we placed even greater focus on prevention – to help protect against tooth decay and show the children how they can keep their own teeth healthy, using educational videos and presentations in Afrikaans," says Dr Stephan Ziegler, who gave several educational talks. It became clear within the first few days just how necessary this focus is: sugar is part of everyday life for many children, sweet drinks are available at all times, and the effects are clearly visible on their teeth.

Alongside the improvised dental practice, we also set up a small cinema in the community hall. Before going to the treatment chair, the children would sit down there and watch a film about nutrition, sugar traps and dental care. The content sparked many light-bulb moments and surprisingly open questions. Afterwards, everyone practised together: brushing teeth with concentration, curiosity and a lot of motivation. Some children wanted to get everything right straight away, others needed time and encouragement. All the more wonderful were the moments when anxious children came back on their own later, proud to show what they had learned.

"This year we carried out around 200 fillings. In previous missions, it was often 240 or more. At the same time, we notice that the fillings today are considerably smaller. This shows just how much prevention and education can achieve."
West Coast Kids 2026: KU64 working towards carefree children's smiles
