beschwerde.gelbe-zaehne.einstieg.0.text.text: [ What to do about tooth discolouration? ]

beschwerde.gelbe-zaehne.einstieg.1.text.text: A smile opens doors. But when teeth appear yellow, it’s often held back. In everyday life, this means your laugh sounds muted, speaking feels more cautious, and encounters lose their ease. What should express joy turns into insecurity instead. The causes of yellow teeth are varied and not always down to oral hygiene alone. At KU64 Berlin, we don’t leave you alone with this. We explain where the discolouration comes from and offer suitable treatments to bring the sparkle back to your smile.

beschwerde.gelbe-zaehne.faq.0.antwort.text:
Many people are puzzled when their teeth look yellow despite thorough brushing. But brushing alone isn't always enough for yellow teeth. The natural thickness of the tooth enamel plays an important role: if it's thinner, the yellowish dentine underneath shows through more strongly. Internal staining caused by certain medications, such as antibiotics, or by illness, also can't be removed with a toothbrush.
Diet and stimulants have an additional effect: coffee, tea, red wine, nicotine or fizzy drinks leave behind pigments that build up even with regular brushing.
Tip: Avoid home remedies such as baking soda or lemon juice for tooth discolouration. They put unnecessary strain on your teeth and mouth. At our dental practice, we instead recommend a professional clean as a foundation, to remove yellow deposits and let your natural tooth colour shine through again. This is also suitable for children from the age of twelve.

beschwerde.gelbe-zaehne.faq.0.frage.text: Why do I have yellow teeth despite brushing?

beschwerde.gelbe-zaehne.faq.1.antwort.text: Many parents are alarmed when their child's new teeth suddenly appear more yellow, even though the child brushes regularly and correctly. The reason: children's baby teeth naturally appear very white, while permanent teeth have a thicker layer of dentine, which is more yellowish and shows through more. Compared side by side, permanent teeth therefore look darker. This colour difference in children's teeth is completely normal and not a sign of poor dental care. Parents should still take a close look inside the mouth while brushing: if spots or discolouration become visible in children, a visit to the dentist is a good idea to identify the cause early.

beschwerde.gelbe-zaehne.faq.1.frage.text: Why does my child have yellow teeth despite brushing?

beschwerde.gelbe-zaehne.faq.2.antwort.text: Very yellow teeth usually can't be whitened by brushing or home remedies alone. A professional clean removes surface staining, but for more noticeable whitening, dentist-performed bleaching is the most effective and safest method. If discolouration is particularly severe or permanent, we recommend veneers. They offer a long-term aesthetic solution for evenly white teeth.

beschwerde.gelbe-zaehne.faq.2.frage.text: How can I make very yellow teeth properly white again?

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.0..text: Tooth decay develops when bacteria convert sugar into acids that attack the tooth enamel. If plaque isn't removed regularly, a hole in the tooth can develop.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.1..text: In the early stages, tooth decay often shows up as white or brown spots on the tooth. Later on, sensitivity to cold or sweet foods, pain or visible damage may follow.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.10.text: Root decay often occurs where the tooth roots are exposed, especially in older age or when the gums recede. The sensitive tooth root is exposed there, unprotected by hard enamel, and is therefore attacked more quickly by bacteria and acids.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.11.text: This form mainly affects the chewing surfaces of the back teeth. Food residue and bacteria collect in the small grooves (fissures), especially when cleaning is difficult.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.12.text: This affects the smooth tooth surfaces and usually develops from persistent plaque that is not removed regularly.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.13.text: Tooth decay develops gradually – from barely visible changes in the enamel to deep defects that can affect the interior of the tooth. The earlier the process is detected, the easier it is to preserve the tooth. The individual stages show how what initially seems like harmless deposits can gradually turn into serious damage.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.14.text: In this early stage, the enamel is already demineralised in some areas, though there is not yet a real hole. Dull, white or slightly brownish spots appear on the tooth surface. If addressed early, the damage at this stage can still be reversed through fluoride treatment and targeted mineral supply.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.15.text: Visible defects now form in the enamel, where food particles and bacteria easily settle. The decay spreads into the underlying dentine, which speeds up the deterioration of the tooth. Brownish discolouration is often visible. The damage is now permanent and requires a filling.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.16.text: The decay has fully reached the dentine. Since this tissue contains fine nerve fibres, the first pain and sensitivity often appear at this stage. The affected areas look dark brown to black, and unpleasant breath may develop. Dental treatment is essential at this point.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.17.text: In the final stage, the decay has reached the tooth pulp, which contains nerves and blood vessels. This leads to severe, throbbing pain and often inflammation of the tooth root. An abscess can form, causing swelling and fever. Immediate dental treatment – usually root canal treatment – is now essential to prevent complications and, if possible, save the tooth.
4. Decay in the tooth pulp – abscess formation

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.18.text: Tooth decay often develops unnoticed. At first it damages the tooth without causing pain, but over time the signs become clearer. If these early warning signs are ignored, the decay can spread down to the tooth root and cause inflammation. Early detection is therefore essential to avoid further damage and preserve the tooth.
How can I recognise tooth decay?

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.19.text: White, yellowish or brown spots on the tooth surface
Sensitivity to hot, cold or sweet food and drink
Pain when chewing or when pressure is applied to the tooth
Visible holes or rough patches on the tooth
Bad breath or an unpleasant taste in the mouth

Do you notice one or more of these symptoms and suspect tooth decay? Then book an appointment at our practice today. We offer professional diagnosis and treatment for tooth decay and help you achieve a healthy, confident smile.
Typical symptoms of tooth decay at a glance:

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.2..text: Early stages can often be stopped without drilling, through targeted fluoride treatment and good dental care. For more advanced decay, fillings or inlays help. Regular brushing, fluoride toothpaste and check-ups with the dentist prevent new damage.
What you can do about tooth decay

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.20.text: Thanks to state-of-the-art methods and an experienced team, our practice offers you first-class care. If tooth decay is suspected, the dentist first examines the teeth, gums and oral mucosa. We check hidden areas between the teeth with a small mirror to detect any decay. If a hole has already formed, the dentist uses a fine probe to check how deep it is. This makes it possible to determine which stage of decay is present.

Alongside this classic approach, modern methods are now also available, such as electrical resistance measurement. A hand-held electrode is used to check whether altered readings point to tooth decay. Another way to diagnose tooth decay is the so-called fluorescence method. This uses the fluorescent properties of the enamel to make the areas affected by decay visible.
Diagnosis: how is tooth decay detected?

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.21.text: Many people only visit the dentist once they have toothache or notice dark spots on their teeth themselves. Most are unaware that a caries risk assessment can be carried out at the dental practice as part of preventive care, helping to protect the teeth from decay and keep them healthy in the long term. The test is very simple, completely painless, quick, and reliably warns of tooth decay.

The dentists at KU64 Berlin take a saliva sample from you. Using this sample, our specialists can identify acid-producing bacteria and Streptococcus mutans (lactobacilli) and give you an assessment of how much your teeth are at risk from harmful bacteria. Old or damaged fillings in the mouth increase this risk. You are also at higher risk from harmful bacteria if plaque has built up due to insufficient oral hygiene. Plaque provides an ideal breeding ground for bacteria.

If the caries risk assessment shows that you are at risk, we can give you the right guidance. This helps you avoid extensive and costly procedures. We are happy to offer you a few simple tips for oral hygiene and diet. We also recommend using a tongue cleaner and an ultrasonic toothbrush to improve your daily oral care routine. Both of these care products have shown very good results, particularly in removing stubborn, problematic plaque. Take precautions in good time and prevent the worst from happening.
Assessing your risk of tooth decay

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.22.text: In children, early detection of tooth decay is especially important so that teeth stay healthy for as long as possible. Children's teeth have thinner enamel than adult teeth and are therefore more vulnerable to bacteria and acids. This means tooth decay can develop much faster here, even with regular brushing. It's all the more important that children have positive experiences at the dentist – without fear, pain or stress. The experienced paediatric dentists at KU64 take their time, explain each step in a child-friendly way and create a relaxed atmosphere.

Milk teeth also deserve particular attention: they don't just hold the place for permanent teeth but also play an important role in speech development and chewing. Even though milk teeth eventually fall out, decay must still be treated. Otherwise, inflammation can spread to the teeth developing underneath.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.23.text: You can explain tooth decay to children in simple terms as "sugar bugs" that nibble little holes in the teeth when a child eats too many sweets and doesn't brush thoroughly. With this picture in mind, your child can easily understand why regular brushing, flossing and dentist visits are so important – they help chase the "bacteria monsters" away.
How can I explain tooth decay to my children?

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.24.text: During pregnancy, not only hormone levels change but also the composition of saliva and the oral flora. All of these factors can significantly increase the risk of tooth decay. Frequent vomiting, cravings for sweet food, or changes in oral hygiene put extra strain on the enamel. At the same time, gum inflammation (pregnancy gingivitis) can raise the risk of bacterial infections in the mouth.

Untreated tooth decay should definitely be avoided during pregnancy, as inflammation in the mouth can also affect the mother's general health and the unborn child. Regular, gentle dental check-ups, fluoride toothpaste, a balanced diet and thorough dental care are therefore especially important. Ideally, a dental examination should take place early in the pregnancy so that risks can be identified and addressed in good time.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.25.text: If the condition is still at an early stage, the affected areas can recover through plaque removal, fluoride application and regular brushing. The more enamel has already been destroyed, the more likely it is that your dentist will need to remove the decay.

If left untreated, tooth decay can lead to inflammation, abscesses or pus formation at the root of the tooth. In severe cases, bacteria can even spread into the sinus or facial areas. Headaches and tension are also possible signs of advanced inflammation.
Can tooth decay heal on its own?

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.26.text: Treatment for tooth decay depends on the extent of the damage and the area affected. The goal is to remove the damaged tissue, preserve the tooth and restore its natural function. Modern dentistry offers a range of gentle and effective methods, from mild fluoride treatment to complex root canal therapy.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.27.text: Early stage: Beginning decay can usually be stopped without drilling, through targeted fluoride treatment or resin infiltration.
Advanced decay: The dentist removes the damaged tooth substance. A filling made of composite, ceramic or resin material is then placed.
Deeper damage: If the decay has already reached the pulp, root canal treatment is needed to save the tooth and clear the inflammation.
Severely damaged teeth: If the tooth can no longer be saved, it is replaced – for example with a crown, bridge or implant.

Thanks to modern methods, treating tooth decay is usually pain-free and preserves as much of the tooth as possible. Still, regular check-ups with your KU64 dentist remain the best way to stop tooth decay before it even starts.
Typical treatment steps for tooth decay

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.28.text: Home remedies cannot cure tooth decay, as destroyed tooth substance doesn't grow back on its own. However, natural measures such as oil pulling, xylitol chewing gum or mineral supplementation through fluoride products can help stabilise the oral flora and slow down early decay processes. In very early stages – before a hole forms – enamel can partly recover through remineralisation. Even so, these methods don't replace professional treatment; they only support it.
Are there alternative treatments for tooth decay?

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.29.text: To stop tooth decay from developing in the first place, there are a number of preventive measures you can take:
How can I prevent tooth decay?

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.3..text: A brief twinge while chewing, a twinge with cold drinks, or a dark spot on a tooth: many people only notice tooth decay once it already hurts. Yet the condition can usually be treated easily if caught early. Good dental care and regular check-ups are key to keeping your teeth healthy in the long term. Do you suspect tooth decay, or would you simply like to be on the safe side? Book an appointment at KU64 now for a thorough examination and timely treatment.
When a twinge in the tooth becomes a real problem

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.30.text: To help prevent tooth decay, it's important to pay attention to – and cut down on – frequent sugary meals and drinks.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.31.text: Fluoride can help prevent the demineralisation of tooth enamel. For this reason, it's worth checking that your toothpaste contains fluoride when you buy it. Other sources of fluoride include certain types of fish, seafood and tap water.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.32.text: You should visit your dental practice twice a year for a check-up so your teeth can be examined. Professional teeth cleaning can also help prevent tooth decay. So it's a good idea to book your next preventive appointment at KU64 today.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.33.text: Regular dental care should include thorough brushing at least twice a day for around three minutes. It's also worth using dental floss or interdental brushes to clean between the teeth. Using a mouthwash afterwards can help prevent the build-up of plaque.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.34.text: As the body's natural defence against tooth decay, saliva plays an important role in preventing cavities. It neutralises acids and keeps supplying the enamel with minerals. A good flow of saliva rinses bacteria from the tooth surface and reduces the risk of decay. Chewing sugar-free gum and drinking plenty of fluids can help increase saliva flow.

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.35.text: Recognise typical symptoms and suspect you have tooth decay? Then you're in good hands at KU64 Berlin. Our experienced team supports you with the most modern diagnostic and treatment methods – tailored to you, gentle and effective. Whether it's a filling, dentures, root canal treatment, professional teeth cleaning, treatment of tooth decay or preventive care: we offer comprehensive services and information on everything to do with healthy, beautiful teeth. We place particular importance on painless, comfortable treatment, so you feel well looked after at all times.
Professional treatment of tooth decay at KU64

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.37.text: Would you like to find out more about everyday life in our practice and our services? A look behind the scenes: KU64 on social media

beschwerde.karies-symptome.abschnitte.38.text: Would you like to know what experiences others have had with KU64? On review platforms such as Google and Jameda, you'll find numerous reviews of our practices in Berlin and Potsdam.
