beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.2.b.text: Tooth misalignments can take many different forms and lead to a range of issues and risks. The dentists at KU64 Berlin have a great deal of experience in straightening misaligned teeth and recommend orthodontic treatment for the following types of tooth and jaw misalignment:

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.2.t.text: Tooth misalignment – one problem, many forms

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.3.b.text: Only around 5 to 10% of the world's population have an underbite. This is when the lower front teeth sit in front of the upper front teeth when biting down. It's often referred to as a reverse overbite. This misalignment either arises due to genetic predisposition or as a result of early childhood habits such as tongue thrusting, dummy use or thumb-sucking.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.4.b.text: When there isn't enough room in the jaw, the teeth end up too close together – this is known as crowding. As a result, teeth either fail to fully emerge or end up rotated and sitting at an angle. Since it's then difficult to reach these teeth with a toothbrush, cleaning becomes harder, which can increase the risk of tooth decay.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.5.b.text: These misalignments can be caused either by teeth that are smaller than average or by too much space in the dental arches. A distinction is made between false and true diastema. While true diastema is hereditary, false diastema usually occurs when teeth come through at different times.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.6.b.text: With an overbite, the upper jaw is too large in relation to the lower jaw, causing it to protrude. This means the gap between the upper and lower front teeth is too large. If the problem lies at tooth level, the axes of the front teeth aren't aligned correctly, whereas if the problem lies at jaw level, the entire lower jaw is set back, resulting in an overbite even when the teeth themselves are correctly positioned.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.7.b.text: This is the most common tooth misalignment among adults, where the front or side teeth don't meet properly when biting down. There's also a small or sometimes noticeable gap between them. Alongside difficulties with chewing or biting, this misalignment can also cause speech problems.

Whatever misalignment you're dealing with, you're in good hands at KU64. We offer tailored treatment methods to correct tooth and jaw misalignments and are happy to advise you. Simply arrange an appointment and discuss with our experts how you can get one step closer to the straight teeth you want. Our whole team looks forward to welcoming you to our practice in Berlin.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.8.b.text: Patients often opt to have their teeth straightened for aesthetic reasons, as misalignment can affect self-confidence in many cases. However, orthodontic treatment can also resolve bite problems and other health issues or risks.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.8.t.text: Consequences and symptoms of crooked teeth

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.9.b.text: Tooth misalignment, and crowding in particular, can make cleaning your teeth more difficult. If teeth overlap, for example, normal brushing isn't enough to remove all food residue and clean the teeth properly. As a result, there's a risk of dental conditions such as tooth decay or gum disease developing.

Using dental floss every day is essential here. We also recommend regular teeth cleaning and preventive check-ups for optimal oral hygiene. Thanks to the wide range of treatments and professional preventive care at KU64, you can keep your teeth healthy for life and help prevent tooth decay and gum inflammation. And whether it's bleeding gums, a broken tooth or toothache – our team is happy to advise you on ways to protect your teeth and give you a reason to smile.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.abschnitte.9.t.text: Crooked teeth making oral hygiene harder

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.beschreibung.text: A radiant smile & straight teeth with KU64 in Berlin-Charlottenburg. Find out more about symptoms & treatments.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.faq.0.antwort.text: At our practice, our goal is to fulfil your wish for straight teeth and bring a smile to your face. Thanks to state-of-the-art orthodontic methods, our specialists are able to correct your misalignments. Depending on how pronounced the issue is, however, comparatively minor treatments such as veneers or aligners can already achieve straight, beautiful teeth.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.faq.1.antwort.text: Not everyone is blessed with straight teeth, as there are a number of causes behind crooked teeth. Often, it's a congenital misalignment, meaning the cause is genetic. A congenital tongue dysfunction can also be a possible cause, leading originally straight teeth to shift over time. In addition, gum disease and inflammation of the tooth-supporting bone can also cause teeth to keep changing well beyond childhood. Accidents, too, can shift teeth or even the jaw, resulting in a misalignment.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.faq.2.antwort.text:
Not everyone is fortunate enough to have straight, beautiful teeth for their whole life, as there are many factors that can lead to misalignment. In children, misalignment can be prevented through thorough dental care from the very first tooth. Regular check-ups at the dentist are also very important in this respect. Adjusting eating and drinking habits can help prevent misalignment as well. Constant sucking on a bottle or dummy, for example, is harmful to the teeth, and a dummy can also affect jaw development. It's advisable to wean children off the dummy by the age of two at the latest.
Adults can also help prevent misaligned teeth by having gaps in the dentition closed promptly, to stop neighbouring teeth from shifting. If you tend to grind or clench your teeth in stressful situations, it's important to use a bite splint to prevent misalignment.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.faq.3.antwort.text: Straight teeth, or correcting misalignments, support dental health. Besides aesthetic reasons, there are also health risks that can be minimised through orthodontic treatment. Speech problems caused by misalignment can be resolved this way. Of course, how effective straightening is always depends on the extent of the misalignment. At KU64, we advise you as best we can, to make the treatment as successful as possible and ensure the best possible results.

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.faq.3.frage.text: WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS OF CORRECTING MISALIGNED TEETH?

beschwerde.schiefe-zaehne.faq.4.antwort.text:
If it results in serious health problems or significant difficulty speaking or chewing, straightening the teeth is advisable. In other cases, it's usually more of an aesthetic and personal decision. Whether treatment is essential for you for health reasons can be determined during a consultation at our practice. There, we'll also inform you about the treatment options, the costs, and how the treatment proceeds.

beschwerde.schmerzempfindliche-zaehne.ab.text: Tooth sensitivity, also known as dentine hypersensitivity, refers to a painful reaction of the teeth to certain stimuli such as cold or hot drinks, sweet or sour foods, or contact from things like a toothbrush. This sensitivity occurs when the tooth enamel – the outer protective layer of the teeth – or the dentine, the tissue beneath it, becomes worn or damaged, exposing the dentine tubules. This allows stimuli to act directly on the nerve endings inside the tooth, causing a painful sensation. Sensitivity is a common dental health problem that can affect quality of life.
What exactly are sensitive teeth?

Oral health plays a crucial role in the overall wellbeing and quality of life of every person. One important aspect of oral health is, in particular, the teeth, which are of great importance not only for chewing and speaking but also for one's aesthetic appearance. Even if it isn't visible at first glance, sensitive teeth are a common and often burdensome problem.
The effects of sensitive teeth can vary widely, ranging from mild discomfort to significant limitations in quality of life. Those affected are often forced to limit or completely avoid certain foods and, in particular, cold or hot drinks, which can have a negative impact on diet and social life. In addition, sensitivity can lead to stress, anxiety and general discomfort in the mouth, which in turn can increase the risk of further dental problems.
An insight into dentine hypersensitivity: How sensitive teeth affect daily life

A number of preventive measures are essential for protecting the teeth and avoiding sensitivity. First, regular and thorough dental care is essential. This means brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste and using dental floss to remove plaque. It is also important to avoid foods and drinks that damage the teeth, particularly those high in sugar or acid.

In addition, regular dental check-ups should be part of your routine to detect and treat problems early. These preventive measures can help avoid sensitive teeth and improve overall dental health. They include professional cleanings, fluoride treatments and sealants.
Preventive measures to avoid sensitive teeth

Regular dental check-ups play a crucial role in maintaining dental health and detecting problems early. During these visits, we at KU64 carry out a thorough examination to identify signs of tooth decay, gum disease, tartar and other issues.
Early detection of problems is crucial, as it allows problems to be treated at an early stage before they worsen and lead to serious complications. This can save costs and reduce the risk of dental damage. For example, early detection of tooth decay may mean that a filling is needed instead of root canal treatment.
In addition to treating existing problems, regular dental check-ups also offer the opportunity to take preventive measures to reduce the risk of future problems. The dentist can give recommendations for improving oral hygiene, such as using fluoride toothpaste or mouthwash. In addition, the dentist may recommend special treatments such as dental sealants to reduce the risk of tooth decay in children and young people.
Regular dental check-ups and early detection of problems

Regular dental examinations are essential for diagnosing sensitive teeth and finding suitable treatment options. Treatment can involve various measures depending on the cause of the sensitivity, such as the use of special toothpastes, fluoride varnishes, dental sealants or, in some cases, even dental procedures such as root canal treatment or gum treatment.
Find out how the pain in your teeth can be relieved and receive valuable tips from our team at KU64. Our experts take the time to look after your treatment and are happy to advise you comprehensively on the topic of sensitivity.
Treating sensitive teeth & improving quality of life

Tooth erosion and the resulting breakdown of tooth enamel are significant causes of sensitive teeth. Tooth erosion occurs when acids attack the tooth enamel and gradually wear it away, resulting in very thin and sensitive enamel. This process can be worsened by consuming acidic foods and drinks, as well as by gastro-oesophageal reflux or excessive brushing. The loss of enamel can expose the underlying tooth structures, leading to pain when eating and sensitive reactions to changes in temperature.
It's essential to identify the reasons for tooth erosion and take appropriate steps to protect the enamel and maintain oral health.
Tooth erosion

Gum recession, also known as gingival recession, can expose the tooth roots and thus cause sensitive teeth. This recession of the gums can be triggered by various factors such as inadequate oral hygiene, excessive brushing and too much pressure from the toothbrush, gum disease or genetic predisposition. When the gums recede, the sensitive areas of the teeth that are normally covered by gum tissue become exposed. This can lead to pain and sensitivity, particularly when eating, drinking or brushing your teeth.
To prevent gum recession and treat exposed tooth roots, good oral hygiene is essential, as are regular dental check-ups and regular professional teeth cleaning.
Gum recession

Gum inflammation, also known as gingivitis, is likewise a common cause of sensitive teeth. This condition arises from the build-up of plaque – a sticky film of bacteria – along the gum line. Inflammation of the gums can cause redness, swelling and bleeding. Ultimately, this can cause the gums to recede and the tooth roots to become exposed. This exposed area is particularly sensitive to external stimuli such as hot, cold or sour foods and drinks, which can cause pain and discomfort.
To prevent gum inflammation and treat sensitive teeth, thorough oral hygiene is essential, including regular teeth cleaning at the dentist and the use of floss to remove plaque.
Gum inflammation

Tooth decay is one of the most common causes of sensitive teeth. This condition arises from the build-up of plaque – a sticky film of bacteria – on the tooth surface, which produces acids that attack the enamel and gradually break it down. If left untreated, it can penetrate deeper into the tooth and damage the underlying dentine, the sensitive tissue surrounding the tooth's nerves. This can lead to toothache and increased sensitivity to hot, cold or sweet foods.

Good oral hygiene is essential to prevent tooth decay and treat sensitive teeth. This includes brushing regularly, using toothpaste or other products containing fluoride, and regular dental check-ups to monitor and treat carious lesions.
Tooth decay

Misaligned teeth can also lead to sensitive teeth, particularly when they cause excessive pressure or wear on certain teeth. If the teeth do not align correctly, this can result in uneven pressure across the teeth, which can overload certain areas and ultimately lead to tooth pain. In addition, misaligned teeth can make it harder to clean the teeth properly, increasing the risk of tooth decay and gum disease, which can also contribute to tooth pain. Orthodontic treatment to correct misaligned teeth can not only improve the appearance of the teeth, but also help protect them and reduce sensitivity.
Misaligned teeth

The symptoms of sensitive teeth can affect quality of life and should be taken seriously, as they may indicate dental disease. If you regularly experience this kind of pain, it is important to see a dentist to determine the cause and discuss suitable treatment options. Sensitive teeth can be relieved through various treatment methods.

Treatment for sensitive teeth can begin with certain products, such as special toothpaste and mouthwash. Desensitising toothpastes contain ingredients such as potassium nitrate or strontium chloride, which can help block the nerve endings in the enamel and reduce sensitivity. Mouthwashes containing fluoride can also help strengthen the enamel and reduce sensitivity by protecting the teeth from acid attacks. It is important to use these products regularly to maximise their effectiveness. They can be used as part of a comprehensive oral hygiene routine to maintain dental health.

Sensitive teeth can also be treated with professional cleanings and other treatments. Regular professional cleaning removes plaque and tartar, which often contribute to tooth sensitivity. In addition, special dental treatments such as fluoride varnish or desensitising agents can be applied to the teeth to reduce sensitivity. These measures help strengthen the enamel and reduce the irritability of the tooth nerves. It is important to attend regular dental check-ups to determine the best treatment options for your specific situation.

Fluoride treatments and sealants can also serve as a treatment method. Fluoride treatments strengthen the enamel and make it more resistant to acid attacks, which can help reduce sensitivity. Dental sealants are thin plastic coatings applied to the teeth that can protect them from decay and external influences. By sealing the tooth surface, they can also help reduce sensitivity. These treatment options should be discussed with a dentist to determine the best approach for your individual case.

Dental procedures such as fillings or root canal treatment are often effective options for treating sensitive teeth. In the case of tooth decay, a filling can repair the damaged tooth and reduce sensitivity. If the sensitivity is caused by an infection of the tooth nerve, root canal treatment may be necessary to eliminate the infection and preserve the tooth. These procedures aim to eliminate the cause of the pain and restore dental health, providing long-term relief. It is important to see a dentist early on to discuss the best treatment options and prevent further damage.
Treatment options for sensitive teeth

If you suffer from sensitive teeth, it is important to seek professional help from a dentist. A dentist can determine the cause of the sensitivity and recommend the appropriate treatment to relieve your symptoms. Do not hesitate to make an appointment to improve your dental health and smile pain-free again. Our team is happy to help you with any symptoms relating to your dental health. Get in touch with us today.
Treating sensitive teeth at KU64

beschwerde.schmerzempfindliche-zaehne.fa.text: In many cases, tooth sensitivity can be successfully treated or reduced. However, it is important to identify the underlying cause and take appropriate measures to achieve long-term results.
Can tooth sensitivity be treated permanently?

Yes, certain foods and drinks can increase tooth sensitivity and should therefore be avoided or reduced. These include acidic foods such as citrus fruits, sour sweets and sour juices, as they can attack the enamel and make the teeth more sensitive. Similarly, hot drinks such as coffee or tea and cold drinks such as water or soft drinks with ice cubes can cause pain in sensitive teeth. Sugary foods and drinks can also be problematic, as they can cause tooth decay, which increases tooth sensitivity. It is advisable to maintain a balanced diet and reduce the consumption of acidic, hot, cold and sugary foods and drinks in order to reduce tooth sensitivity.
Are there certain foods or drinks I should avoid to reduce the sensitivity of my teeth?

Yes, sensitive teeth can be a sign of dental problems that require treatment. The most common causes of sensitive teeth include receding gums, tooth decay, periodontitis, worn enamel, gum inflammation and misaligned teeth. These problems can lead to exposure of the tooth roots, causing pain and sensitivity. It is important to have the cause of the pain determined by a dentist in order to receive appropriate treatment and prevent further damage. Get in touch with our team at KU64.
Can sensitive teeth be a sign of underlying dental problems that need treatment?

Fluoride treatments play an important role in treating sensitive teeth, as fluoride helps strengthen and harden the enamel. This can help reduce tooth sensitivity and make the teeth more resistant to triggers that cause pain. Fluoride can also help remineralise the enamel and combat early signs of tooth decay, which can lead to tooth pain. Your dentist may recommend using fluoride in the form of special toothpastes, mouthwashes or a professional treatment to treat and protect your sensitive teeth.
What role do fluoride treatments play in treating sensitive teeth?

Teeth grinding, also known as bruxism, can increase tooth sensitivity, as it can wear down the tooth enamel. This can lead to exposed tooth necks and increased sensitivity to temperature and touch. Treatment options for teeth grinding may include wearing a specially made splint during sleep to reduce the strain on the teeth. Relaxation techniques and stress management can also help reduce teeth grinding. In some cases, dental treatment may be needed to repair damage caused by teeth grinding and reduce tooth sensitivity. It's important to see a dentist to discuss the best treatment option for your specific problem.

beschwerde.sport-mit-zahnspange.abschnit.text: There is always a risk of impacts and blows during sport that can injure the teeth and jaw – especially in contact sports and those involving fast, jerky movements. For people wearing braces, this protection is even more important, as the teeth are more prone to injury during treatment with braces.
Mouth protection during sport – a must for those wearing braces

Children and teenagers as well as adults have an increased risk of tooth damage while wearing braces. This is because the teeth are being repositioned by the braces and are not yet fully stable. During this repositioning of the jaw, teeth are more sensitive to outside influences, for example unprotected contact during sport. A collision or blow to the face, upper or lower jaw can cause a tooth to loosen or even come out.

In addition, especially with fixed braces, there is a risk that the braces themselves may be damaged. Brackets or wires can come loose and injure the cheeks, lips, tongue or gums. If a bracket is damaged or comes off the tooth, this doesn't necessarily lead to injury. However, it does make another visit to the orthodontist necessary and can extend the length of treatment.
A custom sports mouthguard not only protects your teeth but also helps keep the braces in place.
Why is a mouthguard important for athletes with braces?

Besides the fit, the material of the mouthguard is also an important factor. For people wearing braces, it's especially important during sport that the mouthguard is made of a material that is both robust and flexible, able to absorb impacts well. Materials such as rubber or thermoplastic offer good shock absorption and adapt to the shape of your mouth to ensure maximum protection.

Of course, a good sports mouthguard shouldn't just be sturdy – it should also be comfortable to wear. Materials such as EVA (ethylene-vinyl acetate) offer a soft, flexible surface that is still robust enough to reduce the risk of damage to the teeth in the event of an impact.

You should also check that the mouthguard is compatible with your braces when buying one. Some models are specially designed for fixed braces, while others are better suited to removable braces. A good mouthguard offers both protection and comfort, so you can enjoy your sporting activities without worry. It's best to ask your dentist or orthodontist for advice.
Material

Not every mouthguard is suitable for every sport. If you do boxing or kickboxing, for example, you need a sturdier mouthguard that can withstand strong impacts. For less intense sports, a somewhat more flexible mouthguard may be enough, while still offering sufficient protection.
Suitable for your sport
After playing sport, you should rinse your mouth thoroughly to remove sweat and bacteria. Also clean your braces regularly with special brushes and dental floss.

Regular check-ups with your dentist or orthodontist are essential, especially if you're actively involved in sport. Your practitioner can check whether the braces are still fitting correctly and whether there are any signs of wear. They can also give you tips on caring for and protecting your braces during sport.

Our orthodontics team is happy to help check the condition of your braces or answer any questions you may have about protecting your teeth and braces during sport. Feel free to visit us at our practice on Kurfürstendamm for a consultation!
Tips for looking after your sports mouthguard

A well-fitting sports mouthguard is the best way to prevent injuries. It acts as a buffer, absorbing and evenly distributing the force of an impact or blow. This significantly reduces the pressure on sensitive teeth and braces. Orthodontic patients with fixed braces can choose a mouthguard with extra padding for the brackets for particularly reliable protection.

Besides protecting the teeth and braces, a mouthguard also helps protect the jaw from injury. Forces from collisions are cushioned, reducing the risk of jaw injuries. These can not only be very painful but can also put the entire course of treatment with braces at risk.
So a sports mouthguard is not just a preventive measure – it also helps ensure the smooth progress and success of orthodontic treatment.
The orthodontics team at our Berlin practice is here for you with any questions about treatment with removable or fixed braces. Feel free to make an appointment!
Protection for teeth, braces and jaw

Ideally, if you wear braces, you should use a mouthguard for any sporting activity to protect yourself from injury. However, some sports carry a particularly high risk of direct collisions, blows or falls. Here, a special mouthguard is essential.
Which sports call for a special mouthguard?

In martial arts such as boxing, karate or kickboxing, direct contact with an opponent is part of the sport, which significantly increases the risk of injury to the jaw, teeth and braces. A blow to the face can happen at any time and damage your teeth and braces.
Boxing, kickboxing and other martial arts

In team sports such as hockey, handball and football, collisions happen regularly. Whether it's a knock from a teammate, a hard fall to the ground or a ball hitting the head. Even if direct physical contact isn't always part of the game, there's still an increased risk that such accidents can cause serious damage to teeth or braces.
Hockey, football and other team sports

Even in recreational sport, young and adult braces wearers alike shouldn't neglect mouth protection. Sports such as basketball or skating carry an increased risk of accidents that can damage teeth and braces. Even activities without contact with other players, such as jogging or cycling, can lead to falls with painful and costly injuries.

A sports mouthguard specially designed for people wearing braces helps protect the teeth and jaw. Especially for people who are regularly active, protecting the teeth during recreational sports is an important precaution to avoid damage to the jaw, teeth and braces, and so to safeguard the orthodontic treatment. A sports mouthguard is a good, comfortable option for adults, children and teenagers alike, allowing them to enjoy sport without hindrance. This means they don't need to worry too much about possible injuries.
Other sports and recreational activities

Mouth protection for fixed braces differs in several ways from that for removable braces or aligners. Because of the brackets and wires, fixed braces have a more complex shape. This means the mouthguard needs a special fit to make sure it covers the entire brace while still leaving enough freedom of movement. A specially fitted sports mouthguard for fixed braces protects against impacts and ensures that no parts of the brace shift or get damaged.

For removable braces or aligners, a mouthguard is mainly important to protect the appliance itself. A poor-quality or ill-fitting mouthguard can cause the appliance to fall out or become damaged during an impact. Here it's advisable to choose a sports mouthguard that holds the appliance securely in place while still offering sufficient protection.
Sports mouthguards for fixed and removable braces

A universal mouthguard may be sufficient for occasional use. However, the best choice for people wearing braces is a custom-made mouthguard – especially if they play sport regularly. An individual fit ensures a perfect, secure fit, a comfortable feel, and the best possible protection.

A custom-made sports mouthguard also holds your braces in place and prevents them from shifting. A universal mouthguard often can't be adjusted enough and can't offer the stability, comfort and protection you need.
Individual fitting: why custom-made products make sense

The right fit of the mouthguard plays a crucial role in providing optimal protection. An individually fitted sports mouthguard ensures that both your teeth and your braces are reliably protected, without restricting freedom of movement or feeling uncomfortable to wear. Another advantage: with protection specially fitted to your mouth, you can speak and breathe without difficulty, which benefits your sporting performance. Make sure the mouthguard covers your teeth completely without pressing uncomfortably.

beschwerde.sport-mit-zahnspange.einstieg.text: Sport is an essential part of life for many people – as a balance to work, to reduce stress and, not least, to stay fit. For those wearing braces, sporting activity can come with some extra challenges when it comes to reliably protecting teeth and braces. Here you can find out how to choose the best mouthguard and what to look out for.

beschwerde.sport-mit-zahnspange.faq.0.an.text:
There are various types of mouthguard suited to different needs and types of braces for use during sport. Essentially, mouthguards can be divided into three main categories:
Standard mouthguard
This mouthguard is usually pre-made and comes in various sizes. It offers basic protection for the teeth but cannot be individually adjusted. A standard mouthguard can be an option if you do less intense sports. It's usually also sufficient if you wear removable braces or aligners that you take out during sport.
Boil-and-bite mouthguard
This type becomes flexible enough when heated in water for you to shape it to your mouth. It offers a better fit than a standard mouthguard, but doesn't always protect people with braces optimally, since the fit isn't exact.
Custom-made mouthguard
A custom-made mouthguard is specially matched to the exact shape of your teeth and braces. This is the best choice for maximum protection during sport, as it securely encloses both the teeth and the braces. Custom-made mouthguards offer the best fit, the highest comfort and the most reliable protection, especially for fixed braces.

beschwerde.sport-mit-zahnspange.faq.0.fr.text: What types of mouthguard are there?

beschwerde.sport-mit-zahnspange.faq.1.an.text:
There are mouthguard variants designed only for the upper teeth, as well as products for both the upper and lower jaw.
People with braces often use a sports mouthguard for the upper row of teeth, since this is usually where the braces are fitted. This protects the upper teeth, brackets and jaw from impacts and injuries, without needing to cover the lower jaw as well. Since the lower jaw is less prone to injury, this option is sufficient for many sports.
For intense contact sports, or if you also wear braces on your lower jaw, a double-sided mouthguard may be the better choice. This ensures that your upper jaw, lower jaw and entire braces are all reliably protected. In this case, it's best to choose an individually custom-made sports mouthguard that fits perfectly and doesn't restrict you.

beschwerde.vereiterter-zahn.abschnitte.0.text: A tooth abscess, often called a dental abscess, is a painful infection that develops in the tooth or the surrounding tissue. Such an abscess forms when bacteria settle deep inside the tooth, usually because of damaged tooth tissue or untreated tooth decay. The bacteria multiply and produce pus, a mixture of dead cells, bacteria and tissue remnants, which collects in the affected area and can eventually lead to painful pressure.

An infection usually begins with damage to the tooth or inadequate oral hygiene. If bacteria get inside the tooth or under the gum, they can spread through the tissue and the roots. Without timely treatment, the infection continues to grow, with pus building up in the surrounding tissue and, in the worst case, spreading to other parts of the body.
How does pus form at the tooth?

beschwerde.vereiterter-zahn.abschnitte.1.text: A tooth abscess often shows itself through a number of characteristic symptoms that point to an underlying infection. The signs range from mild discomfort to severe episodes of pain and complications that require urgent dental care. Early warning signs such as increased sensitivity or slight pressure pain can often go unnoticed, yet they can quickly develop into stronger symptoms such as throbbing pain, swelling and visible pus.
Early signs: sensitivity to hot and cold food and drink
Slight pressure pain
Severe toothache: particularly throbbing pain that can radiate into the ear or jaw.
Swollen gums and redness: local inflammation of the gums.
Pus and bad breath: visible pus and an unpleasant smell.
Sensitivity: persistent oversensitivity of the tooth.
Fever and a general feeling of being unwell
Swelling of the face or jaw area
Difficulty swallowing or breathing
Symptoms of a tooth abscess – how do you recognise an infection?

Root canal treatment: A common method for treating an abscessed tooth is root canal treatment. Here, the tooth's nerve is removed, the root canal system is cleaned and then filled to prevent a further infection. This procedure requires precision but is an effective way to preserve the tooth.

Incision and drainage: If the abscess is severely swollen and creating pressure, the dentist may make a small incision to let the pus drain out. This method relieves the pressure and supports better healing.

Tooth extraction: In cases where the tooth is severely damaged and can no longer be saved, extraction may be considered. This step is often the last resort to protect the health of the surrounding teeth and gums.
The long-term solution: dental procedures

Rinsing your mouth with warm salt water can help disinfect the oral cavity and ease mild inflammation. Regular rinsing supports wound healing and can help you feel more comfortable overall. Placing a warm compress on the affected cheek can ease the pain and improve blood flow, which supports healing. It is important, however, to make sure the temperature is right so as not to irritate the surrounding tissue.

At a glance: symptoms & treatments for an abscessed tooth

The best way to avoid a dental abscess is consistent prevention. Regular dental check-ups, thorough oral hygiene and a few simple precautions can significantly reduce the risk of tooth infections. So it's best to book your appointment at KU64 in Berlin today.

Regular check-ups at the dentist mean early signs of tooth decay or gum problems can be spotted and treated before they lead to an infection. The dentist can also carry out targeted preventive measures, such as professional teeth cleaning, which help minimise the build-up of bacteria.
To avoid tooth decay, it helps to eat a low-sugar diet, as sugar encourages bacterial growth. Fluoride toothpaste and mouthwash can also strengthen the teeth and protect them from acid attack.

Thorough brushing and daily flossing are essential for removing plaque and keeping bacterial growth in the mouth under control. Good oral hygiene prevents tooth decay and gum inflammation, supporting overall dental health.

Injuries to the teeth, such as cracks or chips, can make it easier for bacteria to get in. It's therefore advisable to wear a mouthguard during sports such as martial arts or contact sports, to minimise the risk of injury and the infections that can follow.
Preventing a dental abscess

An untreated dental abscess can have far-reaching health consequences that go beyond toothache. The infection can spread from the affected tooth root to the surrounding tissue, the jawbone, and even to other parts of the body.

If a dental abscess is left untreated, the bacteria spread into the surrounding tissue of the mouth. This can lead to a painful inflammation of the gums or cheeks. Swelling often develops, making it harder to eat and speak and significantly affecting daily life. In severe cases, the inflammation can spread to the throat tissue and cause difficulty swallowing.

Untreated tooth infections can lead to the formation of cysts or granulomas, which settle around the tooth root as a result of root inflammation. A cyst is a cavity that fills with fluid, while a granuloma is a chronic inflammation formed by the body as a defence response to the infection. Both can grow larger over time and put pressure on neighbouring teeth or the jawbone, which can also cause bone damage. Surgery is often needed to remove them.

In rare and particularly severe cases, the infection can enter the bloodstream and cause sepsis, or blood poisoning. Sepsis is a life-threatening response of the body to an infection that can lead to organ failure. People with a weakened immune system are at particular risk of the infection spreading more quickly. Sepsis requires immediate intensive medical care, as it can progress rapidly and endanger the patient's life.

One of the most serious complications of a dental abscess is infection of the jawbone, known as osteomyelitis. Bacteria can spread from the tooth root to the jawbone and cause a painful bone inflammation there. This inflammation requires intensive treatment, as it can cause permanent damage to the bone and may even require surgery to remove the infected tissue.

A dental abscess in the upper jaw can spread to the sinus and cause what's known as sinusitis. The connection between the tooth root and the sinus allows bacteria to penetrate the sinus lining, which can lead to chronic sinusitis. Those affected often experience facial pain, a blocked nose, and increased sensitivity around the sinuses.
Possible complications of an untreated dental abscess

In the long term, an untreated dental abscess can also put a strain on the immune system and increase the risk of other systemic illnesses. Studies suggest that chronic tooth infections may influence the risk of cardiovascular disease or diabetes, as the ongoing inflammatory response places a burden on the whole body.

Early and targeted treatment is essential not only for oral health but also for your overall health. This is why it is important to see a dentist as soon as the first signs appear, such as swelling, pain or the formation of pus, so that you can receive a quick diagnosis and treatment.
Acting quickly to prevent serious consequences

A dental abscess is not only painful but, left untreated, can carry serious health risks. Recognising the first symptoms and acting quickly are therefore essential to prevent the infection from spreading. Regular dental check-ups and thorough oral hygiene are the best ways to prevent infections.

So do not hesitate to see our practice at the first signs of toothache, and rely on consistent preventive care. Book an appointment with KU64 today and protect your dental health in the long term!
How to protect yourself from a dental abscess

A dental abscess, which often develops as a result of untreated pulpitis, can cause serious complications if not treated in time by a dentist. When an infection penetrates deep into the tooth root and forms pus there, swift action is crucial to prevent the infection from spreading to the surrounding tissue. In such cases, the dentist can treat the root inflammation and remove the pus through targeted measures such as root canal treatment, in order to relieve pain and preserve the health of the tooth.
Why is pus on a tooth dangerous?

Untreated dental abscesses can lead to serious complications, as the infection can spread and affect neighbouring tissue or the jawbone. In extreme cases, this can lead to the formation of cysts or even life-threatening complications such as sepsis, if the bacteria enter the bloodstream. Prompt treatment is therefore essential.
What are the risks if a dental abscess is left untreated?

Healing after root canal treatment varies depending on the severity of the infection. As a rule, the tissue heals within one to two weeks. Pain relief or anti-inflammatory medication may be prescribed to support recovery. Follow-up check-ups are important to ensure that the infection has fully cleared.

beschwerde.vereiterter-zahn.abschnitte.2.text: A tooth abscess is usually caused by bacteria entering the tooth, triggering an infection inside the tooth or in the surrounding tissue. They can reach the tooth in various ways, causing serious infections and inflammation.

Recurring dental abscesses may indicate an infection that was not fully treated or a new source of infection. A thorough examination helps to clarify the cause and, if necessary, to carry out further treatment, such as a revision of the root canal treatment.
What to do about recurring abscesses?

Although regular tooth brushing provides a good foundation for dental health, it is often not enough on its own to prevent dental abscesses. Additional measures such as daily flossing, antibacterial mouthwash and regular professional teeth cleaning are also important to prevent the development of tooth decay and gum inflammation.
Is brushing your teeth alone enough to prevent dental abscesses?

beschwerde.vereiterter-zahn.abschnitte.3.text: Bacteria can enter the inside of the tooth through damage to the enamel or via the gum. Once inside the tooth, the bacteria spread and release toxic substances that trigger an inflammatory reaction in the tissue. The body responds to this infection by sending white blood cells to fight it, which leads to the formation of pus – a mixture of dead cells, bacteria and tissue remnants.
Bacterial infections – the main cause of a tooth abscess

beschwerde.vereiterter-zahn.abschnitte.4.text: If tooth decay is left untreated, a deep cavity forms in the tooth, breaking through the enamel and opening the way for bacteria to reach the inside of the tooth. In advanced cases, the decay can reach right down to the tooth root and cause an infection there. Since cavities deep inside the tooth often grow unnoticed, the infection frequently goes untreated for a long time and can quickly develop into a painful abscess.
Tooth decay – the often unnoticed danger

beschwerde.vereiterter-zahn.abschnitte.5.text: A small crack or fracture in the tooth can be enough to encourage an infection. These cracks often result from accidents, eating hard food or grinding the teeth at night. Bacteria enter the pulp of the tooth through these small openings and can likewise cause an abscess there.
Injuries and cracks in the tooth – an entry point for bacteria

beschwerde.vereiterter-zahn.abschnitte.6.text: With periodontitis, the gums and jawbone recede, creating small pockets where bacteria can collect. These pockets allow bacteria to spread freely and reach even the roots of the teeth. Gum disease therefore significantly increases the risk of infections and tooth abscesses.
Periodontitis and gum disease – severe inflammation of the gums

beschwerde.vereiterter-zahn.abschnitte.7.text: Diagnosing an abscessed tooth correctly is crucial to starting the right treatment as quickly as possible and avoiding further complications. Your dentist will proceed in a structured and thorough way to pinpoint the exact cause of your symptoms.

The first step in diagnosing an abscessed tooth is a thorough examination by the dentist. The affected tooth is checked for visible signs of infection. Swelling, redness or other changes in the gum area are often noticeable. The dentist will also check whether the tooth is sensitive to pressure, which can be a typical symptom of an abscess. This visual examination provides initial clues, which are then supplemented with further methods.

X-rays play an important role in precisely locating an abscess or inflammation in the jaw area. The X-ray image shows whether and how deeply the infection has taken hold in the tooth, and whether surrounding structures such as the root tip are affected. It also reveals whether the infection has already spread to the surrounding tissue or even the jawbone. This information is essential for determining the right course of treatment and assessing the severity of the inflammation.

To assess whether the tooth is still alive, dentists often carry out what are known as pulp tests or cold tests. These check how the tooth reacts to cold stimuli. In a healthy tooth, a cold stimulus causes a slight tugging sensation, whereas an abscessed tooth either does not react at all or reacts extremely sensitively to the stimulus. These tests reveal whether the pulp (the tooth's 'nerve') has already died or is still alive. Combined with the visual and X-ray findings, these tests help the dentist determine the exact extent of the infection and decide on the best course of treatment.

beschwerde.vereiterter-zahn.abschnitte.8.text: An abscessed tooth requires prompt, targeted treatment to stop the infection and ease the pain. Depending on how severe and widespread the infection is, various treatment methods may be considered.
Treatment options for an abscessed tooth

beschwerde.vereiterter-zahn.abschnitte.9.text: Antibiotics: For a bacterial infection, the dentist will often prescribe antibiotics to fight the bacteria in the affected area and contain the infection. These medications help prevent the inflammation from spreading and support healing.
Painkillers: Painkillers are used to ease the pain and reduce symptoms in the short term. However, they only provide temporary relief and do not replace the necessary dental treatment.
These medications help with an abscessed tooth

beschwerde.weisheitszahn-op.abschnitte.0.text: Many people wonder why a wisdom tooth needs to be removed at all and why wisdom tooth surgery is necessary. The reasons for this are varied and range from lack of space in the jaw to serious health risks.

If you would like to enhance your radiant smile even further, our beauty department is available to you. Here, two highly experienced oral and maxillofacial surgeons take care of your lips and face. Why do wisdom teeth need to be removed?

beschwerde.weisheitszahn-op.abschnitte.1.text:
Wisdom teeth are the last teeth to erupt in adulthood. In many cases, however, they cause problems. A common issue is lack of space in the jaw, as wisdom teeth can often cause problems in the mouth if they don't have enough room to erupt. There is often not enough space for the wisdom teeth to erupt properly. This can lead to toothache, swelling around the tooth and a shifting of the other teeth. Wisdom teeth that grow crooked or misaligned can also cause problems. This can result in misalignment of the teeth and discomfort.
A partially erupted wisdom tooth is prone to inflammation. Bacteria can easily settle and cause infections. This inflammation is not only painful but can also endanger overall dental health. Wisdom teeth are also difficult to clean and prone to tooth decay and gum disease such as periodontitis. Early removal can help avoid these problems.
Reasons for wisdom tooth removal
The first few days after the operation:
Swelling and pain are common in the first few days after the operation. These can be eased with cooling and painkillers. Slight bleeding is also normal and should settle after a short time.
One week after the operation:

Swelling and pain usually decrease.
About a week after the procedure, the stitches are removed, unless dissolvable stitches were used.
Oral hygiene plays an important role during this phase to prevent infections.
Two to four weeks after the operation:

Over the following weeks, the gum continues to heal and the wound closes completely.
Most patients can already eat normally again at this stage and manage their daily life without major restrictions.
During the healing phase, it's important to follow the dentist's instructions closely and attend regular check-up appointments. These appointments help to monitor healing and make sure no complications occur.
Stages of healing after wisdom tooth surgery

Cooling
Avoid physical exertion and sporting activities in the first few days after the operation. Allow yourself enough rest to support healing.

Smoking and alcohol can affect wound healing and increase the risk of complications. Avoid these in the first few days after the operation.

Attend the check-up appointments with your dentist to monitor healing and make sure no complications occur.
Attending check-up appointments
Take the painkillers prescribed by your dentist regularly to keep pain and inflammation under control.
Pain medication
In the first few days after the operation, eat soft, cool foods such as soup, yoghurt or purée. Avoid hot, spicy and hard foods that could irritate the wound.
Soft and cool foods
Take care with thorough oral hygiene to prevent infections. Brush your teeth gently and avoid direct contact with the wound. If needed, use an antiseptic mouth rinse to support oral hygiene.
By following these tips, you can support the healing process after wisdom tooth surgery and help prevent complications.
Oral hygiene

Once the wisdom tooth has been removed, proper aftercare is essential for quick, trouble-free healing following wisdom tooth surgery. There are several important behaviours and dietary tips to keep in mind to support healing and avoid complications.
What should you keep in mind after wisdom tooth surgery?

After wisdom tooth surgery, it is important to cool the affected area regularly to reduce swelling and pain. Use a cold pack or an ice pack wrapped in a cloth and apply it for fifteen to twenty minutes. Repeat this several times a day. Avoid physical exertion and sporting activities in the first few days after surgery. Get plenty of rest to support the healing process. Take the prescribed painkillers regularly to keep pain and inflammation under control. Follow your dentist's instructions when doing so.

Pay attention to careful oral hygiene. Brush your teeth gently and avoid direct contact with the wound. If needed, use an antiseptic mouthwash to help prevent infection. Avoid smoking and alcohol in the first few days after surgery, as these can impair wound healing and increase the risk of complications. Attend your follow-up appointments with your dentist so that the healing process can be monitored and any complications ruled out.
Another important rule is to avoid vigorous rinsing or sucking, as this can disturb the blood clot and impair wound healing. Try to rinse your mouth gently and avoid drinking through a straw.
Tips for behaviour after wisdom tooth surgery

beschwerde.weisheitszahn-op.abschnitte.2.text: Removing wisdom teeth offers numerous benefits. One of the most important benefits is avoiding the pain and swelling that can be caused by teeth that haven't erupted properly. Wisdom tooth surgery also protects the surrounding teeth. If wisdom teeth don't have enough space, they can shift and damage neighbouring teeth.

Another benefit is improved oral hygiene. Wisdom teeth are often difficult to reach and clean, which increases the risk of tooth decay and gum disease. By removing these teeth, you can significantly improve your oral hygiene and thereby promote your overall dental health. In addition, inflammatory processes and related discomfort in the tooth or gum can be avoided, which considerably improves your quality of life.

Another decisive benefit of removing the wisdom teeth, or even just one tooth, is the prevention of cysts. Wisdom teeth that remain in the jaw can form cysts or tumours that can damage the jawbone and surrounding teeth. Removing the wisdom teeth significantly reduces this risk.
Soft and cool foods: In the first few days after surgery, stick to soft, cool foods such as soups, yoghurt, purées or smoothies. These do not put strain on the wound and support healing.
Avoiding hot and spicy foods: Hot and spicy foods can irritate the wound and delay healing. Avoid these foods until the wound has fully healed.
Drink enough fluids: Drink plenty of water to keep your body well hydrated. However, avoid hot drinks and fizzy drinks, as these could irritate the wound.
Chew on the opposite side: Chew your food on the side opposite the surgical wound to protect the affected area and support healing.
Gradually reintroduce solid food: Gradually reintroduce solid food once healing has progressed and you no longer feel any pain. Make sure the food is easy to chew and not too hard.

How wisdom tooth surgery is carried out

beschwerde.weisheitszahn-op.abschnitte.4.text:
Various preliminary examinations are necessary before wisdom tooth surgery to plan the procedure optimally. These include X-rays, which show the exact position of the wisdom teeth and their relationship to surrounding structures such as nerves and sinuses. In complicated cases, three-dimensional imaging may also be necessary.
These examinations are important for determining the best approach to removing the wisdom teeth and avoiding possible complications. They help the dentists understand the exact position of the teeth and plan the necessary steps. A thorough medical history and consideration of all relevant health aspects are also crucial for the successful performance of wisdom tooth surgery. At KU64, care is taken to ensure that all necessary examinations are carried out carefully and comprehensively, to guarantee safe and effective treatment.
Before the operation, you will also receive precise instructions on how to prepare for the procedure. This includes not eating or drinking for several hours before the surgery, particularly if general anaesthesia is planned. We will also discuss the various types of anaesthesia available to you, such as local anaesthesia, sedation or general anaesthesia, and select the method that suits you best.
Preliminary examinations before wisdom tooth surgery

beschwerde.weisheitszahn-op.abschnitte.5.text:
Administration of anaesthesia:
The agreed anaesthesia (local anaesthesia, sedation or general anaesthesia) is administered to ensure no pain is felt during the surgery.

Waiting for the anaesthesia to take effect:
Waiting until the anaesthesia has fully taken effect.

Making an incision in the gum:
The dentist makes a small incision in the gum to gain access to the wisdom tooth.

Removal of jawbone (if necessary):
If necessary, a small piece of jawbone is removed to expose the wisdom tooth.

Loosening and removal of the wisdom tooth:
The dentist carefully loosens and removes the wisdom tooth. If necessary, the tooth is divided into smaller pieces to ensure gentle removal.

Cleaning the wound:
The wound is thoroughly cleaned to prevent infection.

Stitching the wound (if necessary):
If needed, the wound is stitched to support optimal healing after treatment.
The entire treatment usually takes between twenty and sixty minutes, depending on the complexity of the case.

After the procedure, you will receive detailed aftercare instructions. These cover how to keep the wound clean, which painkillers you can take, and how to reduce swelling. You should rest and avoid physical exertion for the first one to two days after surgery.

beschwerde.weisheitszahn-op.abschnitte.6.text: Removing a wisdom tooth is a routine procedure, but as with any surgery, risks and complications can occur. It is important to know about them in order to prepare well and to know how to minimise possible problems.
Risks and complications of wisdom tooth surgery

beschwerde.weisheitszahn-op.abschnitte.7.text: Although removing a wisdom tooth is generally safe, various complications can occur:
Swelling and pain: Swelling and pain in the affected area are common after surgery. However, these can usually be managed well with painkillers and cooling.
Bleeding: Secondary bleeding can occur, and is usually easy to control. However, if bleeding is heavy or persistent, you should contact your dentist immediately.
Infections: If bacteria enter the wound, infections can occur. Thorough oral hygiene and taking antibiotics can help prevent this.
Nerve damage: In rare cases, temporary or permanent numbness in the lips, tongue or chin can occur if nerves are damaged.
Wound healing problems: Some patients may experience difficulties with wound healing, particularly smokers or people with certain pre-existing conditions.
Possible complications during wisdom tooth surgery

beschwerde.weisheitszahn-op.abschnitte.8.text: Experienced dentists can significantly reduce the risk of complications:
Careful planning and preparation of the surgery

A thorough examination and precise planning of the procedure are essential. X-rays and other diagnostic tools help determine the exact position of the wisdom teeth and choose the best approach for removal. A detailed medical history, taking into account all relevant health aspects of the patient, is equally important. This includes clarifying any pre-existing conditions, allergies and current medications. A comprehensive treatment plan is drawn up, covering all steps of the surgery as well as aftercare. This ensures that everyone involved is well prepared and that the procedure can be carried out under optimal conditions.

The use of modern surgical techniques and high-quality equipment minimises risks and supports fast, uncomplicated healing. Laser surgery and minimally invasive methods reduce tissue damage and support faster recovery. Modern imaging techniques allow precise planning and execution of the surgery, which increases safety and reduces the risk of complications.

Careful aftercare is important to ensure that the wound heals well and that any complications are recognised and treated early. The team at KU64 provides comprehensive aftercare and is available for any questions or concerns. Regular check-ups and clear instructions on caring for the wound at home make a significant contribution to smooth healing. Patients receive detailed information on how to behave after the surgery, such as avoiding certain activities and tips on diet.

Thanks to these measures, the risks of wisdom tooth surgery can be significantly reduced and successful healing supported. Close cooperation with experienced surgeons and the use of the latest technology significantly reduces the risk of complications. Trust the experienced team at KU64 to give you the best possible care.

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.abschnitte.0.text: Stay calm: Especially if the tooth broke during an accident, a fall or a strong impact, those affected are usually in shock at first. In such situations, it's important to stay calm and keep a clear head. Act thoughtfully and be aware that you are under the influence of adrenaline.

Recover the tooth piece(s): Not only do the broken tooth fragments on the ground or in your immediate surroundings need to be collected, but also the pieces still loose in your mouth. If the tooth has been knocked out completely, it's important to only hold it by the crown and not by the root.

Stop the bleeding: Are you bleeding from the impact or injury? Try first to locate the bleeding and stop it, for example with a tissue. You can also cool the affected area with a cold pack or a cold flannel to help prevent swelling.

Store the tooth piece(s) correctly: The knocked-out piece must be kept moist and cool so that it doesn't dry out and can no longer be reinserted or bonded back. The tooth can, for example, be stored in whole milk (1–2 hours), saline solution (30 minutes) or saliva (15 to 30 minutes).

Head to KU64: A broken tooth should be examined and treated by a dentist as quickly as possible. Our team at KU64 is well prepared for exactly this kind of situation, and our experts know precisely what to do and which type of first treatment is especially gentle and effective.
First aid for a broken tooth

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.abschnitte.1.text: Under certain circumstances, a tooth that has come out of the jaw completely, root and all, can be reinserted by the dentist. Acting quickly is truly essential here in order to save the tooth. If your tooth was knocked out by a blow or an accident, inform your dentist as quickly as possible. In particularly acute cases with severe pain, it is also advisable to visit an emergency dental service.
What should you do if the tooth has been knocked out completely?

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.abschnitte.2.text: The time between the tooth breaking and treatment by the dentist is particularly critical and can determine whether the tooth fragment can be bonded back on and the tooth “saved”. For this reason, there are a few things and mistakes you should avoid:

Carrying it in your bare hand – Once a tooth has broken, it's essential to keep it cool and moist. Never carry the tooth in your bare hand; instead, place it in a container with liquid such as saline solution or whole milk.
Not visiting a dental practice – A broken tooth needs to be treated by an expert. For this reason, you should never try to treat the tooth yourself, as this can damage the nerve fibres.
Cleaning the tooth or touching the root surface – It is essential that the tooth or the root is not damaged any further. For this reason, those affected should not try to clean the broken tooth.

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.abschnitte.3.text: A blow, a knock or an accident can result in dental trauma. This refers to the loosening or injury of one tooth or even several teeth. In most cases, it is particularly the upper front teeth or the canines that are affected. Various types of injury are distinguished, which can occur alongside a broken tooth fragment or a completely knocked-out tooth as a result of dental trauma:
Concussion: The dental accident causes a shock to the tooth socket, resulting in bruising. As a result, the tooth becomes extremely sensitive to touch and pressure.
Subluxation (loosening): The dental trauma causes the tooth to become loose. This results in bleeding.
Dislocation (displacement): The force involved causes the tooth socket in the jawbone to compress or stretch, changing the position of the tooth.
Intrusion (being pushed inward): the forces acting on the tooth are so strong that the tooth is pushed into the jawbone. As a result, the affected tooth will look shorter.
After such an incident, it is essential to visit a dental practice so the damage can be properly assessed, to avoid risking further serious consequences and endangering the health of your teeth.

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.abschnitte.4.text: The treatment is carried out by our experts. If no tooth fragment remains, fluoridation is often chosen. Here, the tooth or remaining piece is smoothed down and then fluoridated. In the longer term, a crown or an implant will then need to be fitted. If the front teeth are affected, this is advisable for aesthetic reasons alone. If the broken piece is still available, it can, in the best case, be reattached.

As a rule, it is worthwhile saving any tooth that can still be preserved. Our team at KU64 Berlin and Potsdam carefully treats the injured area and repairs your dental damage professionally and with routine skill. At KU64 in Berlin and Potsdam, we treat your broken tooth. In our practice, our dentists are very well prepared for such cases, so you will receive the best possible care and can leave our dental practice without pain. We look forward to your visit!
Dental treatment for a broken tooth

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.abschnitte.5.text: Nowadays, broken teeth or tooth fragments can be reattached very successfully. For this, the dentist uses a special bonding technique. During treatment, the composite adhesive is applied to the break and hardened under a blue light through polymerisation. Afterwards, the tooth in question should be treated with great care.

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.abschnitte.6.text: But what happens if the broken tooth cannot be reattached? If the broken piece of tooth cannot be found, or is no longer suitable for bonding, other measures must be taken. Depending on the size of the defect, the dentist may fit a partial crown or a full crown. Such treatment is usually preceded by root canal treatment. In most cases, the tooth root is still in the jaw. The root can either be surgically removed and replaced with a bridge or an implant, or it can be checked whether the root can still be used and a bridge attached to it.

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.abschnitte.7.text: Of course, an accident cannot be foreseen, and no amount of prevention is effective against such external forces. Nevertheless, there are several ways to help prevent other causes of a broken tooth.

You should visit your dentist at least twice a year to effectively protect your tooth structure from decay or inflammation. The purpose of such a dental check-up is to detect any diseases, vulnerable teeth and inflammation at an early stage. During this, the teeth, gums and oral mucosa are closely examined and checked. Your dentist at KU64 will examine your teeth for tartar, cracks, damaged fillings or reduced vitality. Any dental issues you have experienced can also be discussed at this time.
Get in touch with our team and book your check-up appointment today.

A tooth-friendly diet can do a great deal for the health of your own teeth. It is generally known that sugar promotes the formation of decay and should therefore not be eaten in large amounts. Another factor that particularly affects the brittleness of teeth is the combination of acidic foods followed directly by sweet ones, as this attacks the tooth enamel.

However, there are some foods you can enjoy with a clear conscience to strengthen the firmness of your teeth and protect them from breaking. One mineral that strengthens teeth and also supports their growth is calcium. Dairy products such as camembert, mozzarella or gouda contain a lot of calcium and are therefore particularly suitable. Pulses also strengthen teeth. Fluoride, too, makes tooth enamel more robust, making teeth less sensitive. This helps teeth better fend off bacteria and protects them more effectively against decay. Foods such as salmon, butter, walnuts or prawns contain a lot of fluoride.

In addition to brushing, it is important to clean the spaces between your teeth daily with dental floss or other aids, and to keep the mouth free of bacteria. Regular professional teeth cleaning should also be carried out. Professional teeth cleaning, known as prophylaxis, actively helps prevent decay and inflammation and is therefore the best form of prevention. This treatment is gentle and pleasant. Another advantage is that it protects not only your own teeth but also dental implants from decay. Thanks to prophylaxis, implants, fillings, veneers or inlays last considerably longer and are less prone to bacteria. During professional teeth cleaning, plaque and any discolouration caused by nicotine, tea or red wine are removed. Enamel hardening and deep fluoridation during prophylaxis effectively protect the teeth from acids. Thanks to special polishing instruments such as the AirFlow device, soft and hard plaque is removed and the teeth are strengthened in the long term.
Our dentists at KU64 will be happy to advise you during your appointment on whether professional teeth cleaning is needed. Get in touch by email at info@KU64.de or by phone on 030 864 73 20.

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.abschnitte.8.text: In our practice, you can access a wide range of dental services, such as implants, bridges or veneers. Our specialists at KU64 guarantee you a radiant smile once again, thanks to high-quality dental restorations. If a loose or broken tooth can no longer be saved, a dental implant offers many advantages:
the implant functions like your own tooth
compared to a denture, an implant is considerably more robust
your speech remains unaffected thanks to high-quality dental implants

Thanks to a mix of innovative ideas, various treatments, trained staff, and an appealing, calming design, we manage to take away our patients' fear.
Discover our unique concept and book your appointment at KU64 in Berlin or Potsdam today. We look forward to your visit!
Back to a radiant smile, without any fear

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.faq.0.frage.text: Is it serious if a tooth breaks?

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.faq.1.antwor.text: Depending on how large the broken piece of tooth is, there are different approaches to achieving the best treatment for a broken tooth. If it is a large fragment, the tooth may need to be extracted and replaced with an implant. However, the dentist will first check whether the piece of tooth can be reattached. beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.faq.3.antwor.text: Even years later, teeth can become discoloured due to a past dental injury. This is usually caused by deposits of blood breakdown products or dead nerve tissue in the tooth. This discolouration occurs either directly as an immediate result of the dental trauma or, for example, as a result of root canal treatment. The discolouration can be removed through a special bleaching treatment.

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.faq.3.frage.text: Can teeth become discoloured after a break?

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.faq.4.antwor.text:
The break damages the tooth enamel and, if left untreated, can in the worst case be completely destroyed. If a broken tooth is left untreated, various complications can result:
Inflammation
Formation of pus

Discolouration (brown or black)

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.faq.4.frage.text: What happens if a broken tooth is not treated?

beschwerde.zahn-abgebrochen.faq.5.antwor.text:
A blow or impact can cause a tooth to become loose. In some cases, the affected tooth needs to be immobilised and stabilised with a splint. The splint must be worn until the tooth is firmly anchored in the bone again.
If the loose tooth is so wobbly that it can no longer be saved, the dentist must extract it. Bridges or implants can then be a good way to replace the missing tooth. A bridge is only an option if the neighbouring teeth are still stable. If this is not the case, a dental implant is the right choice.

beschwerde.zahn-locker.abschnitte.22.blo.text: Whether healthy teeth stay firm doesn't depend only on regular dental visits: what matters is building the right habits into your daily routine early on. beschwerde.zahn-locker.abschnitte.23.blo.text: Brushing your teeth daily is a good start. But technique and cleaning between the teeth are what really matter. beschwerde.zahn-locker.abschnitte.24.blo.text: Even with careful care and regular flossing at home, there are spots that are difficult or impossible to reach on your own. Attend regular check-ups so that early signs, such as gum pockets or receding gums, can be spotted and addressed in good time, before teeth become loose.

beschwerde.zahn-locker.abschnitte.25.blo.text: Smoking impairs blood flow to the gums and slows down healing. This significantly increases the risk of periodontitis. beschwerde.zahn-locker.abschnitte.4.bloe.text: A tooth doesn't become loose without reason. In most cases, dental causes are behind it. Some develop gradually, while others show symptoms quite suddenly. The sooner the correct diagnosis is made, the better the chances of saving the tooth.

beschwerde.zahn-locker.abschnitte.5.bloe.text: Periodontitis is the most common cause of loose teeth in adults. Bacterial plaque causes a chronic inflammation that attacks the tissue supporting the teeth, including the jawbone. If left untreated, the teeth lose their support and start to become wobbly.

beschwerde.zahn-locker.einstieg.0.text.text: Loose teeth are always worrying for those affected – whether the wobbling appears suddenly or develops gradually. beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.0.antwort.text:
A tooth doesn't usually become loose without a cause. In most cases, there's an underlying condition affecting the structures that support the tooth, such as untreated gum inflammation that has developed into chronic inflammation. Bacteria and deposits such as tartar cause so-called gum pockets to form over time, in which germs multiply unchecked. This can lead to a breakdown of tissue and bone, causing teeth to lose their hold and start to wobble. Receding gums, severe teeth grinding or uneven bite pressure can also affect stability. Anyone who notices such changes early on should visit a periodontology practice to take action in good time.
Our experienced team at KU64 in Berlin will help you preserve your teeth. Get in touch with us today!

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.0.frage.text: Can a tooth just become loose for no reason?

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.1.antwort.text:
After root-end resection surgery, a tooth can feel temporarily loose – a normal reaction of the tissue to the procedure. This treatment is usually carried out for chronic inflammation at the root tip, often caused by bacteria that have penetrated the area. Opening the area and removing tissue relieves some pressure and causes changes in the surrounding bone, which can initially create a wobbly feeling. Once the inflammation subsides, the tooth often stabilises again. However, if gum recession, gum inflammation or symptoms such as bleeding gums occur, a dental check-up should follow promptly.
Our specialist dentists at KU64 are happy to advise you in person at our practice in Berlin or Potsdam if your tooth feels loose after root-end resection surgery.

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.1.frage.text: Why is my tooth loose after root-end resection surgery?

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.2.antwort.text:
Whether a loose tooth becomes firm again mainly depends on the cause and how far the condition has progressed. In many cases, such as early periodontitis or acute gum inflammation, the structures supporting the tooth can be stabilised with targeted periodontal treatment. This includes thorough cleaning of gum pockets, removal of bacteria and tartar, and supportive measures such as splinting. If bone loss has already occurred, targeted bone grafting may be necessary. In cases of advanced looseness and severe damage, preserving the tooth is sometimes no longer possible. In that case, modern dental prosthetics, for example dental implants, restore stability.
Have your tooth examined in good time by our specialists at KU64. With early diagnosis and treatment, loose teeth can often be saved.

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.2.frage.text: Can loose teeth be made firm again?

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.3.antwort.text:
There's no general answer to how long a tooth wobbles before it actually falls out. It depends heavily on the underlying condition, how far it has progressed, and how it responds to any treatment. With a chronic gum disease such as periodontitis, the process can take months or years, while acute inflammation or injuries in the mouth can lead to tooth loss much more quickly. Patients often only notice the wobbling late on, once the gums have already receded or become inflamed. Acting quickly is therefore crucial: anyone who notices changes early and visits a practice straight away has a good chance of saving the tooth.
Make an appointment at KU64 in good time. Our experienced team in Berlin will help you recognise and minimise the risk of tooth loss early on.

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.3.frage.text: How long does a tooth wobble before it falls out?

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.4.antwort.text:
No, wobbly teeth don't necessarily have to be extracted. Whether a tooth can be preserved depends on the cause and severity of the looseness – for example, whether periodontal disease, bone loss or mechanical strain is behind it. In many cases, teeth can be stabilised with the right treatment, for example periodontitis therapy, splinting or tissue regeneration. Your dentist will assess how advanced the condition is and whether the tooth is still firmly anchored in the jawbone.
 
If the tooth can no longer be saved, modern dental prosthetics – such as dental implants or bridges – provide an aesthetic and functional solution.
At our practice, we assess individually whether a loose tooth can be preserved and advise you fully on all alternatives. Please get in touch with us!

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.4.frage.text: Does a tooth have to be extracted if it's wobbling?

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.5.antwort.text:
Whether a loose tooth becomes firm again after periodontitis treatment (also known as periodontal disease treatment) depends on how far the condition has progressed and on the individual healing process. The aim of treatment is to stop the inflammation, remove disease-causing bacteria from the gum pockets, and prevent further breakdown of gum tissue and bone. In early stages, the tissue can stabilise after therapy, allowing the teeth to regain more support. However, for teeth that are already significantly loose, full stabilisation is not guaranteed.
That's why it's important to take early symptoms seriously and visit a specialist periodontology practice. At KU64, we support you with modern periodontal therapy and years of experience to help find a solution that preserves your tooth.

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.5.frage.text: Do loose teeth become firm again after periodontitis treatment? Dentistry at KU64 dental practice in Berlin.

beschwerde.zahn-locker.faq.6.antwort.text:
The cost of treating loose teeth depends on the cause and the treatment required. In many cases, for example with periodontitis, statutory health insurers cover part of the cost, particularly when systematic periodontitis treatment is medically necessary.
Individual additional services such as splinting, regenerative procedures or high-quality dental prosthetics (e.g. dental implants) are, however, often private services that you pay for yourself or cover through supplementary dental insurance.
