beschwerde.zahnschmerzen.abschnitte.1.bl.text: As a highly non-specific symptom, toothache can occur in very different ways. Patients may perceive it as throbbing, stabbing or dull pain. The pain can also vary from mild to severe. Just as varied as these symptoms are, so too are their underlying causes. This is why an assessment by the dentist is so important.

beschwerde.zahnschmerzen.abschnitte.10.b.text: In extreme cases, a tooth needs to be removed completely. If a tooth is badly damaged and can no longer be saved, extraction becomes necessary. The dentist carefully removes the affected tooth to relieve the pain. Of course, we will also advise you fully on how your bright smile can be restored through our wide range of tooth replacement options.

beschwerde.zahnschmerzen.abschnitte.11.b.text: Prevention is better than cure, and it is the most effective way to guard against toothache. It is also cheaper. After all, the best tooth is a healthy tooth, and as part of our holistic approach to dentistry, we support you with a wide range of preventive measures so that, ideally, your teeth last a lifetime.
Good oral hygiene is the most important thing when it comes to preventing toothache. Here are a few tips for prevention:
Brush your teeth thoroughly at least twice a day with a fluoride toothpaste.
Use dental floss to remove plaque and food debris from between your teeth.
Rinse regularly with an antibacterial mouthwash to kill bacteria.
Avoid excessive consumption of sugary foods and drinks, as they can cause tooth decay.
Visit your dentist regularly for check-ups and professional teeth cleaning.

beschwerde.zahnschmerzen.abschnitte.12.b.text: Not every minor problem with aching teeth calls for extensive medical treatment right away. There are some home remedies that can offer temporary relief from toothache and have a proven effect. With our tips for the best home remedies, you can provide relief yourself. However, it is important to note that these remedies cannot replace professional dental treatment. They do not always work, and only to a limited extent. If in doubt, please book an appointment at our practice so that we can carefully determine the cause of your symptoms.

That said, it is a good idea to first try well-known and effective home remedies to ease or at least reduce the discomfort you are experiencing. Here we have put together the best-known home remedies for toothache that may help:

beschwerde.zahnschmerzen.abschnitte.13.b.text: A salt water rinse has a disinfecting effect and can help reduce bacteria in the mouth and ease inflammation. To make it, mix a teaspoon of salt into a glass of warm water and rinse your mouth with the salt solution for about 30 seconds. Then spit it out. You can repeat the rinse several times a day as needed.

beschwerde.zahnschmerzen.abschnitte.14.b.text: Especially when swelling occurs, the affected area of skin is often warmer than usual. Cooling is therefore a good option to help reduce the pain, as cold dampens the sensation of pain. Place a cooling gel pack or a cold cloth on the affected area for a few minutes to reduce swelling and achieve temporary pain relief.

beschwerde.zahnschmerzen.abschnitte.15.b.text: Clove oil contains a substance called eugenol, which has anti-inflammatory and, as a result, pain-relieving properties. Tea tree oil is said to have a similar effect. You can try it out to see if it helps you. Both are available at any pharmacy. Soak a cotton ball in clove oil and dab it gently on the aching tooth, or carefully drip the oil onto it.

beschwerde.zahnschmerzen.abschnitte.15.t.text: Clove oil and tea tree oil

beschwerde.zahnschmerzen.abschnitte.16.b.text: Chamomile tea has anti-inflammatory properties. This means you can use it in the same way as cold packs and clove oil to achieve a pain-relieving effect. Brew a chamomile tea and let it cool. Rinse your mouth with the cooled tea and spit it out after swishing it around.

It is important to remember that the home remedies mentioned here only provide temporary relief and cannot replace a visit to the dentist. To treat the underlying cause of the toothache and find a long-term solution, you should always see a dentist if the pain does not noticeably ease after a short time.

beschwerde.zahnschmerzen.abschnitte.2.bl.text: In some cases, swelling may occur around the aching tooth or gum alongside the pain. The swelling can appear as a firm lump, or it may be more blister-like with a softer surface.

beschwerde.zahnstein-entfernen-behandeln.text: Tartar is a hard build-up of minerals and bacteria that forms as plaque on the teeth through saliva. This build-up develops from plaque, a sticky substance made up of food residue and bacteria that accumulates on the tooth. If plaque is not removed regularly, it mineralises over time and forms tartar. This can appear yellowish to brownish and feels hard. It typically forms along the gum line and in areas where the teeth touch one another.
What exactly is tartar?

There are various risk factors that promote the formation of plaque and therefore tartar. These include inadequate oral hygiene, poor diet, smoking, genetic predisposition, and certain medical conditions such as diabetes or Sjögren's syndrome. Smoking reduces saliva production, which in turn impairs the teeth's self-cleaning ability and can therefore lead to the formation of plaque and, as a result, tartar. Genetic predisposition can influence the composition of saliva, which can also affect the formation of tartar. In addition, certain medical conditions, such as diabetes, can increase the risk of tartar, as they affect saliva, increase susceptibility to dental problems and lead to the formation of tartar. It is important to be aware of these risk factors and take appropriate measures to prevent tartar formation or at least reduce it.
How does tartar form?

Tartar is not only unsightly but can also lead to various problems with oral health. One of the main reasons why tartar formation is problematic lies in its rough, porous structure. It can irritate the gums and cause inflammation, which may lead to gum recession, gum inflammation and bleeding gums. In addition to these dental problems, tartar can also allow bacteria to settle in the gum pockets, which can lead to an advanced form of gum disease known as periodontitis. Bad breath can also result from tartar, as bacteria settle and multiply in the deposits on the tooth.
Furthermore, tartar can lead to aesthetic problems, as it can take on a yellowish-brown discolouration and thus affect the appearance of the teeth. Removing tartar and plaque through professional teeth cleaning is often necessary to eliminate this discolouration. If tartar is not removed, it can damage the gum and bone beneath the tooth, which can lead to loosening and, eventually, tooth loss.
Tartar as a health risk – effects on teeth and gums

Good oral hygiene is essential to prevent tartar from forming. This includes brushing regularly, ideally twice a day, as well as using floss or interdental brushes to remove plaque between the teeth. Regular dental check-ups and professional teeth cleaning, along with preventive care, are also important for removing tartar and maintaining oral health. The following points are also essential for thorough oral hygiene:
regular and thorough brushing (at least twice a day)
using floss or interdental brushes
using fluoride toothpaste
a balanced diet & avoiding sugary food and drinks
regular visits to the dentist (teeth cleaning, preventive care)

Following these measures to prevent tartar can help maintain oral health and reduce the risk of complications such as gum inflammation or tooth decay. Ultimately, consistent and thorough oral hygiene is the key to preventing tartar formation and preserving the health of teeth and gums in the long term. Regular visits to the dentist are also essential to detect and treat any signs of tartar at an early stage.
Prevention: measures for healthy teeth

The formation of tartar is not just an aesthetic issue but can also have serious effects on oral health. This is why thorough oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups are important to prevent tartar from forming and to avoid related problems. If tartar has already formed, it is equally important to seek professional help quickly. Tartar can usually be removed well, and there are various options and treatments available for this.

Professional teeth cleaning is an essential part of oral hygiene and plays a decisive role in removing tartar. This treatment is usually carried out by dental hygienists or a dentist. During a professional teeth cleaning, tartar and plaque that have built up on the teeth over time are thoroughly removed. This is done using special instruments such as ultrasonic devices and hand instruments. Hard tartar is removed from the teeth, and the spaces between teeth and hard-to-reach areas, which are often not fully accessible with conventional means, are cleaned.

It is recommended to have a professional teeth cleaning every six months, although the frequency can vary depending on individual needs. People at higher risk of tartar formation, such as smokers or those with a history of gum disease, may benefit from more frequent cleanings.

Alongside traditional mechanical methods, advanced technologies such as ultrasonic and laser devices are now also used to effectively remove tartar. Ultrasonic devices use high-frequency vibrations to gently loosen tartar from the teeth. A special ultrasonic tip is directed at the tartar deposits, causing them to break apart and become easier to remove. This method is particularly gentle on the gums and provides thorough cleaning without damaging the surrounding tissue.

Laser devices are also used to remove tartar, particularly stubborn deposits. Here, too, laser beams are directed specifically at the tartar, splitting and vaporising it. This method is precise and minimally invasive, as it only targets the tartar while sparing the surrounding tissue. In addition, the laser has a disinfecting effect, which helps reduce bacteria and promote healing.

The mechanical removal method aims to remove particularly hard tartar from the tooth surface in order to maintain oral health and prevent problems such as tooth decay and gum disease. Various instruments are used for the mechanical removal of tartar, including special tartar scrapers such as scalers and curettes. These instruments allow tartar to be thoroughly removed from the tooth surface and the gum line, where deposits can easily build up.

The process of mechanical tartar removal requires skill and care to ensure that the tartar is completely removed without injuring the surrounding gum tissue. Mechanical removal of tartar is crucial for keeping teeth and gums healthy and preventing oral health problems. It is important to schedule regular dental check-ups and professional teeth cleaning to ensure that tartar is effectively removed and that oral health is optimally maintained.
Goodbye tartar: the importance of professional cleaning

Removing tartar yourself at home – home scalers, home remedies and pharmacy products make it seem temptingly simple. But what actually works, what does more harm than good, and when is a visit to the dentist unavoidable? Find out in our blog post. And one thing in advance: stubborn tartar should always be removed professionally.
Home treatment – can you remove tartar yourself?

Tartar can lead not only to superficial problems such as discolouration and bad breath, but can also trigger serious diseases of the gums and the structures supporting the teeth. Fortunately, a wide range of treatment options are now available to effectively treat these conditions and restore the health of teeth and gums:

For deeper discolouration or irregularities in shape, veneers can offer a lasting solution. Veneers are wafer-thin shells made of ceramic or composite, custom-made and bonded to the front of the teeth to improve their shape, colour and size. It is important to note, however, that veneers represent a permanent change to the teeth, so a thorough examination and consultation with a dentist is necessary beforehand to make sure they are the right option.

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.abschnitte.0..text: Tooth discolouration refers to changes in the colour of the teeth, which can be caused by a number of different factors and often affects the appearance of the smile. This discolouration can be divided into two main categories: intrinsic (internal) and extrinsic (external) tooth discolouration.

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.abschnitte.1..text: Intrinsic (internal) discolouration is caused by changes within the tooth tissue itself. This type of discolouration can result from taking certain medications, such as tetracycline, during tooth development, from illness, or from traumatic events affecting the tooth pulp. Intrinsic discolouration is usually set deeper within the tooth structure and is therefore more difficult to treat than extrinsic discolouration.

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.abschnitte.10.text: Professional treatment methods offer effective solutions for removing tooth discolouration and restoring the natural whiteness of your teeth. These methods range from thorough teeth cleaning to special whitening treatments, which can be carried out at the dental practice or at home.
Professional treatment methods for tooth discolouration

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.abschnitte.11.text: A professional teeth cleaning and polish is often the first step in removing surface discolouration. This thoroughly removes deposits such as plaque and tartar that can stain the teeth. The subsequent polishing smooths the surface of the teeth, reducing the build-up of strongly coloured substances from food and drink. This treatment is not only effective in restoring the natural whiteness of your teeth but is also important for overall oral health.

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.abschnitte.12.text: Whitening is a popular method for treating stubborn tooth discolouration that cannot be removed with normal cleaning. There are various whitening options, used depending on individual preference and the condition and degree of discolouration of the teeth:

In-office whitening: This method is carried out directly at the dental practice and offers fast, visible results. A highly concentrated whitening agent is applied to the teeth, and the process is often supported by a special light or laser treatment. This method can noticeably whiten teeth in a short time.

Home whitening: With home whitening, your dentist provides you with custom-fitted trays and a whitening agent for use at home. The process is slower than in-office whitening but offers a convenient and more affordable alternative. It does, however, require consistent use over several weeks.

Over-the-counter products: There are also whitening products available without a prescription, such as toothpastes, gels and strips. These products contain lower concentrations of whitening agents and are therefore less effective than professional treatments. However, they are an affordable option for mild discolouration.
Although whitening is generally safe, some side effects can occur, particularly if used incorrectly:
Tooth sensitivity: After whitening, teeth may temporarily become more sensitive to hot and cold foods and drinks. This sensitivity usually subsides after a few days.
Gum irritation: If the whitening agent comes into contact with the gums, it can cause temporary irritation or inflammation.
Uneven results: Especially with heavily filled or root-treated teeth, whitening can lead to uneven results, as fillings and dental restorations do not whiten.
After successfully treating tooth discolouration, it is important to maintain the results in the long term. This requires careful aftercare and adjusting certain habits to avoid new staining.

In the first few days after whitening, teeth are particularly prone to new staining. It is advisable to avoid strongly staining foods and drinks such as coffee, tea, red wine, berries and soy sauce. Smoking should also be avoided, as nicotine causes strong discolouration.

Regular brushing with a fluoride toothpaste and daily use of dental floss help keep teeth clean and prevent discolouration. A professional teeth cleaning every six months also helps remove plaque and tartar, which can contribute to staining.
After whitening, whitening toothpastes can be used to prolong the result. These toothpastes contain mild abrasives that remove staining before it can set in.

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.abschnitte.13.text: Alongside classic methods such as professional cleaning and bleaching, there are also gentler alternatives for treating tooth discolouration. These methods are particularly suitable for people with sensitive teeth or who wish to avoid aggressive bleaching agents.
Alternative and gentle methods for treating tooth discolouration

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.abschnitte.14.text: Veneers and Lumineers are thin, custom-made shells that are placed on the front surface of the teeth to conceal aesthetic problems such as tooth discolouration.

Veneers are made from ceramic or composite materials and offer a long-lasting solution for tooth discolouration. However, they do require minimal grinding of the tooth surface so they can be firmly anchored to the teeth. The main advantage of veneers is their natural appearance and durability. They resist discolouration and can last for years.

Lumineers are a special type of veneer that are even thinner and can often be applied without grinding down the tooth substance. This makes the procedure less invasive and reversible. The downside, however, is that Lumineers do not always look as natural as conventional veneers and may be less effective at covering heavily discoloured teeth.

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.abschnitte.15.text: Both veneers and Lumineers provide an immediate aesthetic improvement and are particularly effective for tooth discolouration that cannot be sufficiently removed by bleaching. They are durable and offer a stable solution.
Veneers require irreversible preparation of the tooth, while Lumineers sometimes do not provide the desired natural look. Both options are also more costly than other methods.

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.abschnitte.16.text: Many people prefer natural methods for whitening teeth, which are less invasive and gentler. The most common natural and home remedies include:

Baking soda: rubbing the teeth with baking soda is a common method for removing surface discolouration. It acts as a mild abrasive and can remove plaque and discolouration from the teeth. However, it should not be used too often, as it can wear down the tooth enamel.

Oil pulling: oil pulling is an Ayurvedic method in which oil is swished around the mouth for a few minutes. It is said to help remove bacteria and clean the mouth. Although there is no direct evidence of a whitening effect, some people swear by the method as a way of improving oral hygiene.

Strawberries and lemon juice: rubbing the teeth with a paste of mashed strawberries and lemon juice is promoted as a natural bleaching agent. However, the fruit acids can attack the tooth enamel, so this method should be used with caution.

These natural methods can remove mild discolouration, but they are usually less effective than professional treatments. They offer a gentle alternative, but the results vary and are often not as long-lasting. Some home remedies, such as lemon juice or baking soda, can damage the tooth enamel if used incorrectly and lead to sensitive teeth over the long term. It is advisable to use such methods sparingly and with care.
Natural and home remedies for discoloured teeth

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.abschnitte.3..text: Consuming certain foods and drinks such as coffee, tea, red wine or strongly pigmented fruits can lead to tooth discolouration. These substances contain chromogens, which attach to the tooth enamel and cause the teeth to become stained.

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.faq.5.antwort.text: Some home remedies, such as rinsing with coconut oil or brushing with baking soda, are often recommended for treating tooth discolouration and can help keep teeth white. However, these methods should be used with caution, as they may damage the enamel or fail to achieve the desired results. It's always advisable to consult a dentist before trying home remedies.

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.faq.5.frage.text: Can home remedies help with tooth discolouration?

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.faq.6.antwort.text: It's advisable to see a dentist for any form of tooth discolouration, so that the cause can be identified and suitable treatment options discussed. In particular, sudden or uneven discolouration should be assessed by a professional as soon as possible.

beschwerde.zahnverfaerbung.faq.6.frage.text: When should I see a dentist if I notice tooth discolouration?

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.abschni.text: Leaking fillings, loose or broken teeth, and cracks in the tooth can lead to an infection of the root canal if left untreated.
A root canal infection has clear causes
It is accompanied by a throbbing pain that often appears suddenly, along with swelling or even an abscess at the affected tooth.
A root canal infection has typical symptoms

Impacts and blows to the teeth, or teeth grinding, can cause small cracks to form or blood vessels to burst. This gives bacteria the chance to enter the tooth and trigger an infection of the root canals.
Injuries to the tooth
These are the typical symptoms of an inflamed tooth root:
Severe, usually throbbing toothache appears quite suddenly, even at the start of the infection.
A “swollen cheek” caused by painful swelling of the gum.
Sensitivity when eating and unpleasant sensations in the tooth, especially with sweet foods.
A feeling of pressure in the tooth.

If you have toothache, it is advisable to see a dentist straight away. Even if the pain goes away again, this does not mean the inflammation has healed. Without treatment by a dentist, this is only possible in very rare cases. In the worst case, pain that suddenly subsides can mean that the tooth has already died. For this reason, you should have any possible inflammation around the tooth root checked by your dentist right away, along with an examination of your teeth, jaw and gums.
What are the symptoms of an inflamed tooth root?

An untreated inflammation of the tooth root can have serious consequences for both body and mind. Our teeth are connected to the entire body through nerves and blood vessels. This means that bacteria causing the inflammation can travel from the tooth root into the bloodstream and affect other organs. The risk of these bacteria causing inflammation elsewhere in the body is particularly high in people with a weakened immune system.

Pain caused by an inflamed tooth root does not only affect the mind. It often leads to further pain, such as headaches, migraines or earache. Tension and sleep problems are also possible consequences of an inflamed tooth root.
To prevent the condition from spreading, it is essential to seek dental treatment as soon as possible. Get in touch with the KU64 team today and book an appointment at our practice.
What are the consequences of an inflamed tooth root?

At the KU64 Berlin dental practice, we first examine your entire set of teeth and specifically the affected tooth. Since an inflamed tooth root is not directly visible from the outside, it helps a great deal if you, as a patient, can give us precise details about the duration and nature of your symptoms.

If there is a suspicion that the inflamed tooth has died, a test using a cold substance or a slight electrical stimulus can provide clarity. In a dead tooth, the dental pulp does not react to these stimuli.

If necessary, the dentists at KU64 will also take an X-ray to get to the bottom of the inflamed tooth root. This is because decay-causing bacteria may have settled unnoticed under a filling or crown, and the pulp inflammation may have developed from there. The X-ray also shows whether these germs have already reached the jawbone and caused damage to the bone.
How is an inflamed tooth root diagnosed?
When treating an inflamed tooth root, our dentists discuss the course of treatment with you and take the time to answer any open questions. The therapy involves both medication and surgical measures.
Inflamed tooth root – treatment and therapy

Even though it cannot heal the tooth root itself, dentists initially prescribe an antibiotic in the case of an infection. This helps the inflammation subside for the time being and eases the pain and swelling at the tooth root.
Preparatory treatment with antibiotics

The most important procedure for treating a root inflammation is root canal treatment. Many patients feel anxious about this, fearing pain during the procedure. However, our experienced specialists carry out the treatment as gently as possible, and it is almost entirely pain-free.
The affected tooth is given a local anaesthetic by injection. The anaesthetic takes a few minutes to take effect, which the dentist checks before starting the treatment.
The dentist drills a small hole into the enamel to clear the affected areas of bacteria.
The dentist then removes the diseased pulp.
The tooth is then rinsed and thoroughly disinfected.
Finally, the dentist seals the tooth with a filling. The infection can then heal undisturbed.

After root canal treatment for a root inflammation, the affected tooth and the surrounding area are particularly sensitive for the first few days. For this reason, there are a few points patients should bear in mind after the procedure:
Only eat and drink again once the local anaesthetic has worn off.
Avoid very cold or hot food and drinks for the first few days.
Also avoid alcohol, nicotine and caffeinated drinks for the first few days.
Root canal treatment as the standard procedure

In rare cases, a simple root canal treatment is not enough, because the inflamed tissue cannot be fully removed. In this case, your dentist has to open the gum and drill into the bone as far as the root tip of the tooth. Both the inflamed tissue and the root tip are then removed – hence the term apicoectomy. We only carry out this dental treatment if it allows the tooth to be preserved.
Apicoectomy as an additional procedure

In extreme cases, the tooth is already so badly affected and destroyed by bacteria that it can no longer be saved through root canal treatment or an apicoectomy. In this case, the only option left is to extract it. Extraction is a comparatively small and quick procedure. Afterwards, we will discuss with you all the possible options and costs for dental replacement, in order to close the resulting gap in your mouth.

To avoid extraction becoming necessary, it is important to see a dental practice early if you have symptoms. Our dentists at KU64 Berlin have years of experience in treating root inflammations and ensure that your pain is relieved quickly and any damage kept to a minimum.
Last resort: extraction

To prevent inflammation of the dental pulp (pulpitis) – accompanied by symptoms such as swollen gums and jaw pain – from occurring in the first place, regular oral and dental hygiene is essential. This means brushing your teeth at least twice a day after meals.
How can I prevent a root inflammation?
The infection can usually be stopped with medication such as antibiotics and a root canal treatment; in the worst case, the tooth has to be extracted.
A root canal infection can be treated well
Regular preventive check-ups ensure that a tooth inflammation is detected in good time, so that a procedure such as root canal treatment is not needed at all. Visit your dental practice regularly.
Preventive care

Professional teeth cleaning removes hidden, soft and mineralised plaque both above and below the gum line. You should have a professional teeth cleaning as a preventive measure against tooth decay every six to twelve months. Our specialists are happy to advise you on this.
Professional teeth cleaning

To prevent tooth decay, it is important to attend regular dental check-ups. The team at KU64 Berlin takes plenty of time during your appointment for a caries risk assessment. Using a saliva sample, we identify acid-producing bacteria and mutans streptococci (lactobacilli). If there is an increased risk of harmful bacteria, our dentists will give you important information and tips on oral hygiene and diet, to help you improve your daily oral care and reduce your risk of tooth decay. The risk is particularly high if you have old or damaged fillings, or if your oral hygiene is not thorough enough.
Book your appointment today for a caries risk assessment or a professional teeth cleaning with our dentists. Our specialists will be happy to inform you about the costs and other dental treatments
Caries risk assessment

Until just a moment ago, it was an ordinary morning: the first sip of coffee, a bite into a crispy bread roll – and suddenly this sharp, throbbing pain in a molar. On the way to work it settles down briefly, but when you eat your snack during your break, it starts throbbing again, as if the tooth had its own pulse. Your cheek feels tight, and it's hard to concentrate or hold a conversation. "It'll pass," you think – until night comes and the pain returns.

This is the typical start of a root canal infection: gradual at first, then clearly noticeable. With the right treatment early on, however, the infection can usually be brought under control and the tooth can often be saved. Here you'll find all the information on how to recognise the infection, what causes it, and how we treat it gently – so that a painful morning is quickly followed by an ordinary day again.
When pain clouds your smile

A root canal infection, known medically as pulpitis or apical periodontitis, is an infection of the tooth root or the pulp – the inner part of a tooth containing nerves and blood vessels. It occurs when bacteria enter the tooth through decay, cracks, or leaking fillings.

The infection can cause severe toothache, sensitivity to pressure, and swelling, and if left untreated, can spread into the jawbone. Early treatment is essential to save the tooth and avoid complications.

A root canal infection can be very painful. Without dental treatment, it can even lead to tooth loss as the condition progresses. For this reason, it's important to visit our dental practice as soon as possible if you suspect a root canal infection, so the affected tooth can be professionally examined and treated.
What is a root canal infection?
Dentistry distinguishes the forms of a root canal infection according to the location of the infection

Pulpitis refers to an infection of the soft core of the tooth. This is where the pulp is located, containing blood and lymph vessels as well as fine nerves. When the pulp becomes infected, severe pain occurs, as the pulp also runs through the fine canals of the tooth root. The infected nerves then reach the inside of the tooth, causing a strong pain response.

Apical periodontitis occurs when the root tip of the tooth, and thus parts of the periodontium, become infected. Usually, the bacteria have spread from the pulpitis through the root canal to the tooth root.
Do you suspect you have an infection in a tooth? Then it's best to book an appointment at KU64 in Berlin today.
What types of root canal infection are there?
Regular dental and gum care is extremely important in preventing a root canal infection. The following factors are the most common causes and triggers.
What causes a root canal infection?

When teeth are affected by decay, the enamel is destroyed by acid. This acid is produced when bacteria convert sugar. Decay is therefore also known as caries. It can reach as far as the pulp or the dentine. As a result, the body responds with an infection, and swelling forms around the infected area.
Tooth decay – dental damage from acid

Inflammation or infection can enter the tooth not only from the top, as with tooth decay, but can also attack the root from below. If the periodontal membrane around the tooth becomes inflamed, bacteria can travel through the fine root canals into the dental pulp. The result is periodontitis, an inflammation of the tooth-supporting tissue. If left untreated, the inflammation continues to spread through the mouth and affects further parts of the teeth.
Periodontitis – inflammation of the tooth-supporting tissue

Harmful bacteria can damage many areas on and in the tooth, as well as in the mouth. This can lead to inflammation of the gums. Gingivitis occurs, for example, when bacteria build up on the surface of the tooth. As the gums recede, parts of the tooth root become exposed. Gingivitis, too, can eventually lead to inflammation of the tooth root.
Gingivitis – inflammation of the gums

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.beschre.text: Root canal infections are painful & should be treated quickly. Find out more now about the condition & dental treatment at KU64!

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.einstie.text: A root canal infection is usually very painful. Leaking fillings and tooth decay are often the cause. At our practice at KU64 Berlin, we make sure your symptoms are relieved quickly. Are you suffering from toothache and suspect a root canal infection? Book an appointment today.

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.0.a.text: Teeth affected by a root infection are very sensitive to pressure, cold and heat. Because the most sensitive part of the tooth – the dental pulp – becomes inflamed in a root infection, patients experience severe pain. Because of this toothache, most people notice that something is wrong and see a dentist.

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.0.f.text: How do I notice a tooth root infection?

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.1.a.text: If you suspect a tooth root infection, have it checked by a dentist straight away, ideally on the same day. Until your appointment, you can ease the discomfort by cooling the swelling from the outside, rinsing with lukewarm salt water, choosing soft, cool food and chewing on the other side. Ibuprofen or paracetamol can help bridge the gap until you see the dentist. Only professional treatment can remove the cause for good – the earlier this happens, the better the chances of saving the tooth.

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.1.f.text: What should I do if I have a root infection?

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.2.a.text:
An acute but short-lived, painful irritation of the tooth root usually heals by itself. Home remedies can help ease the discomfort in the meantime.
However, if pulpitis or periodontitis is already present, the inflammation is chronic. A chronic tooth root infection does not go away on its own and cannot be treated at home! It will not resolve by itself. Please consult a dentist so that treatment can begin as soon as possible.

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.2.f.text: CAN A TOOTH ROOT INFECTION HEAL ON ITS OWN?

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.3.a.text:
A tooth root infection is a bacterial infection – home remedies can only ease the inflamed root tip and pulp temporarily. The infection cannot heal naturally! Please contact our practice as soon as possible.
Ginger, sage and camomile contain natural anti-inflammatory substances. Rinsing with a tea made from these can temporarily ease the inflammation. Rinsing with salt water has a similar effect.
Over-the-counter painkillers such as ibuprofen can reduce the pain until you can be seen by a dentist.

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.3.f.text: Which home remedies help with a tooth root infection?

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.4.a.text: An untreated inflammation of the tooth root (pulpitis) can cause serious nerve damage and lead to the tooth dying. If the symptoms of a root infection are not recognised and treated early enough, the bacteria can spread to the surrounding tissue and jawbone, and even affect other organs.

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.4.f.text: HOW DANGEROUS IS A TOOTH ROOT INFECTION?

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.5.a.text: There is no fixed timeframe. Depending on the cause, bacterial load and blood supply, an infected tooth root can die within a few days or over weeks to months. A typical sign is that the severe pain suddenly subsides because the nerve tissue has died – but the infection continues at the root tip and can still cause swelling. That's why you should see a dentist promptly if you suspect an infection; the earlier the treatment, the better the chance of saving the tooth.

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.5.f.text: How long does it take for an infected tooth root to die?

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.6.a.text: In most cases, a root infection is caused by tooth decay. These bacteria destroy the various layers of the tooth and work their way down to the pulp. There, the root of the tooth becomes inflamed, resulting in a painful root infection. This should be treated by a dentist as a matter of urgency.

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.6.f.text: WHICH BACTERIA CAUSE A TOOTH ROOT INFECTION?

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.7.a.text:
The most common procedure for treating the infection is root canal treatment. The dentist removes the affected areas using fine medical instruments. If pus has formed due to the infection, it is removed from the gum pockets.
The dentist then carefully disinfects the entire tooth and seals it with a filling.

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.7.f.text: WHAT DOES THE DENTIST DO FOR A TOOTH ROOT INFECTION?

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.8.a.text: Your German statutory health insurance usually covers the cost of root canal treatment if it allows your dentist to save the tooth. Our practice team will give you all the information you need beforehand.

beschwerde.zahnwurzelentzuendung.faq.8.f.text: DOES THE GERMAN STATUTORY HEALTH INSURANCE COVER THE COST OF ROOT CANAL TREATMENT FOR A TOOTH ROOT INFECTION?

leistung.aligner.dauer.text: 6 to 18 months, depending on your starting position

leistung.aligner.faq.0.antwort.text: At least 20 to 22 hours – in other words, all the time except when eating or brushing your teeth. This is the point where treatments succeed or fail. If you don't keep to the wearing time, the treatment will take considerably longer.

leistung.aligner.faq.0.frage.text: How many hours a day do I need to wear the aligner?

leistung.aligner.faq.1.antwort.text: Barely, at normal conversation distance. If so-called attachments – small tooth-coloured bumps – are needed, these may be visible up close.

leistung.aligner.faq.1.frage.text: Can people see the aligners when I speak?

leistung.aligner.faq.2.antwort.text: Only with a retainer. Teeth naturally tend to drift back to their old position. That's why permanent stabilisation is needed after any orthodontic treatment – usually a thin wire behind the front teeth.

leistung.aligner.faq.2.frage.text: Will my teeth stay straight afterwards?

leistung.aligner.kasse.text: For adults, this is usually a private (self-pay) treatment. For children and young people, the statutory health insurance covers it from misalignment grade KIG 3 onwards – though this usually means fixed braces rather than aligners.

leistung.aligner.kurz.text: Straighten your teeth with clear aligners instead of fixed braces.

leistung.aligner.patientenfrage.text: How long does aligner treatment take for adults?

leistung.aligner.teaser.text: Aligners are removable, transparent trays that move your teeth in small steps. They're hardly noticeable in everyday life, and you simply take them out to eat or brush your teeth. For mild to moderate misalignments, they're a very good alternative to fixed braces.

leistung.all-on-4.dauer.text: Procedure 2 to 4 hours, final restoration after 3 to 6 months

leistung.all-on-4.faq.0.antwort.text: Yes, if they are positioned correctly. The two back implants are placed at an angle to make the best use of the available bone. This method has been documented for over twenty years. If the bone conditions are less favourable, we use six implants instead.

leistung.all-on-4.faq.0.frage.text: Are four implants really enough for a whole jaw?

leistung.all-on-4.faq.1.antwort.text: The temporary teeth are fixed, but not yet able to bear full pressure. For around three months, we recommend soft food and avoiding anything very hard. After that, the final bridge can be used without restriction.

leistung.all-on-4.faq.1.frage.text: What can I eat in the first few weeks?

leistung.all-on-4.kasse.text: Fixed subsidy for the comparable standard treatment. Payment in instalments is possible.

leistung.all-on-4.kurz.text: A complete jaw supported by four implants – with a fixed temporary set of teeth on the same day.

leistung.all-on-4.patientenfrage.text: Can I really get fixed teeth in just one day?

leistung.all-on-4.synonyme.2.text: immediate treatment for a toothless jaw

leistung.all-on-4.teaser.text: When a jaw is badly damaged or has no teeth left, a bridge fitted to four to six carefully positioned implants can carry the entire jaw. Often a fixed temporary set of teeth can be fitted on the very day of the procedure – so you don't go home without teeth.

leistung.behandlung-in-narkose.faq.0.ant.text: It's administered by a specialist anaesthetist and monitored throughout. Beforehand, there's a consultation to review your medical history. For healthy people, the risk is very low.

leistung.behandlung-in-narkose.faq.1.ant.text: No. You'll need someone to accompany you, and you mustn't drive or make important decisions for 24 hours.

leistung.behandlung-in-narkose.faq.1.fra.text: Can I go home alone afterwards?

leistung.behandlung-in-narkose.kasse.text: Statutory health insurance only covers the anaesthetic in certain cases, for example with a proven phobia or disability. Otherwise it must be paid for privately.

leistung.behandlung-in-narkose.kosten.text: Anaesthetic 600 to 1,500 € in addition to treatment

leistung.behandlung-in-narkose.kurz.text: Extensive treatment in a single session – you sleep, we work.

leistung.behandlung-in-narkose.patienten.text: Is dental treatment under general anaesthetic safe?

leistung.behandlung-in-narkose.teaser.text: For severe anxiety, a strong gag reflex, or very extensive treatment needs, a general anaesthetic is a good solution. An anaesthetist monitors you throughout while we take care of everything necessary in one session.

leistung.cmd-behandlung.dauer.text: Diagnosis 60 to 90 minutes, treatment over several months

leistung.cmd-behandlung.faq.0.antwort.text: Typical signs are clicking or grinding in the jaw joint, restricted mouth opening, morning tension in the cheek muscles, recurring headaches around the temples, and ear noises with no ENT findings. Several of these signs often occur together.

leistung.cmd-behandlung.faq.0.frage.text: How do I know if it might be TMJ disorder?

leistung.cmd-behandlung.faq.1.antwort.text: Many people notice an initial improvement after a few weeks with the splint. Stabilisation usually takes three to six months. In more pronounced cases, we work together with physiotherapy.

leistung.cmd-behandlung.faq.1.frage.text: How long does the treatment take?

leistung.cmd-behandlung.kasse.text: Statutory health insurance covers the splint where the findings justify it. The instrumental functional analysis is a private service.

leistung.cmd-behandlung.kurz.text: When your jaw, neck or ears ache and no one can find the cause.

leistung.cmd-behandlung.patientenfrage.text: Could my headaches be coming from my jaw?

leistung.cmd-behandlung.teaser.text: Temporomandibular dysfunction (TMD) occurs when the teeth, jaw joints and chewing muscles don't work together properly. The symptoms often show up far from the jaw – as headaches, ringing in the ears or neck tension. We measure your jaw function systematically and treat the underlying cause.

leistung.dentosophie.ablauf.0.text.text: We look at how breathing, tongue position, lip closure, chewing and swallowing work together – and what has fallen out of sync.

leistung.dentosophie.ablauf.1.text.text: A soft, mouthguard-shaped training appliance. It supports correct tongue position, encourages a natural swallowing pattern and promotes nasal breathing.

leistung.dentosophie.ablauf.2.text.text: Myofunctional exercises to correct the muscle imbalance. Active participation is part of the concept – new movement patterns are practised, not acquired on their own.

leistung.dentosophie.ablauf.3.text.text: Over six to twelve months, we monitor the progress and adjust the appliance and exercises as needed.

leistung.dentosophie.dauer.text: About six to twelve months, with regular check-up appointments

leistung.dentosophie.faq.0.antwort.text: For children and adolescents during development, as well as for adults. It is a gentle approach wherever functional issues play a role: mouth breathing, incorrect tongue position, abnormal swallowing, grinding, clenching or jaw misalignment. It is often used alongside other dental treatments.

leistung.dentosophie.faq.1.antwort.text: An elastic training device shaped like a dental arch, made of plastic. It supports tongue function, lip closure, swallowing and nasal breathing. During the therapy phase, it is worn regularly together with the accompanying exercises.

leistung.dentosophie.faq.2.antwort.text: This depends on the findings, age and treatment goal. As a rule, it takes around six to twelve months. In individual cases, longer-term support may be advisable.

leistung.dentosophie.faq.2.frage.text: How long does Dentosophie treatment take?

leistung.dentosophie.faq.3.antwort.text: Statutory health insurers in Germany generally do not cover Dentosophie. For privately insured patients and those with private supplementary dental insurance, cover depends on the specific policy. We will advise you in detail about the process and costs before treatment begins.

leistung.dentosophie.faq.3.frage.text: Does health insurance cover the cost?

leistung.dentosophie.faq.4.antwort.text: Dentosophie works on function, while a brace works on position. Where a misalignment has developed due to an unfavourable pattern – mouth breathing, incorrect swallowing – Dentosophie addresses the cause. Where the position itself is the problem, orthodontic treatment is unavoidable. Which applies in your case will become clear from the examination.

leistung.dentosophie.faq.4.frage.text: When does Dentosophie make sense, and when is a brace needed?

leistung.dentosophie.kasse.text: Statutory health insurance in Germany does not usually cover Dentosophy. For private insurance and supplementary dental insurance, it depends on the tariff – we will discuss the process and costs with you before starting.

leistung.dentosophie.kurz.text: Bringing breathing, tongue position and bite into balance – without braces.

leistung.dentosophie.patientenfrage.text: Can misaligned teeth be treated without fixed braces?

leistung.dentosophie.teaser.text: Dentosophy addresses the root of many problems: breathing, tongue position, lip closure, chewing and swallowing. A soft training appliance, combined with exercises, gradually helps change unconscious patterns – in children and adults alike.

leistung.dvt-3d-roentgen.faq.0.antwort.text: Considerably less than with a medical CT scan and, depending on the device and field size, roughly equivalent to a few days of natural background radiation. We only take a scan when there is a clear reason for it, and we always choose the smallest possible image field.

leistung.dvt-3d-roentgen.faq.1.antwort.text: Yes. If you wish, you can have the data on a digital file – for example, for a second opinion or for other specialists involved in your treatment.

leistung.dvt-3d-roentgen.faq.1.frage.text: Can I take the scan with me?

leistung.dvt-3d-roentgen.kurz.text: Three-dimensional imaging for planning where every millimetre counts.

leistung.dvt-3d-roentgen.patientenfrage.text: How much radiation exposure does a CBCT scan involve?

leistung.dvt-3d-roentgen.teaser.text: Digital volume tomography shows the jaw, teeth and nerve pathways in three dimensions. It is used when a two-dimensional X-ray does not provide enough certainty – for example before implant placement or wisdom tooth surgery.

leistung.feste-zahnspange.faq.0.antwort.text: After fitting and after each adjustment, your teeth feel sensitive to pressure for two to three days. This is uncomfortable but manageable – soft food helps during this time.
